4. The Collector may thereupon, not withstanding anything contained in the
order admitting such instrument in evidence, or in any certificate granted
under Section 42, or in Section 43, prosecute any person for any offence
against ine Stamp law which the Collector considers him to have
committed in respect of such instrument :

Provided that

(a) _ nosuch prosecution shall be instituted where the amount (including duty
and penalty) which, according to the determination of such Court, was
payable in respect of the instrument under Section 35, is paid to the
Collector, unless he thinks that the offence was committed with an intention
of evading payment of the proper duty;

(b) except for the purposes of such prosecution, no declaration made under
this section shall affect the validity of any order admitting any instrument
in evidence, or of any certificate granted under Section 42

Elucidation :

The section deals with the procedure and revision of the decisions of
Subordinate Courts regarding the sufficiency of stamp duty paid on. the
Instruments. It empowers the Appellate Court or a Court of reference, of
it’s own motion or on application of the Collector to take into consideration
the order of a Sub ordinate Court

The High court, as appellate court, may also take action of its
own motion. !

CHAPTER - VII
Criminal Offences and Procedure

62. Penalty for executing etc., instrument not duly stamped :-

1. Any person. i

(a) drawing, making, issuing, endorsing or transferring, or signing otherwise
than as a witness, or presenting for acceptance or payment, or accepting,
paying or receiving payment of, or, in any manner negotiating, any bill of
exchange payable otherwise than on demand or promissory note without
the same being duly stamped; or

(b) executing or signing otherwise than as a witness any other instrument
chargeable with duty without the same being duly stamped; or

(c) voting or attempting to vote under any proxy not duly stamped, shall for
62 Stamp Act (Sections 63 & 64)
every such offence be punishalbe with fine which may extend to five
hundred rupees : .

Provided that, when any penalty had been paid in respect of any instrument
under Section 35, Section 40 or Section 61 the amount of such penalty shall be
allowed in reduction of the fine (if any) subsequently imposed under this section
in respect of the same instrument upon the person who paid such penalty

2. If a share warrant is issued without being duly stamped, the company
issuing the same, and also every person who, at the time when it is issued,
is the Managing Director or Secretory or other Principal officer of the
Company, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred
rupees

Elucidation :

The Section governs penalty for executing etc instruments not duly
stamped. Receiving an unstamped pronote is not an Offence (Note 4 under
sec.62 APSM P.77)

The following are offences

a) Drawing or Negotiating an unstamped pronote or bill of exchange
is an offence.

b) Executing or signing otherwise than as a witness any instrument not
duly stamped

c) Voting under a proxy not duly stamped
d) — Issuing a Share Warrant by a company not duly stamped.
63. Penalty for failure to cancel adhesive stamp :-
Any person required by Section 12 to cancel an adhesive stamp and

failing to cancel such stamp in manner prescribed by that section, shall be
punishable with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees

Elucidation :

The Section deals with punishment to be given for failure to cancel
properly the Adhesive stamps as required by section 12 .It is an Offence
punishable with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees.

64. Penalty for omission to comply with provisions of Section 27 :-
Any person who, with intent to defraud the Government -

(a) ~ executes any instrument in which all the facts and circumstances required
by Section27 to be setforth in such instrument are not fully and truly
setforth; or

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

|
Stamp Act (Sections 64A&65) | 63
(b) being employed or concerned in or about the preparation of any instrument,
neglects or omits fully and truly to set-forth therein all such facts and
circumstances; or

(c) does any other act calculated|to deprive the Government of any duty or
penalty under this Act shall be punishable with fine which may extend to
five thousand rupees

Elucidation: '

The Section provides for imposition of penalty for failure to comply
with the provisions of section27. |

64A. Recovery of amount of deficit stamp duty :-

1. where any person liable to pay duty under this Act is convicted of an
offence under Section 64, in respect of any instrument (not being an
instrument specified in entry 91 of List] in the Seventh Schedule to the
Constitution), the Magistrate shall, in addition to the punishment which
may be imposed for such offence, recover summarily and pay to the
Collector, the amount of duty if any, due under this Act from such person
in respect of that instrument and the Collector shall thereupon certify by
endorsement on that instrument that proper duty has been levied in respect
thereof :

Provided that if the person referred to in this sub-section has already
paid any amount towards the duty payable under this Act in respect of the
instrument in relation to which such person was convicted, the Magistrate shall
recover only the difference in the amount of duty

2. The amount recoverable under sub-section(1) shall be recovered by the
Magistrate, as if it were a fine imposed under the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973. (2 of 1974)

Elucidation :
This section was newly inserted by Act. No. I of 1992. wef 1-4-1992.

The section provides for recovery of amount of deficit stamp duty by courts
in addition to punishment imposed under section 64

65. Penalty for refusal to give receipt and for devices to evade duty
on receipts :- |
Any person who -

(a) _ being required under section30 to give a receipt, refuses or neglects to
give the same; or

(b) with intent to defraud the Governement of any duty, upon a payment of
64 Stamp Act (Sections 66 & 67)
money or delivery of property exceeding twenty rupees (now rupees
five thousand from 1-4-2004) in amount or value, gives a receipt for an
amount or value not exceeding twenty rupees (Now rupees five thousand
from 1-4-2004) or separates or divides the money or property paid or
delivered; shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one hundred
rupees.

Elucidation :

The Section empowers imposition of penalty of fine upto rupees one
hundred for refusal to give receipt or to devide the money to evade duty
on receipt.

66. Penalty for not making out policy or making one not duly
stamped :-

Any person who -

(a) _ receives or takes credit for any premium or consideration for any contract
of insurance and does not, within one month after receiving, or taking
credit for, such premium or consideration, make out and execute a duly
stamped policy or such insurance; or

(b) makes, executes or delivers out any policy which is not duly stamped or
pays or allow in account, or agrees to pay or allow in account any money
upon or in respect of any such policy; shall be payable with fine which
may extend to two hundred rupees

Elucidation :

The Section is designed to prevent the loss of Revenue that may occur
if Insurance. business was done on slip or unstamped Policies.

Failure to issue duly stamped insurance Policy is an offence.

67. Penalty for not drawing full number of bills or marine policies
purporting to be in sets :-

Any person drawing or executing a bill of exchange payable otherwise
than on demand or a policy of marine insurance purporting to be drawn or
executed in a set of two or more, and not at the same time drawing or executing
on paper duly stamped the whole number of bills or policies of which such bill or
policy purports the set to consist, shall be punishable with fine which may extend
to one thousand rupees.

Elucidation :

This Section provides for penalties for special offences like drawing

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

|
Stamp Act (Sections 68&69) | 65
or executing unstamped Bill of exchange or policy of marine insurance. It
does not interfere with the general provisions of section62.

Failure to execute full number of duly stamped Bills of Exchange and
Marine Insurance Policies is an offence.

Sections 66 and 67 create special offences in respect of Insurance
Policies.

68. Penalty for postdating bills and for other devices to defraud the
revenue :-

Any person who -

(a) With intent to defraud the Government of duty, draws, makes or issues
any bill of exchange or promissory note bearing a date subsequent to that
on which such bill or note, is actually drawn or made; or

(b) knowing that such bill or note has been so post-dated, endorses, transfers,
presents for acceptance or payment, or accepts, pays or receives payment
of such bill or note, or in any manner negotiates the same; or

(c) with the like intent, practises or is concerned in any act, contrivance or
device not specially provided for by this Act or any other law for the time
being in force;

shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
Elucidation :

The section imposes penalties in certain cases of post dating of Bills
of Exchange and Promissory Notes.

Post dating bills with a view to deprive Government of the revenue is

an offence. |

69. Penalty for breach of rule relating to sale of stamps and for
unauthorised sale :- |

(a) Any person appointed to sell stamps who disobeys any rule made under
Section74 and

(b) any person not so appointed \ who sells or offers for sale any stamp (other
than a ten paise or five paise adhesive stamp);

shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend
to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or
with both.

Elucidation :

Disobedience of rules by licensed stamp vendors and sale of stamps
66 Stamp Act (Section 70)

by unlicensed vendors is an offence.

When a licensed vendor purchases stamps from a private person he
is liable for punishment for abatement of an offence under section
69(b)(Note 3 under section 69 APSM (P81)

70. Institution and conduct of prosecution :-

1. No prosecution in respect of any offence punishable under this Act or
any Act hereby repealed shall be instituted without the sanction of the
Collector or such other officer as the State Government generally, or the
Collector specially, authorises in that behalf.

2. The Chief Controlling Revenue Authority, or any officer generally or
specifically authorised by it in this behalf, may stay any such prosecution
or compound any such offence by levying a compounding fee which
shall include the deficit stamp duty, if any and a penalty of three
times of the deficit stamp duty.(Act 16 of 2002 With effect from 1-9-

2002)

3. The amount of any such composition shall be recoverable in the manner
provided by Section48

Elucidation:

The section empowers the District Collector or any other Officer
appointed as Collector under section 70 of the Stamp Act to sanction
prosecution before prosecution is commenced.

This Section read with section 70 relates to sanction of prosecution
for offences under the Act, staying such prosecution and compounding
the offences.

Joint Sub-Registrar I in Registration office and the Sub Registrars
grade I who are authorised to exercise powers of District Registrars under
section 35 of the Registration Act can compound offences.

The C.C.R.A or any Officer generally or specially authorised by it in
this behalf may stay any such prosecution or compound any such offence
by levying a compounding fee which shall include the deficit stamp duty if
any and a penalty of three times of the deficit stamp (Act 16/2002 with
effect from 1-9-2002).

Previous sanction of the Collector for the prosecution is a must and it
must exist on the record.

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Stamp Act (Sections 71, 72& 73) 67

Note

There is no provision in the Act empowering CCRA to remit fully or
partly of the compounding fee as it is levied with the consent of the parties

71. Jurisdiction of Magistrates :-

No Magistrate other than a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate whose
powers are not less than those of a Magistrate of the second class, shall try any
offence under this Act.

Elucidation :

Only Magistrates whose powers are not lesst han that of a magistrate
of the second class can try offences under the act

72. Place of trial :-

Every such offence committed in respect of any instrument may be tried
in any district or presidency town in which such instrument is found as well as
in any district or presidency town in which such offence might be tried under
the Code of Criminal Procedure for the time being in force.

Elucidation :
The Section specifies the place of trial for offences under the Act

CHAPTER - VII
Supplemental Provisions

73. Books etc., to be kept open for inspection :-

Every public officer having in his custody any registers, books, records,
papers, documents or proceedings, the inspection whereof may tena to secure
any duty, or to prove or lead to the discovery of any fraud or omission in relation
to any duty, shall at all reasonable times, permit any person authorised in writing
by the Collector to inspect for such purpose the registers, books, papers,
documents, proceedings, and to take such notes and extracts as he may deem
necessary, without fee or charge.

Elucidation :

The Rules for collection of duties secured in the course of inspection
under section 73 are incorporated under Chapter I (H).

The section empowers the collector or any person authorised by him
in writing to conduct audit in public offices to detect fraud in payment
Proper stamp duty
68 Stamp Act (Sections 75, 75A, 76, 76A)

   

74, Power to make rules relating to sale of stamps :-
The state Government, may make rules for regulating, -

(a) _ the supply and sale of stamps and stamped papers,
(b) _ the persons by whom alone such sale is to be conducted, and
(c) the duties and remuneration of such persons.

Provided that such rules shall not restrict the sale of ten paise or five
paise adhesive stamps

75. Power to make rules generally to carry out Act :-

The State Government may make rules to carry out generally the purposes
of this Act, and may by such rules prescribe the fines, which shall in no case
exceed five hundred rupees, to be incurred on breach thereof

75A. Rules made by the State Government to be laid before the
State Legislative :-

1. All rules made by the State Government under this Act shall, unless they
are expressed to come into force on a particular day, come into force on
the day on which they are published in the Official Gazette

2. Every rule made under this section shall, immediately after it is made, be
laid before each House of the State Legislature if it is in session, and if it
is not in session, in the session immediately following, for a total period of
fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive
sessions, and if before the expiration of the session in which it is so laid
or the session immediately following, both the Houses agree in making
any modification in the rule or in the annulment of the rule, the rule shall
thereafter have effect only in such modified form or shall stand annulled,
as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment
shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under
the rule.

76. Publication of rules :-

1. All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette

2. Allrules published as required by this section shall upon such publication,
have effect as if enacted by this Act.

3. Every rule made by the state government under this Act shall be laid as
soon as may be after it is made before the State Legislature (Central Act
4 of 2005)

76A. Delegation of certain powers :-

The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette,

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

Stamp Act (Sections 77,77A, 78&79) 69

delegate, -
(a) all or any of the powers conferred on it by Section 2(9), 33(3)(b), 70(1),
74 and 78 to the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority;

(b) all or any of the powers conferred on the Chief Controlling Revenue
Authority by Sections 45(1)(2), 56(1) and 70(2) to such subordinate
Revenue Authority as may be specified in the notification and

(c) all or any of the powers conferred on it by Section 9(1)(b) to the
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps.

77. Saving as to Court-fees :-

Nothing in this Act contained shall be deemed to affect the duties chargeable
under any enactment for the time being in force relating to Court-fees,

77A. Saving as to certain stamps :-

All stamps in denominations of annas four or multiples thereof shall be
deemed to be stamps of the value of twenty five paise or, as the case may be
multiples thereof and shall, accordingly be valid for all the purposes of this Act.

78. Duty to be paid or allowances to be ntade for fraction of ten
paise :-

In the determination of the amount of duty payable, or of allowance to be
made, under this Act, any fraction in ten paise equal to or exceeding five paise

shall be counted as ten paise and other fractions of ten paise shall be disregarded
(Act 10 of 1997 with effect from 20-10-1997)

CASE LAW

Article 6 (B) of Schedule 1A of the Stamp Act .. i) Art 6B would
be applicable only in such specified cases mentioned against the Article and
that the same can't override the general provisions of Art. 6A of SchedulelA .
Agreement of sale of vacant site falls under general provision of Article
6(A) of Schedule 1A. Art.6 (c) of Schedule 1A should be construed to be a
case not falling under either A or B of Art.6 of Schedule 1A [2004(1) ALD
557. Confirmed in S. Peda Appaiah Vs Narasimha Reddy, 2004 (5) ALD
653(DB)A.P.H.C.Judgment dated 8-11-2003 in C.R.P.No.4396 of 2003]

ii) If the Developer, on agreement construct a building on the land of the
owner, there is no transfer of interest in the property in favour of a
Developer nor the agreement constitute an instrument under which any
right, title or interest has been transferred from the land owner to the
Developer and that the land owner continues to be owner of land and
construction thereon. [Prabhu Laxman Ghate v. Sub-Registrar of
Collector of Stamps, AIR 2004 Bombay 267]

iii) In the judgement dated 7-9-2004 of the A.P. High Court it was observed
that the Stamp Act is fiscal in nature and that it has to be construed
strictly in accordance with law. The agricultural lands are not covered
by Article 6B. It covered only specific items of property mentioned
against the Article. It can't have universal application of all transactions
covering immovable properties. Martand Dairy and Farm v. Union of
India, AIR 1975 SC 1492 followed. Saranam Peda Appaiah Vs Narasimha
Reddy, 2004(5) ALD 653(DB) = 2004(6) ALT 237(DB) C & IG RS
Memo No.S1/16160/04, dated 2.3.2005]

CASE LAW

In the judgment of the Bombay High Court it has been held that when
there is no conveyance, the question of reconveyance can't arise on such
conveyance, the deed of cancellation can't fall under Art. 25 of Schedule 1 of
Bombay Stamp Act (60 of 1958). It falls under Art. 15 and is chargeable to
stamp duty prescribed therein. [Crest Hotels Ltd.v. Asst.Supt. of Stamps AIR
1994 Bombay, 228] .

FAMILY MEMBERS - CLARIFICATION

In C & IGRS Cir.No.S1/14060-A/2005, dt.28-10-2005 it is clarified as

follows :

i)

ii)

iii)

iv)

Family members as defined in explanation under sub-clause (a) of Art.49A
(Settlement) apply under Art.40

Widowed mother, Unmarried daughters, Unmarried sisters, Widowed wife
of deceased brother where sons either minors or having no sons, and
sons/daughters where parents predeceased are treated as family
members. But in such cases, where provision is made by way of
separate share in their favour have to be treated as gift
(Settlement) under Section 2(24) as distinct from the value of
separated share in a partition deed.

Grand mother, Grand father, Adopted father, Adopted mother are
excluded from the scheme of partition and concession of 1% shall not
apply if provision is made in their favour in a partition.

The concession of 1% does not apply to partitions affected among
co-owners under a partnership deed

Section 2(15) and Article 40 of Schedule 1-A :-

@

Gi)

iii)

Gi)

Partitions of immovable property of Joint Hindu Family - Arbitrators
alloting one share to one brother, another share to another brother and
third large share to other three brothers jointly. The award is an instrument
of partition. Art. 40 of Schedule 1-A is attracted - Largest share must be
eliminated and the stamp duty is charged on the separated shares. [T.C.
Thimmaiah Chetty v. Dist. Registrar, Kurnool, AIR 1986 A.P. 14(F.B.)=
1985(2) ALT 179 (F.B.)

The partition list which is sought to be admitted as doucument contains
only the list of properties and does not refer to the details or process of
mediation. Therefore the partition lists cannot be construed as an
instrument of partition and as such not liable to stamp duty [Munimantha
Reddy v.Lakshmikantha Reddy 1982(2)ALT384]

Partition is considered to be ultimate evil resulting from co-ownership.
The recital in document shows,that any one or more of the co-owners
decide to relinquish their right in favour of others and that their right in
common hot-patch to be divided among other co-owners, it can't be said
that the partition would be vitiated.(Case law discussed " Dhirajlal
Ramachand & others v. State of Kerala)

The distinction between partition and release is explained [Board of
Revenue vs. B.A. Mallayya, AIR 1971 Mad 210]

CASE LAW
Distinction between a Special and a General Power of Attorney

“Tn the judgment of the Madras High Court dated 9-1-1913 in CMSA No.
56 of 1911, it was held that the expression a single transaction seems to apply
either to a act or to acts so related to each other to form one judicial transaction
such as all the acts necessary to perfect a mortgage or a sale of a particular
property ....... The acts to be done should not be of various and numerous kinds
to constitute as a Special Power of Attorney” (S.O. 348)

CASE LAW

(i) | The Question is whether an agreement of sale stipulating delivery of
possession on payment of certain amount is eligible to stamp duty as
conveyance under explanation to Art. 47-A of Schedule I-A as applicable
in A.P. when subsequently, as per the stipulation, possession is delivered.

Held that by fiction introduced by the explanation, this has to be stamped
as regular sale deed and that the document can't be admitted in evidence
as it is insufficiently stamped ; (M.Linga Reddy V.D. Gangi Reddy 1995(2)
ALD 59)

i) | Where a document contains a recital recording delivery of possession of
property in pursuance of an agreement of sale, whether by way of an
endorsment on the reverse of the agreement, or under a separate receipt,
it has to be stamped as a sale deed as contemplated by Article 47-A of
Schedule 1-A of the Stamp Act. [Jannuchander Batra v. Manchikatla
Satyanarayana and others, 2003 (2) ALD 640].

(iii) |The APHC observed that for determining the stamp duty on a sale deed,
the factor to be kept in view is what is the property conveyed under the
instrument xxx, when there is merely a recital that certain sum of money
was received for the sale of movable and immovable properties, but
movable properties were not conveyed under the instrument, the
consideration referred to for the sale of movable properties cannot be
taken into account for determination of the stamp duty payable on such
instrument under the I.S Act, Stamp duty is assessed on the basis of the
consideration payable for the property transferred under the document
and not for other recitals contained therein which are incorporated for
the purpose of recording the circumstances under which the particular

CHAPTER I (C)

Rules Under The Indian Stamp Act, 1899
CHAPTER I
Preliminary.
1. Short title:
These rules may be called the Inuian Stamp Rules, 1925.
2. Definitions :
In these rules,

a) “The Act” means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (II of 1899)
b) “Section” means a Section of the Act
c) “Schedule” means a Schedule of the Act

d) The Inspector General of Stamps means the Inspector General of Stamps,
Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad or any officer appointed by the Government
to perform the functions of Inspector General of Stamps.

e) “Government” means, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject
or context the “Government of Andhra Pradesh”.

3. Description of Stamps:

(1) _ Except as otherwise provided by the Act or by these Rules —

(i) All duties with which any instrument is chargeable shall be paid and such
payment shall be indicated on such instrument, by means of stamps issued
by Government, for the purposes of the Act.

 

 

 

 

 
120 Indian Stamp Rules, 1925

(ii) A stamp which by any word or words on the face of it is appropriated to
any particular kind of instrument, shall not be used for an instrument of
any other kind.

(iii) | Stamps purchased in A.P. State alone shall be used for instruments
chargeable with duty under the Act as in force in that State.

(iv) Omission to add the signatures on the stamp papers by Stamp Vendors
amounts the documents not duly stamped. Such document should be
impounded (Sec. 33)

A document engrossed on stamp paper which did not contain the Stamp
Vendor's endorsement shall be impounded

Provided that stamps purchased in the State of A.P. may also be used
for instruments chargeable with duty under the Act as in force in the
transferred territories.

Note: The term “Transferred Territories: shall mean the areas transferred to
the state of A.P under the provisions of A.P. and Madras (Alteration of
Boundaries) Act, 1959 (Central Act 56 of 1959).

(iv) The stamp paper will bear the endorsements of the stamp vendors
prescribed under the rules made under Section 74. .

(2) There shall be two kinds of stamps for indication of the payment of duty
with which instruments are chargeable, namely-

(a) Impressed stamps and
(b) Adhesive stamps

CHAPTER II
Of Impressed Stamps

4, Hundi:

(1)  Hundis, other than hundis which may be stamped with an adhesive stamp
under Section 11, shall be written on paper as follows namely:

(a) A hundi payable otherwise than on demand, but not at more than one
year after date of sight, and for an amount not exceeding rupees thirty
thousand in value, shall be written on paper on which a stamp of the
proper value bearing the word ‘Hundi’ has been engraved or embossed.

(b) A hundi for an amount exceeding rupees thirty thousand in value, or
payable at more than one year after date of sight, shall be written on
paper supplied for sale by the Government to which a label has been
affixed by Inspector General of Stamps, and impressed by him in the
manner prescribed by rule 11.

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Indian Stamp Rules, 1925

 

(2) Every sheet of paper on which a hundi is written shall be not less than
85/8 inches long and 51/8 inches wide and no plain paper shall be subjoined
thereto.

(3) The provision of sub-rule (1) of rule 7 shall apply in the case of Hundis.
5. Promissory Notes and Bill of Exchange:

A Promissory note or Bill of Exchange shall, except as provided by Section
11 or by rules 13 and 17, be written on paper on which stamp of the proper
value, with or without the word ‘Hundi’ has been engraved or embossed.

6. Other instruments:

(1) _ Every other instrument chargeable with duty shall, except as provided by
Section 11 or by rules 10,12,.13 be written on paper on which a stamp of
the proper value, not bearing the word ‘Hundi’ has been engraved or
embossed.

(2) A stamped paper, on which the stamp has been engraved or embossed
purchased by or for the use of a person shall be used only, by that person
or his legal representative or duly authorised agent of such person
provided that the Govt. may relax the provision of this sub-rule in genuine
and deserving cases.

Note :

i) Stamp paper purchased in the name of the person can be used by his
lelgal representative or duly authorised agent of such person

ii) Rule 6(2) does not apply to documents stamped with adhesive lables

iii) | Stamps purchased in the name of Principle District Munsif were used
for documents executed by the Ist Addl.District Munsif. There is no
contravention of Rule 6 (2)

7. Provision where single sheet of paper is insufficient:

(1) Where two or more sheets of paper on which stamps are engraved or
embossed are used to make up the amount of duty chargeable in respect
of any instrument, a portion of such instrument shall be written on each
sheet so used.

Note:-
i) The purchase of stamp papers for use together in one transacticn does
not operate to prevent their being used separately for different transactions.

Nor is there any objection to the use of stamp papers purchased in one
year together with other stamp papers to be purchased subsequently.

ii) The signature of executants and attesting witnesses do not form an integral
122 Indian Stamp Rules, 1925

_ portion of a deed. Hence such document should be impounded.

(2) Where a single sheet of paper, not being paper bearing an impressed
hundi-stamp, is nsufficient to admit of the entire instrument being written
on the side of the paper which bears the stamp, so much plain paper may
be subjoined thereto as may be necessary for the complete writing of
such instrument.

PROVIDED that, in every such case a substantial part of the instrument
shall be written on the sheet which bears the stamp before any part is written
on the plain paper subjoined.

Note:

(1) The Madras High Court has held that this sub rule (2) while favouring
the writing of an instrument only on the side which bears the stamp, does
not prohibit writing on the other side.

(2) A Collector ruled that a Conveyance was not duly stamped the writing
being on both sides of the paper. The High Court held that, the ruling was
wrong and that both sides may be written upon.

(3) The words ‘substantial part’ apply not to length or quantity but to
materiality. In this view the price or rent, the names of the Parties and
the date which are set out in the introductory portion of vernacular
documents are all material parts of the documents. The date will only
appears in this introductory portion and in some classes of vernacular
documents it is the same with the price. Such introductory portion of a
vernacular document is a substantial part of the instrument within the
meaning of rule7. (The advocate-General’s opinion in Board’s
proceedings No.16/136, Mis. dated 17" January 1901).

8. 10 paise, 15 paise and 20 paise impressed stamps:

The duty on any instrument which is chargeable with a duty of 10 paise
under the Act or of 15 paise under Article 19,36,37,49 and 52 of Schedule 1 or
of 20 paise under Article 5,38(a) of Schedule I-A may be denoted by a coloured
impression marked on a skeleton form of such instrument by the Inspector
General of Stamps.

9. The Proper Officer:

The Officer specified in Appendix I and any cfficer appointed in this behalf
by the State Government of a State are empowered to affix and impress or
perforate labels and each of them shall be deemed to be the ‘Proper officer’
for the purposes of the Act and of these rules.(Vide appendix I after Rule 22)

Note :

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Indian Stamp Rules, 1925 123

Any Proper Officer can affix and deface Special Adhesive stamps on the
instruments mentioned in Appindex (ii) and (iii) of Indian Stamp Rules irrespective
of the situation of the property

10. Affixing aud impressing of labels by proper officer permissible in
certain cases:

Labels may be affixed and impressed or performed by the Proper officer
in the case of any of the following instruments, namely:

(i) Those specified in Appendix II, (Vide appendix II after Rule 22) and the
Counterparts thereof other than instruments on which the duty is less
than fifteen paise, and

(ii) Those specified in Appendix III, (Vide appendix III after Rule 22) when
written in any European language, and accompanied, if the language is
not English, by a translation in English.

PROVIDED that, the State Government may direct that this rule shall
apply, subject to any conditions which it may prescribe to any of the instruments
specified in Appendix-III, (Vide after Rule 22) other than Bills of Exchange,
when written in any oriental languages.

11. Mode of affixing and impressing labels:

(a) The proper officer shall, upon any instrument specified in rule 10 being
brought to him before it is executed, and upon application being made to
him, affix thereto a label of such value as the applicant may require and
pay for, and impress or perforate such label by means of a stamping
machine or a perforating machine and also stamp or write on the face of
the label or labels the date of impressing or perforating the same. In the
case of instruments written on parchment, the labels shall be further
secured by means of metallic eyelets.

Note: No court fee should be levied under Clause<k) of Article 10 Schedule-II
of the A.P.Court Fees & Suits Valuation Act, 1956 on application made
to Collectors to have impressed labels affixed to documents,

(b) On affixing any label or labels under this rule, the Proper officer shall,
where the duty amounts to rupees five or upwards, write on the face of
the label or labels his initials and where the duty amounts to rupees twenty
or upwards , shall also attach his usual signature to the instruments
immediately under the label or labels.

(c) Any principal assistant of the Proper officer may discharge the functions
of the Proper officer under sub-rule (2) if empowered by the Government
in this behalf.
Indian Stamp Rules, 1925

 

12. Certain instruments to be stamped with Impressed labels:

(1) _ Instruments executed out of the State and requiring to be stamped after
their receipt in the State (Other than instruments which, under Section 11
or Rule 13, may be stamped with adhesive Stamps) shall be stamped
with Impressed labels.

(2) Where any such instrument as aforesaid is taken to the Collector under
Section 18, sub-section (2), the Collector, unless he is himself the Proper
officer, shall send the instrument to the Proper officer, remitting the amount
of duty paid in respect thereof; and the Proper officer shall stamp the
instrument in the manner prescribed in rule 11 and return it to the Collector
for the delivery to the person by whom it was produced.

(iii) and 52 of Schedule I and Articles 17 and 32 of Schedule I-A.

(g) Instruments of transfer of shares of public Companies or Associations.

(h) Bonds executed under any law relating to Central duty of excise or any
rules made thereunder.

CHAPTER IV
MISCELLANEOUS

18. Provision for cases in which improper description of stamp is
used:

When an instrument bears a stamp of proper amount, but of improper
description, the Collector may, on the payment of the duty with which the
instrument is chargeable, certify by an endorsement that it is duly stamped.

PROVIDED THAT, where the stamp borne on the instrument is a Postage
stamp and the proper description of stamp is a stamp bearing the words ‘Indian
Revenue’ the Collector shall so certify if the instrument was executed before,
and shall not so certify if it was executed on or after the 1* April 1935.

19. Evidence as to circumstance of claim to refund or renewal:

The Collector may require any person claiming a refund or renewal under
Chapter V of the Act, or his duly authorised agent, to make an oral deposition
on oath or affirmation, or to file an affidavit, setting forth the circumstances
under which the claim has arisen and may also, if he thinks fit, call for the
evidence of witnesses in support of the statement setforth in any such deposition
or affidavit.

19A. Furnishing of affidavits regarding instruments executed out of
India:

The Collector, may require any person or his duly authorised agent
presenting an instrument executed out of India for stamping under Section 18
or for opinion under section 31 to furnish an affidavit or other evidence as to the
date of its first receipt in India.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

Indian Stamp Rules, 1925 127

20. Payment of allowance in respect of spoiled or misused stamps or
on the renewal of Debentures :

when an application is made for the payment, under Chapter V of the Act,
of an allowance in respect of a stamp which has been spoiled or misused or for
which the applicant has no immediate use, or on the renewal of a debenture,
and an order is passed by the Collector sanctioning the allowance or calling for
further evidence in support of the application, then, if the amount of the allowance
of the stamp given in lieu thereof is not taken or if the further evidence required
is not furnished, as the case may be, by the applicant within one year of the date
of such order, the application shall be struck Off and the spoiled or misused
stamps (if any) sent to the Inspector General of Stamps or other officer appointed
in this behalf by the State Government for destruction.

21. Mode of canceling original Debenture or refund under Section
55:

When the Collector makes a refund under Section 55, he shall cancel the
original Debenture by writing on or across it the word ‘Cancelled’ and his usual
signature with the date thereof.

22. Rewards:

On the conviction of any offender under the Act, the Collector may grant
to any person who appears to him to have contributed thereto a reward not
exceeding such sum as the State Government may fix in this behalf.

CHAPTER I (D)

Guidelines On System Of Payment Of Stamp Duty, Transfer Duty,
Registration Charges Etc., Through Banks

( Memo No. G1/16619/03 dated 27-10-2003 of the IGR&S
Hyderabad).

The Government accorded permission to the Inspector General of Regn.&
Stamps to work out operational modalities for payment of money towards Stamp
duty, Registration Fee etc., into Government Treasury through the designated
Branches of State Bank of India / Hyderabad / Nationalized Banks (Vide
G.O.Ms.No.953 dated 10-9-2003 and G.O.Ms.No.958, dated 13-9-2003)

Accordingly, basing on the experience of implementation of this system in
Hyderabad District from 22-09-2003 the following operational Guidelines for
collection of Stamp Duty, Registration Fee etc., through designated Branches
of State Bank of Hyderabad / State Bank of India are issued.

1) Each Sub-Registrar office will have a separate designated Branch of
State Bank of Hyderabad / State Bank of India. The name and address
of that Branch should conspicuously be displayed in the notice board of
that SRO.

2)  Anon-drawal “Stamp Duty Collection Account” will be opened in the
designated Branch of the Bank as ordered in the G.Os mentioned above.
Specimen signatures of the Bank authorities will be furnished to the Sub-
Registrars for verification of receipts issued by the Bank and those of
Sub-Registrars to the Bank authorities.

4)

Two types of challan forms, i.e., one challan for public use and another
for SRO use are designed. The District Registrars should get the challan
forms printed in triplicate in light blue colour estimating the requirement
of the challans for the period upto March, 2004. The expenditure for
printing may be met from user charges and the amount requried for this
purpose may be got alloted by the Inspectore General of Registration &
Stamps separately. Sufficient stock of the challan forms and rubber stamps
denoting the name of Bank Branch with A/C No. should be made
available both at the Banks and at the Sub-Registrar offices. The challans
shall be supplied free of cost to the parties.

The party has to pay the amount through challan in triplicate in the
designated Branch of the Bank, which is attached to that Sub-Registrar
office only, where the document is to be: presented and the Bank will
give unique number to the challan and the receipt. The challan and the
receipt have to be accepted in that particular Sub-Registrar office only.

The Sub-Registrar/Assistant has to guide the public in filling up of the
challan and add his initials, if the party approaches him with challan before
remittance. However, the parties are at liberty to pay the amounts through
challans directly in the designated Branches.

It is important to note that the payment of Stamp Duty, Transfer Duty,
Registration fee etc., should be through a separate challan for each
document by the parties concerned. Payment of amounts through one
challan for multiple documents should not be accepted as the challan and
receipt are unique for each document.

The Sub-Registrar shall, on production of the Challan and Bank receipt,
verify the signature on the receipt with the specimen signature of the
Bank authority and issue a receipt to the parties with details of payment
and proceed with registration if the document is otherwise in order. He
shall note the details of payment made through Badk challan in the
presentation endorsement by denoting the amount through Bank
challan/Receipt. After registration of the document the following
endorsement shall be made on the page containing registration
endorsement”

“Rs. towards Stamp duty including Transfer duty
U/S 41 of L.S.Act and Rs. towards Registration fee on the
chargeable value of Rs.. were paid by the party
through SBI/SBH. Receipt Number. dated ___ at

Branch.”

the S.R.O. on the date of payment, If the party presents such challan at

challan register as well as in the daily challan register.

along with challans (S.R.O copies) to the Sub-Registrars at the end of
the day for verification.

Chapter I ( E)

THE ANDHRA PRADESH STAMP (FRANKING IMPRESSION OF
STAMPS) RULES, 2005

[G.O.Ms.No.1455, Revenue (Registration-I), 26" July, 2005]

(Published in A.P.Gazette (extra ordinary) Rules supplement
dt.16.8.2005 )

In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 74 and 75 read with
clause (c) of sub-section (13) of Section 2 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899
(Central Act II of 1899) and as amended by the Indian Stamp (Andhra Pradesh
Amendment) Act, 2003 (Act No.8 of 2003) and all other powers hereunto
enabling him, the Governor of Andhra Pradesh hereby makes the following
rules, namely:-

1.Short title and Commencement:-

(1) These rules may be called “The Andhra Pradesh Stamp (Franking
Impression of Stamps) Rules, 2005.”

(2) They shall come into force from the date of publication of these rules in
the Andhra Pradesh Gazette (Published in A.P. Gazette dt. 16-08-2005
142 Franking impression of Stamps Rules 2005

2. Definitions:-

In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,-

(a) “Act” means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Central Act II of 1899);

(b)  “Authourised User” means any Body incorporate or organisation including
any insurance company or Scheduled Commercial Bank, authorised by
the Commissioner & Inspector General of Registration and
Stamps/Chief Controlling Revenue Authority to use the machine
for making impression of Stamps indicating the payment of Stamp
Duty on the instruments for their internal use or for providing service to
the public on obtaining Stamp Vendors License from the Competent
Authority.

Provided that the Stamp Vendors licensed to vend the stamps may also be
authorised by the Commissioner & Inspector general of Registration and Stamps/
Chief Controlling Revenue Authority after verification of antecedents to use
the Franking Machines for providing service to the public.

(c) “Form” means the form appended to these rules:
(d) “Government” means the Government of Andhra Pradesh,

(e) “Proper Officer” means the Assistant Inspector General (Stamps), Office
of the Commissioner & Inspector General of Registration and Stamps,
Sub-Registrar/Superintendents in the Office of the Commissioner &
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps and the Sub-Registrar
appointed under the Registration Act, 1908 and such other officers as
may be specified by the Government in this behalf who are empowered
to affix and impress labels by franking machine as per Rule 9 of the
Indian Stamp Rules, 1925.

3. Scope and extent of use of the Franking Machine:-

The Franking Machines shall be used for franking impression of stamps
upto a value of Rs. 1,000/- on all kinds of instruments under the provisions of the
Indian Stamp Act, 1899 and the rules made thereunder.

“Provided that the franking impression may be’made to denote stamp
duty upto Rs.2,00,000/- (Two lakhs) on every non-registerable instrument
by the departmental counters and authorised users like Banks and Corporate
Institutions (G.O.Ms.No.599 Rev (Reg.1) dept, dated 26.5.2006

Editors Note : -

The proviso is applicable only to Banks and Corporate Institutions

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 

Franking impression of Stamps Rules 2005 143

4. Procedure regarding use of Franking Machine by the Proper
Officer:-

(1) Franking Machines shall be installed at the Office of the Commissioner
and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, Hyderabad, Offices
of the District Registrars and Offices of the Sub-Registrars and in any
other office as may be authorised by the Chief Controlling Revenue
Authority in Andhra Pradesh for impressing Stamps indicating the
payment of Stamp Duty on the instruments chargeable with duty.

(2) The machine shall be operated under the strict control and supervision of
the Proper Officer after the machine is installed in the presence of the
Proper Officer.

(3) . Before the machine is put to use, the same shall be authorisedly loaded
and sealed by the Assistant Inspector General (Stamp), Office of the
Commissioner & Inspector General of Registration and Stamps or District
Registrar or Sub-Registrar or such other officer authorised by the
Commissioner& Inspector General of Registration and Stamp/Chief
controlling Revenue Authority.

(4) _ The Assistant Inspector General (Stamps), Office of the Commissioner
& Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, Andhra Pradesh,
Hyderabad or the District Registrars or the Officers authourised under
sub-rule (3) shall maintain a Register in Form No.1 regarding loading and
reloading and shall send a return in Form No.2 to the District Registrar
every month.

(S) The Proper Officer other than the District Registrar shall take permission
in writing from the District Registrar well in advance regarding periodical
loading of the machine. The machine shall be loaded or reloaded by
such Proper Officer only after receiving permission from the District
Registrar. In respect of each reloading, the entries shall be made in
Form No.3, which shall be authenticated by the Proper Officer. The
permission for loading should be sought by the Proper Officer in such a
manner ihat the machine shall not remain idle for want of reloading.
Monthly returns shall be sent in Form No.2 to the District Registrar every
month and the District Registrar shall consolidate the returns received in
Form No.2 and send a return every month to the concerned Deputy
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, who shall make a review
of the same and send a copy to the Commissioner and Inspector General
of Registration and Stamps/Chief Controlling Revenue Authority.

(6) The access code to the numeric of the Franking Machines shall be
exclusively with the Assistant Inspector General (Stamps), Office of the
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps Andhra
144 Franking impression of Stamps Rules 2005
Pradesh, Hyderabad or District Registrar who shall be responsible for
non-disclosure, thereof to any person and who shall maintain a separate
register in respect of each loading/reloading/incrementing of the amount
which shall be in his/her personal custody.

(7) The Proper Officer shall ensure that the seals are not tampered with in
any way by any person or that the machine is not handled by any
unauthorised persons.

(8) The Proper Officer shall be responsible for the custody of the machine.
A register in Form No.4, shall be maintained in which the meter readings
are recorded separately, both at the commencement of.the day and at
the closing of the day.

(9) The parties desirous of having stamps impressed on any instrument
specified in Rule 3 shall make an application in Form No.5 along with the
instrument and pay the value of stamps to be impressed to the Proper
Officer authorised to use Franking machine.

(10) On receipt of the application, the Proper Officer, after satisfying himself
of the payment made by the parties, shall emboss the instruments by
means of Franking Machine with the requisite amount of Stamp Duty.
Thereafter the Proper Officer shall affix his signature in the space provided
on the impressed stamps.

(11) All the applications received for stamping shall be kept in a file, each
being serially numbered and the particulars entered in the Register in
Form No.6.

(12) The Deputy Inspector General of Registration and Stamps and other
Inspecting officers shall in the course of their inspection tours, ensure
that these rules are complied with. They shall also verify credits at
random, on different days in each month since the last inspection in respect
of sale of stamps made through Franking Machine and record the result
in their inspection or visit notes by adding a certificate in the relevant
records.

5. Use of Franking Machines by the authorised users:-

(1) An authorisation for use of Franking Machine may be granted by the
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps/Chief
Controlling Revenue Authority on application, filed by the intending user
along with an undertaking and Indemnity Bond duly stamped in Form
No.7.

(2) The intending user shall pay a fee of Rs.1,000/- for grant of Authorisation
for use of the Franking Machine along with the application. Authorisation
shall be valid for a period of one calendar year from the date of

The Chief Controlling Revenue Authority reserves himself/herself the

The authorised user shall at his own cost and through the Chief Controlling
Revenue Authority, obtain Frankn Machine of approved model and
make from the approved manufacturer. The model, the make, unique
number of the machine and particulars of the supplier shall be specified
in the authorisation. |

(A) The authorisation for each Franking Machine may be renewed every
year on payment of a Fee of Rs.1,000/-. The renewal will be subject to
satisfaction of the Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration
and Stamps/Chief Controlling Revenue Authority about proper use of
the machine. For this purpose he will obtain report on the following
points:

Instances of tampering of seals;

About the mechanical efficiency of the unit;

Average daily usage during the past twelve months;

Whether there is any suspicion about the mis-use of the machine;
Maintenance of connected records.

Where there is Prima facie suspicion, that the machine is not being used
properly, the renewal may be refused and the machine be kept in the
custody of the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority.

The application for renewal shall be accompanied with a report from the
supplier or his authorised dealer as to whether or not the machine is in
proper working order. In the case of an adverse report the authorisation
will not be renewed.

The Authorised User shall apply for renewal of authorisation a month in
advance of the date of expiry of authorisation in force through the District
Registrar. If the authorised user does not want to get the authorisation
renewed or has not applied for the renewal, he/she shall surrender the
machine to the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority on the day on which
the authorisation in force expires.

When the authorised user wishes to discontinue the usage of machine,
the amount remaining unused at the time of such surrender shall be
refunded.

The authorised machine shall be utilised for franking/impressing stamps

The authorised user shall send account of the monthly use of the machine

The government or the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority shall not be

account of misuse or mis-handling of the machine or for any damage
caused to the machine or loss of the machine on any ground.

The authorised user is not permitted to keep with him any unserviceable
or worn-out Franking Machine. He shall surrender the same on the next
day of its having been rendered as such to the Chief Controlling Revenue
Authority, who shall ensure that all the parts of the said machine are
surrendered with the machine. This fact shall be entered in the franking
machine record book and ledger pertaining to the machine. The authorised
user shall also surrender the authorisation to the Chief controlling Revenue
Authority.

The authorised user must take adequate steps to guard against the
fraudulent use of the machine. Any change in the location of the machine
except in case of repairs, shall be notified by the authorised user to the
authorizing authority and also to the District Registrars concerned.

The authorised user shall maintain the following records separately for
each franking machine:

Franking Machine Register regarding posting in Form No.8.

Franking Machine Records Book inform No.9

The authorised user shall at all reasonable times allow authorised officer
or the authorizing authority or the District Registrar to inspect the machine
and collect records without notice.

The authorised user shall not sell or transfer or dispose of in any manner
whatsoever the Franking Machine.

(4) The seal of Franking machine and pliers for the lead seal for sealing

(9) Franking or impression on any instrument shall be allowed upto an amount

(10) All franks or impressions for the purpose of payment of stamp duty must
be made as far as possible on the right top corner of the first page of the
instrument itself.

(11) The impression or franks of the machine recorded on the instrument
should not be interfered with in anyway. The impression should be in
bright colour, clear and distinct and should not overlap. Where by mistake
a wrong amount is impressed then that impression shall be torn from the
instrument and pasted in the register of daily posting and shall be
authenticated by the authorised user or proper officer. At the time of
resetting, set off equal to the amount of wrong impression shall be given.

(12) The Assistant Inspector General (Stamps), Office of the Commissioner

(a) Master Ledger in Form No. 10; and

(b) List of Authorised Users in Form No.11.

The above Registers shall be verified every year by the Deputy Inspector
General of Registration and Stamps concerned/Deputy Inspector General (R&S)
in the Office of the Commissioner & Inspector General of Registration and
Stamps, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad and a Certificate shall be appended after
satisfying about proper maintenance.

7. Procedure for repairs:-

(1) The maintenance, service and cleaning of the Franking Machine or any
repairs thereto, including the replacement of any parts thereof shall be
the responsibility of the authorised user and at his own cost and expenses.

(2) The procedure for repair of Franking Machine shall be as follows:-

(a) _ the users of Franking machine shall in the event of the machine requiring
repairs immediately stop using the same;

(b) The user shall immediately, in such event, bring the fact to the notice of
the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority who shall immediately notify
the manufacturer or his authorised dealer in this regard;

(c) | The authorised user shall make his own arrangements for transportation
of the machine to the authori cd officer or District Registrar;

(d) | Whenever a machine is fo: nd to be defective, the authorised user should
bring the machine to the Assistant Inspector General (Stamps), Office

Necessary entries to the effect that the machine has been repaired and
re-sealed and the authorisation therein will be made in the Franking
Machine record books, ledger and register of postings. The meter reading
at that time shall also be recorded in these books;

The dealer shall maintain a register containing the following information:-
Name of authorised user;

Model and manufacturing number of the machine;

Particulars of authorisation for the use of the said machine;

Name of the office through which the machine is received;

Date of repair;

Date of despatch after repair;

Particulars of the part of the machine

(i) repaired (ii) replaced

Signature of authorised official of the manufacturer or his authorised
dealer;

Signature of authorised user or his representative.

The authorised repairer or the manufacturer shall also enter in the job
card and Franking Machine record book the particulars of the parts
repaired and replaced with his signature and date.

The record of repair and job card have to be preserved for two years
and shall be open for checkup by the authorised official of the Chief
Controlling Revenue Authority or the Deputy Inspector General (R&S)
or Assistant Inspector General (Stamp), Office of the Commissioner
150

(6)

and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps. Andhra Pradesh,
Hyderabad or District Registrar at any time.

The reason for delay of more than fifteen days in repairing the franking
machine shall be investigated by a Committee consisting of Deputy
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, District Registrar
concerned and a Technical Officer of the Company to find out if there is
anything to suspect the misuse of the franking machine under repair.

The Chief Controlling Revenue Authority reserves the right to deauthorise
and keep the franking machine under custody, if there is any deviation
from the prescribed conditions including non use or irregular use of machine
or any misuse of the machine. The Government of Andhra Pradesh
shall not be responsible for any loss, which the authorised user may incur
thereby, However, any sum that may be due to the Government on
account of Stamp Duty shall be liable to be recovered as arrears of land
revenue under Revenue Recovery Art.

QUESTIONS & ANSWERS

What is meant by Franking impression of Stamps?

“Franking impression of Stamps” means making impressions of Stamps
indicating the payment of Stamp duty on the instruments (Rule 2(b)).
Explain scope and extent of use of the Franking machine?
Franking machine is used for franking impression of stamps upto a value
of Rs.1,000/- on all kinds of instruments under the provisions of the
Indian Stamp Act, 1899. (Rule 3).

However Banks and corporate Institutions and the Departmental
Counters are authorised to denote stamp duty upto Rs.2,00,000/- on every
NON-REGISTERABLE instrument by means of franking (Proviso under
Rule 3)

Who is competent to authorise officers other than the officers of
the Registration and Stamps department to use Franking
Machine?

The Chief Controlling Revenue Authority is the competent authority (Rule
Ai).
160

4)

5)

6)

1)

8)

Explain the procedure for periodical loading of the Franking
Machine?

The proper Officer other than the District Registrar should take permission
in writing from the District Registrar, well in advance, regarding periodical
loading of the machine. In respect of each loading entries should be
made in the Register of daily readings (Form No.3) and be authenticated
by the proper officer. (Rule 4(5)).

What are the precautions to safe guard the “Access Code”?
The ‘Access Code’ to the numeric of the Franking Machine shall be
exclusively with the District Registrar. He shall be responsible for non-
disclosure thereof to any person. He shall maintain a separate register in
respect of each loading/Reloading incrementing of the amount. This
Register shall be in the personal custody of the District Registrar (Rule
4(6)).

Detail the procedure to have impression of stamps on an
Instrument by means of Franking Machine?

The party shall make an application (Form No.5) to the proper officer to
affix Impressed Stamps on document along with the document and pay
the value of stamps to be impressed. The “ Proper Officer “ shall emboss
the document by means of Franking Machine with the requisite value of
the amount of stamp duty and affix his signature in the space provided on
the Impressed Stamps (Rule4(9 &10)).

How the compliance of the rules in respect of Franking
impressions of stamps are ensured?

The Deputy Inspector General of Registration and Stamps and other
Inspecting Officers shall, in the course of their inspection tours shall
have to verify credits at random on different days in each month since
the last inspection in respect of sale of stamps made through Franking
Machine and record the result in their Inspection or visit notes by adding
a certificate in the relevant records (Rule 4(12))

What are the conditions imposed on ‘Authorised Users’ with
regard to the use of Franking Machine?

The Authorised user must take adequate steps to guard against the
fraudulent use of the machine. Any change in the location of the machine,
except in case of repairs, should be notified by the Authorised user to the
Authorising Authority and also to the District Registrar concerned. (Rule
5(13)). The Authorised user, at all reasonable times, must allow
Authorised Officers or the Authorising authority or the District Registrar
to inspect the machine and collect records without notice (Rule 5(15)).

 
Franking impression of Stamps Rules 2005 161

9)

10)

1)

12)

15)

Mention the records that are to be maintained by the Authorised

user ?

The Authorised user should maintain.

a)  Franking Machine Register regarding posting in Form No.8 and

b) _ Franking Machine Records book in the prescribed in form No.9.
[Vide Rule 5(14)]

What is the procedure for setting or resetting Franking machine

and sealing thereof by the Authorised user?

The Authorised user should pay in advance through Bank a minimum

sum of Rs.50,000/- as advance stamp duty. He should produce the

Franking Machine and the record book register regarding the posting in

the office of the District Registrar. The entries in respect of advance

payments made in the Franking Machine record book of the Authorised

user and in the concerned office records should be got attested by the

concerned Officer (Rule 6(1), (2) & (3)).

What are the circumstances when the Authorised user should

stop using the Franking Machine?

The Authorised user should immediately stop using the Franking Machine

and bring the matter to the notice of the Authorising Authority and the

Dt. Registrar in the following circumstances.

a) Breaking or Tampering with the seals.

b) Discrepancy in the Meter readings (Rule 6(7)).

What is the amount allowed for franking of impression of stamps

on an instrument by an ‘Authorised User’ .

The amount that can be impressed on any instrument by an Authorised

User is upto Rs.1,000/- only. But Authorised users like Banks and

Corporate Institutions and Departmental counters can denote stamp duty

upto Rs.2,00,000/- on every NON-REGISTERABLE instrument (Sub

Rule 9 under Rule 6).

Detail the procedure for repairs to Franking Machine?

Vide (a) to (e) under sub Rule (2) of Rule 7.

What are the details to be furnished in the Register maintained

by the Dealer or the Manufacturer?

Vide Sub Rule (i) under Rule 7.

What is meant by the term “Job Card” and specify the period of

its preservation?

The job card is a record maintained by the Authorised repairer or the
162

Franking impression of Stamps Rules 2005

16)

17)

18)

Manufacturer containing information regarding the particulars of parts
repaired or replaced attested with his dated signature. The job card is
preservable for two years (Sub Rules (3) & (4) under Rule 7).

Who are the members to constitute as a “Committee” for
investigating reasons for delay of more than 15 days in repairing
the Franking Machine?

The Committee is constituted with the following officers.

i) | Deputy Inspector General of Registration and Stamps.

ii) District Registrar concerned.

iii) | Technical Officer of the company (Sub Rule (5) of Rule 7)

How the recovery is effected in the case of stamp duty due to
Government?

The recovery of stamp duty due to the Government from the authorised
user is effected as arrears of land Revenue under Revenue Recovery
Act (Sub Rule (6) of Rule 7)

Enumerate the “Dos” and “Don’ts” in operating Franking Machine
“Dos” Check if the seal is intact, Machine is unlocked, Denominations
are in Xerox position, there is sufficient ink in the ink well, date in the
Machine is set and place the handle in 6’ O clock position

“Don’ts” The handle should never be rotated anti clock wise. Do not
rotate the handle unless it is required for franking purpose. (G.S.O. No.
2/21659/95, dt.6.12.95)

(C&IGRS. Circular Memo No.GSO 2/21659/95, dt.6.12.1995)

 
 

 

Impounding of Documents 163

Chapter I ( F )
IMPOUNDING OF DOCUMENTS

1. Every person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive
evidence and every person in charge of a Public office except an officer
of Police, before whom any Instrument chargeable in his opinion, with
duty is produced or comes in the performance of his functions shall, if it
appears to him that such Instrument is not duly stamped, impound the
same as per Section 33(1) of Indian Stamp Act.

2. The expression “Duly Stamped” in Section 2 (Vide S.No. 37 under
Chapter 2) would seem to mean not only bearing stamp of proper value
but also stamped at the right time (Sec. 17. 18 and 19) in the proper
manner (Sec. 13 and 14) with proper description of stamp (Sec. 10 and
11) under the Stamp Rules and duly cancelled (Sec. 12 and 13)

3. ASub Registrar is an officer in charge of Public office within the perview
of Section 33.

4. When insufficiently stamped document is presented before a Registering
Officer, he shall impound it under Sec.33 of Indian Stamp Act and forward
it to the Collector (Dist. Registrar) (under Section 38 (2)) registration
being suspended (R.R.32 (ii) and pending orders on such reference to a
Registrar or prior to sending a document to the Collector, the registering
officer may however record admission of the execution and examination
of witnesses if any(R.R.32(iii)).

5. In every Registration Office a Register in Form (V). (Vide Proforma
after para 6 below) shall be maintained in which every document
impounded shall be entered on the date on which the register‘ng officer
decides to impound the same [S.0.462].

6. A document impounded by a Sub Registrar shall be forwarded to the
Registrar to whom he is subordinate together with an extract of columns
1 to 8 of the Register of impounded documents signed and dated by the
Registering officer. A copy of the document shall also accompany the
extract. No covering letter is necessary [S.0.462].

7. If the Registrar is ofc opinion that the Document is properly and sufficiently
stamped and is needlessly impounded, he shall return it to the Sub Registrar
after adding a certificate on the document under Sec. 42 that the document
is duly stamped.

8. (i) _ The Registrar, if he is of the opinion that a document forwarded to

him is not duly stamped, shall inform the Sub-Registrar concerned,
of the deficit stamp duty and penalty to be collected (S.0.462)
after giving reasonable opportunity to the party to represent his
case before final orders are passed (Bds.LDis 683/W/64. dt. 20-
02-1965 with IG’s Endt. No. 51/5768/65-1 Dt.12-3-1965)

ii) On receipt of this intimation the Sub-Registrar shall communicate
the decision to both the claimant and the executant requiring payment
to him by either of them of the amount (S.0.462).

(iii) The amount shall be brought to Account ’C’ and remitted into
Treasury on a separate challan.

(iv) The (Miscellaneous) receipt shall be granted for the amount
received,

(v) The fact of payment of deficit duty and Penalty shall be reported
immediately to the Registrar with particulars of name and residence
of Payer (Sec. 42(1) of I.S.Act) and date of payment and challan |
which should also be submitted to the Registrar.

Impounding of Documents 165

(vi) On receipt from the Sub-Registrar of the intimation of payment the
Registrar shall endorse on the document as required by Sec. 42(i)
of Indian Stamp Act and return it to the Sub-Registrar.

(vii) On receipt of the document, duly certified by the Registrar, the
Sub-Registrar will admit the document for Registration.

(viii) The entire stamp duty paid on the document i.e., duty paid in the
shape of stamp initially and duty paid in cash subsequently should
be accounted for in Account ‘A’ and Transfer Duty should be
allocated on the entire stamp duty. If the document is found to be
insufficiently stamped at the time of presentation some parties come
forward with new stamps purchased to make up the deficiency
and attempt to attach them to the document by canceling them
with a line or by some writings. This is highly objectionable and
Stamp Act does not allow such a practice.

(ix) Documents produced in connection with the Undervaluation enquiry,
the Sub-Registrar cannot impound as the enquiry is an administrative
function but he can send it to Registrar for impounding if it is not
properly stamped. After compounding under Sec. 70 the Registrar
can proceed under Sec. 40 and 42 of Indian Stamp At but not
under Sec. 35 and 38(i) as it is not admitted in evidence. The person
who produced deficitly stamped document has to pay the deficit
stamp duty under Sec. 44 of Indian Stamp Act.

A Sub Registrar cannot impound a registered document since he becomes
functus officio after he registers the document [(Inspector’s General S1/
27106/68 dated 28-10-65) (AIR 1966 Madhya Pradesh 20(V) 58 CM)
(R.G. 1967 Dec. 1)]

If an unstamped or deficitly stamped document is presented in evidence
in the course of will enquiries, the Sub-Registrar can add certificate under
section 42(1) of Indian Stamp Act after collecting deficit stamp duty and
penalty. If a wrong adjudication is made by a Registrar as Collector and
the document is returned to the Sub-Registrar, the Sub-Registrar has no
option except to register it. Sub-Registrar should clearly understand the
basis of impounding. If on the face of it the document is duly Stamped, it
has to be accepted. At times SubRegistrars impound documents which
should be dealtwith under Sections 27 or 47-A .Following illustrations
will clarify the point.

A sale of property in a gram Panchayat for a consideration of Rs. 10,000/
- in respect of property worth Rs. 12,000/- (as mentioned in the deed
itself) is presented on a stamp of Rs.1,100/-. The document has to be
166 Destruction of impounded documents
impounded for the deficit duty of Rs.220/-. (The document was dated
1-4-2002)

II) Sale for Rs 10,000/-According to the party the Market value is
Rs.10,000/- but according to Basic Value Register, the Market value is
Rs.12,000/- Stamp borne by the document is Rs.990/-. The Sub-Registrar
should keep the document pending and then refer under Sec.47A as the
party is disputing the Market Value of Rs.12,000/-

Il) A Simple Mortgage bond for Rs.10,000/- is presented before a Sub
Registrar on a stamp of Rs.300/-. During the course of examination by
the Sub Registrar the executant states that he had delivered possession.
In such a case the Sub-Registrar should not impound it treating it as
Mortgage with possession requiring stamp duly as such. He should register
the document since it is duly stamped. He should record statements from
the parties as regards delivery of possession and should file a prosecution,
under sections 27 read with section 64 of stamp Act for not truly and
correctly setting forth the facts I.ading to the chargeability of the
instrument.

Note:- Deficit stamp duty and penalty need not be included in total value of
Stamps.

Vide Annexure for Rules for the destruction of instruments impounded
under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899

ANNEXURE

RULES FOR DESTRUCTION OF INSTRUMENTS IMPOUNDED
UNDER INDIAN STAMP ACT, 1899

In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (b) of sub-section (2) of
Section 3 of the Destruction of Records Act, 1917 (Central Act 5 of 1917) the
Chief Controlling Revenue Authority is pleased to make the following rules
regarding the disposal of certain instruments impounded under Section 33 and
dealt with under Sections 35, 40 and 41 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Central
Act 2 of 1899).

lL These rules may be called the Rules for the Destruction of Instruments
impounded under the Indian Stamp Act.

2. In these Rules : -

(i). "Instrument" means any instrument other than the instruments chargeable
with a duty of 20 paise or Bill of Exchange or Promissory Note

(ii) "Collector" means within the limits of Hyderabad and Secunderabad, the
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps and outside those limits,

the Collector of a District and Officers generally authorised to act under
Sections 35,38(2),40 and 41 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

 
 

 

Destruction of impounded documents

167

3. The Coolector shall maintain in the form appended to these rules a register
of all instruments impounded by him under Section 33 or received by him
under Section 38(2) and dealtwith under Section 35,40 and 41 of the

Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

4, Such instruments in respect of which deficit stamp duty and penalty are
ordered to be written off shall be retained for a period of 12 years (twelve
years) from the date of their execution and at the end of that period, the
Collector shall cause them to be destoryed by fire in his presence or in
the immediate presence of a Gazetted Officer. The fact of such
destruction shall be noted in the Register prescribed in Rule 3 above.

168 Adjudication under section 4

CHAPTER I(G)
Adjudication under Sec. 41 of the Stamp Act in respect of documents
falling U/Sec. 47 A (Executive instructions)
(Sub-Registrar’s functions)

In cases where a document is not duly stamped, then Collector has power
under Section 41 to adjudicate the document if satisfied that the omission to
duly stamp has been occasioned by accident, mistake or urgent necessity. The
deficit duty can be collected by the Collector if the person voluntarily produced
the document offering to pay the deficit duty. There is no provision to collect
penalty under this section. The time limit for the party to avail the benefit
of this section is one year from the date of execution. All District Registrars
and Sub-Registrars are Collectors under this section. If during the course of an
inspection or audit it is noticed that a document is insufficiently stamped, the
Sub Registrar has to advise the party to take the advantage conferred under
Section 4! before the expiry of one year from the date of execution of the
document.

Documents executed not in conformity with the market value, the ordinary
recourse is to refer such cases under section 47-A to the authorities empowered
to determine Market Value. If the party pleads that by mistake he had not
adopted the market value and expresses his willingness to pay the deficit duty,
he may be allowed to do so and instead of following the procedure in section
47-A the registering officer shall follow the procedure laid down in sec. 41.

Where the party voluntarily seeks to get the document adjudicated in case
where he fails to pay duty on market value, the party shall file an application
duly affixed with Court-fee label of Re. 1/-, under Sec. 41 for adjudication
voluntaring to pay the deficit stamp duty. If the application is filed before
registration, the deficit stamp duty and the registration fee should be levied on
the Market Value. The Sub Registrar should file the application with his remarks.
The deficit duty should be credited to relevant account head.

Certificate under Sec, 41 on the document shall be added in the following
form after retaining an office copy of the certificate in the file.

CHAPTER I(H)
Rules for collection of Duties secured in the course of Inspection
[G..O.Ms.No. 997, Rev.(u), Dt.14-8-1986]

In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 75 of the Indian Stamp
Act, 1899 (Central Act II of 1899) and of all other powers hereunto enabling
and in supersession of the rules issued in G.O.Ms.No.702, Revenue, dated the
19" April 1961 and published at page 284 of Part-I, Rules Supplement of the
Andhra Pradesh Gazette, dated the 14" May, 1961, the Governor of Andhra
Pradesh hereby makes the following rules for the collection of duties secured
in the course of inspection under Section 73 of the Indian Stamp (Andhra Pradesh
Amendment) Act, 1986. These rules shall come into force on the 16" day of
August, 1986.

RULES
1 In these rules unless the context otherwise requires:-

(a) ‘Act’ means, the Indian Stamp (A.P. Amendment) Act, 1986.

(b) ‘Inspector-General of Registration and Stamps’ includes the person
authorised in writing by him as the Collector appointed under Sec.
73 of the Act to exercise the powers under that Section.

(c) ‘Head of office’ means, the Head of the office inspected by the
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps under Section 73.

(d) ‘Section’ means a section of the Act.

(e) ‘Any premises’ includes any public office or any place where
registers, books, documents etc., are kept under the custody of a
person the inspection whereof may tend to secure any duty.

2. (1) The notes of inspection under Section 73 shall be sent to the Head
of office with a copy to the Head of the District office, if the office
inspected is subordinate to him, or with a copy to the Head of the
Department concerned if the office inspected is the District or
Regional Office.

(2) The first report of the compliance shall be sent to the Inspector-
General of Registration and Stamps, immediately on receipt of the
notes of inspection by the Head office, with copy to the Head of
the District Office concerned, if the office inspected is subordinate
to him or with a copy to the Head of the Department if the office
inspected is a District or Regional-Office.

3. When deficitly stamped documents are detected during the course

of inspection the following procedure shall be followed:

(i) The Inspector-General of Registration and Stamps or the person

 
 

 

 

 

Collection of duties secured in Audit 171

 

authorised by him shall seize and impound such documents and
after giving an opportunity to the parties levy deficit duties if any,
without penalty and collect the same-from the persons liable to
pay under sub-section (3) of Section 73 and add the following
certificate on the original document:-

“I hereby certify that the deficit / proper stamp duty of
