(ii) If the parties fail to pay the deficit under sub-rule (i), it shall be collected
by the Head of office. The amounts so collected shall be remitted to the
Treasury under the following Head of account by means of a challan.

Deficit duties

Major Head =: “M.H. 030 Stamps & Registration fee.
MinorHead : M.H-C.~— Stamps Non- Judicial
Sub-Head : 010 Duty on impressing of documents.

The Head of office shall then forward the original challan to the Inspector-
General, Registration and Stamps who shall add the certificate prescribed in
this sub-rule on the original document and return them to the Head of office.

Note

When complete postal address or sufficient particulars of the parties
are available in the documents, the notice providing them an opportunity against
the levy of deficit stamp duties shall be issued by the Inspector General of
Registration and Stamps direct. If such address is not available in the documents
or if such notice issued in the first instance is returned undelivered, the notice
shall be served by the Head of office inspected.

(ii) If the parties fail to pay such deficit duties, the Inspector-General of
Registration and Stamps shall forward the original document to the
Collector exercising powers under Section 48 of the Indian Stamp Act,
1899 over the area for effecting recovery by coercive process. After
the amounts are so collected, the procedure laid down in sub-rule(i) shall
be followed.

In the absence of original documents, and on the basis of copies of such
documents, if they are found to be not duly stamped, the procedure for
collection of the duty as laid down in the rule (iii) shall be followed:

If the parties are aggrieved by the levy of duties they may apply to the
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps for revision before the
certificate prescribed under Rule 3 is added.

In the event of deficit duties not being recovered even after adopting the
procedure outlined in Rule 3 or if the circumstances of any case do not
permit the recovery of the loss to the Government from the parties, the
Inspector General of Registration and Stamps shall report the matter'to
the Head of the Department concerned for taking such appropriate action
as he deems fit against the person adiudged as responsible for the loss
sustained by the Government.

Every public officer shall keep copies of all documents produced before
him and returned to the parties before or after the disposal of the case.
The Inspector General of Registration and Stamps may write off
irrecoverable arrears of deficit stamp duty levied during the inspection
upto Rs. 1,000/- and the Commissioner of Survey, Settlement and Land
Records (now the Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration
and Stamps who is the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority from 25-3-
1995) may write off sums exceeding Rs.1,000/-. The Inspector General
of Registration and Stamps may authorise any of his subordinate officers
to write of irrecoverable arrears of stamp duty upto Rs.500/-

Sub Registrar's function under section 16 199

Sub Registrar’s functions as Collector
under sections 16, 41 & 42 of Indian Stamp Act,1899

1) Denoting duty already paid (Section 16):-

Section 16 of the Stamp Act provides for denoting upon certain documents
the duty already paid on the relevant original documents. All registering officers
are “COLLECTORS” u/s 16 of the Indian Stamp Act 1899 (S.0.476(a)). A
certificate under Section 16 denoting the duty already paid on the relevant
original Instrument shall be added on the subsequent Instruments in respect of
which the duty was paid on the basis of the Stamp duty paid on the original
Instruments (S.0.476(c)(i)). Vide para 4 infra).

2) Documents for which Section 16 is applicable:-

The following categories of instruments attract Section 16 of the Stamp
Act.

i) Sale in favour of mortgagee stamped under the last. proviso to section 24
of the Stamp Act.

i) Further charge with possession on Simple Mortgage

iii) | Supplemental deed falling under section 4.

iv) Duplicates

v) Counterparts

vi) Lease deeds executed in favour of mortgagee without possession falling
under the explanation to Article 35 of Schedule 1-A

vii) Auxiliary, Collateral, additional and substituted Security deeds

viii) Lease, Partition and Settlement deed stamped under Articles 31, 40 &
49 respectively of Schedule 1A

ix) Sale deeds executed in pursuance of an Agreement to sell stamped either
under Article 6-B or under Article 47 of Schedule 1-A

x) Sale deed transferring house plots by the Co-operative Housing Society
in favour of its members if full stamp duty was paid on the sale deed by
the Society while acquiring the said property.

3) Proforma of application and the certificate under Section 16:-

(i) (a) The presentant of the document should submit an application in writing
duly affixed with a C.F, label of Re.1/- along with the present and the
previous original instruments
(b) The application under Section 16 shall be filed in the FILE OF

5. Abatement of Stamp duty:-

Abatement of Stamp duty to the extent of entitlement only shall be
allowed. A register shall be maintained for watching the details of Stamp duty
paid on agreements and rebate given on sale deeds.

Note:- “entitlement” means the Stamp duty actually payable as on the
date of execution of the document (Section 17 of Indian Stamp Act ).

6) Levy of Transfer Duty:- (surcharge)

duty) on certain classes of documents like Sales, Exchange, Gifts, Mortgages
with possession leases in perpetrity relating to immovable property is also leviable.
Transfer duty also should be added to the Stamp duty actually payable and
totaled for purpose of collection.

Agreement (Art 5): - An agreement is an instrument whereby the
parties willfuly agree to perform certain acts or refrain from doing
something unilaterally or bilaterally.

Annuity (Sec.25) : - Annuity is the amount payable every year. When it
is payable for a definite period the duty should be paid on the total amount.
When it is not terminable with any life in being (living) on the date of
document, it is payable on the total amount payable during 20 years.
When it is terminable with any life, in being, it is payable on the total
amount payable during 12 years.

Apprenticeship Deed (Art 10) : - It is a writing relating to the service
or tuition of any apprentice, Clerk or servant placed with any master to
learn any profession, trade or employment.

“Athentication” means recording the fact of execution of a power by
the principal in the presence of the officer authenticating after proper
identification. Vide Registration Rule 49 (1) for the form of authentication
Award (Art 12) :- It is a decision in writing by any arbitrator or umpire.
For the purpose of Stamp Act, award directing partition should be stamped
as a deed of partition. However awards made on a reference by an
order of court are not chargeable with Stamp Duty. Stamp duty is attracted
in the case of private awards only.

Banker (Sec.2 (1) : - Banker includes a Bank and any person acting as
a Banker (vide Sec 2(1)). A Banker is one who receives money in trust,
to be drawn again as the owner has occasion for it. Banker includes also
persons or a corporation or Company acting as Bankers. (Sec. 3 of
Negotiable Instruments Act.)

Bill of Exchange (Sec.2 (2) & Art. 13 of Sch 1) : - Bill of exchange is
an instrument in writing containing an unconditional order signed by the
maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to,
or to the order of a certain person or to the bearer of the instrument
eg.Cheque. (Vide sec. 5 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1981). It
includes also a hundi and any other document entitling any person to
payment by any other person of, or to draw upon any other person for,
any sum of money. (Sec. 2(2)).

Bill of Exchange Payable on Demand (Sec 2(3)) : - It includes an
order for the payment of any sum of money by a Bill of Exchange or
Promissory Note for the delivery

of any Bill of Exchange or Promissory Note in satisfaction of any sum of
money or for the payment of any sum of money out of any particular
fund, which may or may not be available, or upon any condition or

ofa letter of credit that is any instrument by which one person authorises

Note : Hundi stamps are used for the Bill of Exchange

Bill of Lading (Sec.2 (4) & Art. 14 of Sch 1) : - Bill of lading includes a
" through bill of lading " but does not include a mate's receipt (Sec 2 (4)).
A Bill of Lading is a receipt by the master of a ship for goods bailed to
him for delivery to X or his assigns.

Bond (Sec 2(5) & Art 13 : - Bond includes
any instrument whereby a person obliges himself to pay money to another,

on condition that the obligation shall be void ifa specified act is performed,
or is not performed, as the case may be

any instrument attested by a witness and not payable to order or bearer
whereby a person obliges himself to pay money to another and

any instrument so attested whereby a person obliges himself to deliver
grain or other agricultural produce to another.

First is called "conditional bond”. The second and third are called "simple
bonds". The important word in the definition is "obliges". Therefore no
document can be a bond unless it creates an express obligation to pay.

When a deficitly stamped document is presented for adjudication to a
Collector under Sec.31, the collector becomes functious officio after he
determines the duty payable. He cannot therefore impound the said
document even if the deficit duty if any is not paid.

When a Registering Officer registers a document he becomes functious

‘Hundi : - There is no legal definition of the term "Hundi". The term is

The system is adopted to collect debts and facilitate credit. The Hundi
is mainly an order for payment of money. Duty on such instruments is
payable as Bill of Exchange under Article 13 of Sch.1 of I.S.Act.

Promissory Note ( Pronote ) ( Sec. 2(22) & Art. 49 of Sch 1) :- A

condition or contingency which may or may not be performed or happen.

Public Officer : - The term is not defined in the Act. Every one who is

and receives a compensation whether from Government or otherwise is

The CCRA has been authorised to determine who shall be deemed to

Receipt ( Sec. 2(23) & Art. 53 of Sch. 1) : - A receipt is any note,

Release ( Art. 46 ) : - A deed of release is an instrument whereby a

Rent : ( Sec. 105 of T.P. Act 1882 ) : - Rent is money, a share of crops,

Periodical payments made for the continuous enjoyment of the benefits
under the lease is RENT.

Respondentia Bond ( Art. 47 ) : - It is an instrument securing a loan on
the cargo laden or to be laden on board a ship and making repayment
contingent on the arrival of the cargo at the port of destination.

Sale ( Art. 47-A & Sec. 54 of T.P. Act 1822) : - Sale is not defined in
Stamp Act. It is included in the definition of conveyance (Section 2(10))

promised (Section 54, T.P. Act. 1882)

All Sales are conveyance but all conveyances are not sales. Conveyance
for a “price” alone becomes a sale. This distinction is important because
Transfer Duty under local bodies Act is leviable only on ‘sales but not on
all conveyances. Vv

but sale of property subject to the existing mortgage thereon. The
explanation to section 24 is attracted to such a case (AIR 1984 MP114)

Simple Mortgage ( Sec. 58(b) T.P. Act ) : - Where, without delivering

Spoiled Stamps (Sec. 49(a) and (b) ): - Spoiled stamps fall under two

The first category is dealt with in Sec. 49(a) & (b) and the second
category, in Sec. 49(d). There is a special provision for pronotes and

such stamps deducting 10 Ps for each rupee or fraction of rupee if

following the procedure prescribed in Rules 19 and 20

Stamp ( Sec. 2(26) ):- " Stamp " means any mark, seal or endorsement

and includes an adhesive or impressed stamp for the purpose of duty
chargeable under the Act as inserted by Finance (No.2) Act 2004 (C &
IGR & S endt no. 20067/04 dt:27- 10-2004).

Sublease or Under lease ( Art. 31 ) : - A sub lease or under lease is a
grant by a lessee to another of part or his whole interest under the original
lease reserving to himself a reversion.

Usufrucruary Mortgage ( Sec. 58(d) of T.P. Act 1882) : - Where the

property to the mortgagee authorises him to retain such possession until
payment of the mortgaged money and to receive the rents and profits or
any part of them accruing from the said property and to appropriate

Warrant for Goods ( Art. 56) : - It is an instrument evidencing the title

Will : - A will is a legal declaration of the intention of the testator (Person
who executed the will) with respect to his / her property which he / she
desires to be carried into effect after his / her death (Section 52 (b) of
Indian Succession Act). It is a testamentary disposition of property. Will
can be in anybody's favour. It requires no stamp. The will is always
revokable or variable by the testator during his / her life time.

CHAPTER -3
DISTINCTION BETWEEN TERMS
(Arranged in Alphabetical order)

N.B: In this Chapter

i) "Sec or Section" quoted herein relates to Section of the Indian Stamp
Act, 1899

i) “Art. or Article" quoted herein relates to Article of Schedule 1A to the
Indian Stamp Act, 1899 unless otherwise stated

iti) "Sch" denotes Schedule
iv) "Rule" quoted herein relates to Indian Stamp Rules, 1925
v) " APSM" denotes the Andhra Pradesh Stamp Manual, 1974

TERMS

1. ASSIGNMENT OF LEASE AND TRANSFER OF LEASE : - Both
the terms convey the same meaning. Transfer of lease can be by two
ways, assignment and underlease or sublease (vide S.No.78 below) In
the case of assignment of lease, the lessee transfers all his rights under
the original lease to the transferee who will be answerable to the original
lessor. It is chargeable under Art. 54. Underlease or sublease falls under
Art. 31. In this, the sub lessee is to pay the rent to the original lessee.
The lessee will be responsible to the lessor to the terms and conditions of
the original lease who will hold himself responsible to the lessor to the
terms and conditions of the original lease

2. | AGREEMENT RELATING TO DEPOSIT OF TITLE DEEDS AND
MORTGAGE BY DEPOSIT OF TITLE DEEDS : - Both the classes of
documents are chargeable under Art. 7. They are also called equitable
mortgages. They are executed to secure repayment of money by the
deposit of title deeds evidencing the title to any property other than
marketable security. This is applicable to deposit of title deeds in towns
and places notified under Section 58 (f) of T.P.Act 1872.

3. | AGREEMENT RELATING TO DEPOSIT OF TITLE DEEDS AND
EQUITABLE MORTGAGE : - Vide S.No.2 above

4. | ADHESIVE STAMP AND REVENUE STAMP : - Revenue Stamps
also are adhesive stamps bearing the inscription “India Revenue” of the
denominations of Re. I/-, 25 Ps., 1SPs.,10 ps. and 5 Paise. They are
used for instruments on which stamp duty cannot be paid for the reason
that the necessary stamps are not in circulation. (Rules 13-A and 16).
They are sold through post offices, Treasuries and Stamp Counters in
S.R.Os. The Revenue goes to the State government. Unlicensed Vendors
226

Distinctions between Terms

can sell these stamps. (Section 69(b)). Adhesive stamps are labels affixed
and impressed by "Proper Officers" for indicating the payment of stamp
duty on instruments mentioned in section 11 and rules 13 to 17.
ANNUITY BOND AND ANNUITY MORTGAGE : - An instrument
by which a person obliges to pay’a certain amount periodically to another
person or persons is an Annuity bond chargeable under Art. 13 read with
Sec. 25. Whereas in such a document if property is offered as security
for such payment it is Annuity Mortgage chargeable under Art. 35 read
with Section 25.

ADOPTION DEED AND AUTHORITY TO ADOPT : - Adoption
deed is a non-testamentary instrument recording the fact of taking a
child in adoption registerable in Book 4, An authority to adopt is a deed
by which the husband authorises his wife to adopt a child. It is a
testamentary document registerable in Book 3. An adoption deed does
not require registration unless it creates immediate right in in movable
property. An ‘authority to adopt is compulsorily registerable. (Sc tion 17(3)
Registration Act).

ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION AND MEMORANDUM OF
ASSOCIATION : = A Memorandum of Association contains the objects
for which the company is incorporated, while the Articles of Association
contain the detailed provisions for the working of the Company. The
former is chargeable under Article 34 while the later under Article 11.
ADJUDICATION AND IMPOUNDING : - Adjudication is the act of
determination by the ‘Collector’ of the Stamp Duty payable on an
instrument (Secs. 31 and 40) while impounding is detaining a deficitly or
insufficiently stamped document by the Court or officer before whom it
is produced in the performance of their duties. (Sec. 33).
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT AND BOND : - An acknowledgement (Art.
1) is executed merely to supply evidence of debt. It should not contain
any promise to repay it or to pay interest, whereas a bond contains an
express obligation to pay money, grain or other agricultural produce to
another (Sec. 2(5) and Art. 13),

BOND AND AGREEMENT : - Bond requires attestation by a witness.
It contains an express obligation to pay money or deliver grain etc. The
obligation to pay is chief covenant in Bond whereas in an Agreement,
breach of the contract is compensated in damages. However an
unattested bond should be treated as an agreement. (Sec. 2(5)).
BOND AND MORTGAGE : - Bond is a personal obligation to repay a
debt while mortgage is a creation of interest in specified property as
security for repayment of debt, or for performance of an engagement.

(Section 2(5) and Sec. 2(17)). Bond falls under Article 13 and Mortgage,
under Article 35.

BOND AND PRONOTE : - Pronote is a negotiable instrument while
Bond is not. Pronote is payable to order or bearer but bond is not so
payable. Bond requires attestation. In a pronote attestation is not
compulsory. Pronote contains an undertaking to pay money only. Bond
may contain an undertaking to deliver grain or other agricultural produce
also. (Secs. 2(5) and 2(22)). Duty in respect of Bond is payable under
Art. 13 of Sch. I-A. Duty on pronote is pay-able under Art. 49 of Sch. I
(Union List).

CANCELLATION AND REVOCATION : - Cancellation (Art. 15) is a
residuary article. It requires attestation. Cancellations not otherwise
provided for fall under this Article. Cancellations specially provided for
are Revocation of Settlement (Art 49B) and Revocation of Trust (Art
55B). Cancellations of Settlements and Trusts are called Revocations
CHEQUE AND BILL OF EXCHANGE : - Bill of Exchange is defined
in Section 2(2) of Stamp Act and Section 5 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act. It includes also a Hundi or any other docurmnt entitling or purporting
to entitle any person whether named therein or not to payment by any
other person of or to draw upon any other person for, any sum of money.
When a Bill of Exchange is drawn on a Banker, it is called cheque. It is
payable only on demand. (Section 2(7)).

CONVEYANCE AND COMPOSITION DEED : - In a conveyance
there is a direct transfer of property by the debtor to the creditors whereas
in a composition deed, the property of the debtor is conveyed to the
trustees for the benefit of the creditors. Duty on conveyance is payable
under Article 20 while duty on composition deed is payable under Article
19.

CONVEYANCE AND SALE : - See — Chapter 2 (S.No. 28 and 88)
on Definitions and meanings

CO-OWNERS (JOINT OWNERS) & CO-PARCENERS : - Persons
jointly owning property or tenants in common are called co-owners or
joint owners, eg. partners in a firm or persons who purchased or acquired
property jointly. Members of joint family owning _ properties in joint
are called co-parceners.

COPY AND DUPLICATE : - A duplicate is an exact reproduction of
the original containing the original signatures of parties and witnesses. A
copy also is an exact reproduction of the original, but does not contain
the original signatures of parties and witnesses. It is certified as a copy
by an authorised officer

DEBENTURE AND SHARE CERTIFICATE : - Debenture is an
instrument evidencing the debt due to the debenture holder by the
Company while a share certificate evidences the title of the holder to the
share in the company. A debenture holder is entitled to fixed rate of
interest while a holder of a share certificate is entitled to dividend which
is fluctuating
DECLARATION OF TRUST OR TRUST AND TRANSFER OF
TRUST : - Declaration of Trust — See Chapter 2 (S.No.107) on

management of trust property. It is an instrument chargeable under Article
55 A. Transfer of trust is an instrument whereby trust property is
transferred from one trustee or Board of trustees to another trustee or
Board of trustees or to the beneficiary. It is chargeable under Article
53(d). .
DULY STAMPED AND PROPERLY STAMPED : - Duly stamped is
applied to an instrument. It means that an instrument bears stamp of
required value and proper discription and that such stamp has been affixed
or impressed or used in accordance with the law for the time being in
force (Sec. 2(11).) When an instrument bears a stamp of proper value
but of improper description it is said to be not properly stamped rendering
the instrument as not duly stamped (Sec.37)
EARNEST MONEY AND PREMIUM :: - Earnest money is an amount
advanced in consideration of a contract which is adjustable in the final
settlement, Premium is a price paid or payable in lumpsum or instalment
by the lessee to the lessor in consideration of the lease (Sec. 105, T.P.
Act, 1882) It is neither adjustable in rent, nor repayable
ENGLISH MORTGAGE AND MORTGAGE BY CONDITIONAL
SALE : - English Mortgage is an ostensible (appearing to be real but not
real) sale. Mortgage by conditional sale is an ostensible sale. In an English
Mortgage the mortgagor transfers the property absolutely to the
Mortgagee subject to retransfer on repayment of the mortgage money.In
a mortgage by conditional sale the mortgagor ostensibly sells the property
to the mortgagee subject to the following conditions.
(a) on default of re-payment of the mortgage money by a certain date
the sale shall become absolute.
(b) onsuch repayment being made the sale shall become void.
(c) on such repayment being made the buyer shall retransfer the
property to the seller, (Sec. 58(c) and (e) T.P. Act, 1882)

EX-OFFICIO VENDOR AND LICENSED STAMP VENDOR : - The
Treasury Officer or such other officer of the Government as the CCRA
or Government may appoint shall be ex-officio Vendor of all descriptions
of Stamps in local depot. (Rule 27 of Rules for supply and distribution of

(BSO 65). Private persons are licensed by District Registrars, as licensing

licensed Stamp Vendors
FURTHER CHARGE AND FRESH MORTGAGE : - Some times the
same mortgagee advances further sums of money to the mortgagor on
the same security and conditions. The deed securing this further sum is
called a further charge. If however, the outstanding debt is merged with
the fresh advance and a deed is executed to secure the repayment of the
total debt, it is a fresh mortgage.

Duty on further charge is payable under Article 28 while fresh mortgage
is chargeable under Art. 35.
FAMILY ARRANGEMENT AND FAMILY SETTLEMENT : - Both
the terms apply to one and the same transaction. Family settlement is a
kind of compromise. When members of a family compromise their
disputes about family property or the property of a relation about the
inheritance of which there is a bonafide dispute between them, the
transaction is known as family settlement or family arrangement.

GENERAL POWER AND SPECIAL POWER : - A special agency
exists when there is an authority to do a single act, a general agency
exists when there is a delegation to do all acts connected with a particular
trade, business or employment etc.

A person who is authorised through an instrument to execute a particular
deed or sign a particular contract or to purchase a particular property or
merchandise etc. pertains to a single act and the person authorised is
called a special power of attorney agent. But when a person is authorised
to execute all deeds, sign all contracts or to purchase all goods required
ina particular business or employment etc., such an instrument is a general
power. Power given for consideration and authorising the Attorney to
sell any immpovable property falla under under Article 42 (e)

The general power falls under Article 42(c), (d), (f) and (g) while special
power falls under Article 42(a) & (b).

Gift and settlement : - See S.No.46 (Gift) and S.No.92 (Settlement) under
Chapter 2- Definitions and meanings

HYPOTHECATION AND PAWN OR PLEDGE : - Hypothecation is
mortgage of movable property without possession. Pawn or pledge is
mortgage of movable property with possession. The former is chargeable
under Art 6. if unattested and the latter under Art 7

INDEMNITY BOND AND SECURITY BOND : - Indemnity Bond is
a bond by which one party promises to save the other from the loss
caused to him by the conduct of the promisor or of any other person.
(Sec. 124 of Contract Act.) It falls under Article 30 whereas security
bond is one which is executed by way of security for due execution of an
office or to account for money or property received by virtue thereof or
executed by a surety to secure the due performance of a contract. It
falls under Article 48. ,

IMPOUNDING AND COMPOUNDING :- See Chapter No.2
(Definitions) S.No.49 on “Impounding” and S.No.27 on “Compounding”

A deficitly stamped document is impounded and deficit stamp duty and
penalty are collected. A document in respect of which any offence under
Stamp Act is committed need not necessarily be impounded as they fall
under violations under section 27. The parties concerned can be prosecuted
or the offence can be condoned (Compounded) on payment of composition
fee (Sec.70).

INSTRUMENT AND DOCUMENT : - Every writing containing
evidence or information is a document. All instruments are documents
but all documents are not instruments. Instrument includes a document
by which any right or liability is, or purports to be, created, transferred,
limited, extended, extinguished or recorded (Sec. 2(14). But in Stamp
Act, copies and affidavit which do not create etc., such rights are brought
within the purview of instruments for purpose of stamp duty.

LEASE OF USUFRUCT AND USUFRUCTUARY MORTGAGE : -
Ina lease of usufruct, there is a transfer of right to enjoy the usufruct of
the property in consideration of rent or lumpsum amount. The amount
paid is not debt and no security is created in the property.

In an usufructuary mortgage the mortgagor delivers possession of the
property to the mortgagee and authorises him to appropriate the usufruct
(profits) in satisfaction of the debt and interest. A security is created in
the property for the repayment of the debt. (Section 58(b) T.P. Act.1882)
Lease is chargeable under Article 31 while the usufructuary Mortgage is
chargeable under Art. 35(a)
Distinctions between Terms 231

36. LEASE FOR INDEFINITE PERIOD AND LEASE IN PERPETUITY
:- Where the period is not specified in a lease, it is a lease for indefinite
period chargeable under Article 31(a)(vi)(a). Where a lease is granted
permanently it is a lease in perpetuity chargeable also under
Art.31(a)(vi)(a).

37. LEASE FOR MONEY ADVANCED AND MORTGAGE WITH
POSSESSION : - In both the cases, a lumpsum is paid and possession of
property is given to the person who paid the amount. In a lease there is a
transfer of right to enjoy the property in consideration of the amount paid
whereas in MWP there is transfer of right in the property to secure the
repayment of the money advanced. The crucial test is creation of security
over the property. If security is created it is a mortgage otherwise it is a
lease (Secs.2(16) & 2(17)

Lease for money advanced is chargeable under Article 31 (a) (vi) (b)
and Mortgage with possession under Art. 35(a).

38. LEASE WITH ADVANCE AND LEASE FOR PREMIUM : - Advance
is the amount paid before or after arising of the liability to pay rent and is
adjustable in rent. When the lessee pays any rent before it falls due it is
advance. It does not fall under Art 31(c) requiring additional duty (vide
proceedings No.S5/7423/93, Dt.6-3-1999 of C&IGR.S.

Premium is the amount paid in lumpsum or in instalments and not
repayable. It is a price paid as consideration for the grant of lease. (Sec
105 T.P. Act,1882). The amount is paid in lumpsum or in instalments for
parting with the interest of the lessor (TP Act Sec. 105, AIR 1965
SC1871, AIR 1977 All 1979, IG’s Progs. S3/23775/83 dt 3-6-1991),

39. LEASE AND LICENSE: - A license differs from a lease in that under
a lease an interest in immovable property is transferred while no interest
is transferred under a license. A license is unlike a lease, generally
revocable and not assignable. It is revocable only under some special
circumstances (Sec. 60 of Easements Act.) Control and possession over
the property is the main criteria. If control is with the owner, it would be
a mere license, otherwise a lease. License is chargeable under Art. 6
(Agreement) while lease is chargeable under Art. 31

40. LOCAL DEPOT AND BRANCH DEPOT: - See. S.No.60 of
Chapter 2 - Definitations and Meanings

41. MORTGAGE AND CHARGE: - A mortgage is a transfer of an interest
in specified property while in a charge there is no such transfer but only
the creation of a right of payment out of certain property. (Sec. 58 and
100 of T-P. Act, 1882), For the purpose of Stamp Act both are chargeable
as Mortgage under Article 35
232 Distinctions between Terms

42, MORTGAGE WITH POSSESSION AND USUFRUCTUARY
MORTGAGE : - Both are chargeable under Art. 35(a). In MWP the
mortgagee enjoys the property in lieu of interest and retransfers the
property on repayment of the mortgage money while in usufructuary
mortgage he enjoys the property in lieu of principal and interest and
retransfers it after the stipulated period.

43. MORTGAGE AND SECURITY MORTGAGE : - Mortgage is a general
provision and Security Mortgage is a special provision. When a person
creates a right in favour of another person in specified property to secure
the repayment of debt or for the performance of an engagement it is
chargeable as Mortgage under Art. 35. But when such a mortgage is
executed for any of the 3 specific purposes mentioned in Article 48 it is
chargeable as Security Bond / Security mortgage under the said Article

44, MINING LEASE BY GOVERNMENT AND MINING LEASE BY
A PRIVATE PARTY : - In a mining lease, royalty or a share of the
produce is reserved, the value of rent for the purpose of stamp duty shall
be calculated as under:

If Government is lessor, the Collector shall estimate the royalty payable
in a year. If private party is the lessor the value shall be taken as Rs.
20.000/- p.a. (Sec. 26).

45. _MORTIGAGE WITH POSSESSION AND LEASE FOR PREMIUM
:- Ina MWP a security is created over the property for the repayment of
the debt (mortgage money). The mortgagee retains possession of the
mortgaged property until the repayment of the debt. (Sec. 58 T.P.
Act.1882) It is chargeable under Art. 35(a).

Lease for Premium evidences transfer of property by the lessor for
enjoyment of the lessee for a specified period in consideration of the
price viz premium. It is chargeable under Art. 31 (b)

46. PARTITION AND DISSOLUTION OF PARTNERSHIP : - Partition
is an instrument whereby the co-owners or co-parceners of property
divide or agree to divide the joint property in severalty (Section 2(15).
Dissolution of partnership is a deed whereby the partners agree to put an
end to the partnership. The arrangements consequent on such dissolution
may also involve partition of the assets among the partners in which case
it is to be treated as dissolution of partnership and partition chargeable
wuu the higher duty under Sec. 6.

47. PARTITION AND FAMILY SETTLEMENT : - When co-parceners
of joint property divide it into severalty, the instrument recording it is
called a partition deed (Sec. 2(15). The duty is payable on the value of
separated share (vide S.No.91 in Chapter 2) under Art. 40, when the

PERFORATION AND CANCELLATION : - When a "Proper Officer"
referred to in Stamp Rule 9 affixes impressed labels on unexecuted
documents he defaces them in two ways namely perforation with a
perforating machine or cancellation with his signature or initials. (Rule
11). This process is called perforation or cancellation respectively

POWER OF ATTORNEY AND TRUST : - In a Power of Attorney
(Art. 42) the Agent acts for and in the name of the principal in respect of
the specific matters mentioned in the power. In a trust, the trustee
administers the trust property for the benefit of the beneficiary. (Article
55-A.)

PREMIUM AND ADVANCE : - Vide lease with Advance and Lease
for Premium (S.No.38 supra)

PREMIUM AND RENT : - When the interest of the lessor is parted
with for a price, the price paid in lumsum or instalemnts for obtaining the

Periodical payments made for the continous enjoyment of the benefits
under the lease is called Rent. (Section 105 of the T.P.Act, 1882 & LG.
R&S Proceedings No.S3/23775/83, dt.3.6.1991)

PROVISO (a) TO SECTION 35 AND SEC. 40(i)(b) : - When an
insufficiently stamped document is produced in evidence in a Court, the
Court, shall impound it and admit it in evidence only if the deficit duty and
penalty equal to ten times the deficit duty subject to a minimum of Rs.
15/- are paid (vide Proviso (a) Section 35)

If the party wants the court to admit the insufficient stamped document
in evidence, the court has to levy the deficit stamp duty and penalty equal
to 10 times. If however, the party wants the court to send the insufficiently
stamped documents to the Collector for adjudication, the Court has no
other option except to comply with the request.

When the Collector impounds a deficitly stamped document or receives
such a document under section 38(2) he shall levy the deficit duty anda
penalty of Rs. 5/- or an amount not exceeding ten times the deficit duty
whether it exceeds or falls short of Rs. 5/-

PROSPECTING LICENCE AND MINING LEASE : - See ‘Lease
and Licence’ (S.Nos.56 & 59 - Chapter 2) In a prospecting licence, the
licensee is authorised to prospect for minerals on a specified land. He is
not given exclusive possession of the land. He can enter it only for the
specific purpose of prospecting. Whereas in a mining lease, the lessee is
Distinctions between Terms

54.

given exclusive possession of the land to excavate and take away the
minerals on payment of Royalty or dead rent in addition to ground rent
and taxes etc. A prospecting licence is chargeable as an agreement under
Article 6-A while mining lease is chargeable under Art. 31.
PRONOTE AND BILL OF EXCHANGE :: - Both are negotiable
instruments. The broad distinction between the two is that in the former,
the executant promises to pay himself, while in the latter, he directs a
third person to pay. Bill of Exchange falls under Article 13 of schedule 1
and Pronote under Art. 49 of Sch-l.

RECEIPT AND RELEASE : - A receipt merely acknowledges the
receipt of money in satisfaction of debt etc., whereas Release is an
instrument whereby a right or claim is relinquished, eg. if the Mortgagee
merely acknowledges receipt of principal or interest or both it is a receipt,
whereas if words, denoting release of mortgage right are used it becomes
a Release chargeable under Art. 46.

A receipt is chargeable under Article 53, Schedule — I while Release
of mortgage right is chargeable under Article 46, SchedulelA.
However in the case of releases of Mortgage right the ILG.R &S
has clarified such documentsare to be treated on par with
reconveyance of mortgaged proverty under Art.45 leviable with the
maximum stamp of Rs.50/- (vide IG R & S progs. No. S1/15659/88
dt 11-10-1988 and $3/24952/95 dt 11-10-1995)

RECEIPT AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF DEBT : - An
acknowledgement of debt is one executed in order to supply evidence of
already existing debt while in contrast a receipt is executed in token of
acknowledgement of satisfaction of debt or acknowledgement of receipt
of money advanced. Acknowledgement of debt is chargeable under Art.
1 of Schedule 1A while Receipt is chargeable under Art. 53 of Sch.-I.
RECTIFICATION DEED AND RATIFICATION DEED : - A document
by which a clerical error in a previously executed instrument is rectified
not creating transfer, limit any right or liability is a rectification deed
requiring no stamp duty (vide Note under Sec. 2(14)) A document by
which a party ratifies a previously executed instrument for no fresh
consideration is a Ratification deed (supplemental deed) chargeable
with a duty of Rs.5/- under Sec.4 which applies to Sale, Mortgage
~nd Settlement deeds only.

RELEASE AND CONVEYANCE : - Release is an instrument whereby
a co-owner or a person having already a limited interest in property
relinquishes his claim in favour of all the remaining co-owners. When
such a release is in favour of only some of the remaining co-owners and
Distinctions between Terms 235

59.

61.

62.

not in favour of all co-owners or when property is transferred in favour
of a person not having pre-existing right in the property it amounts to a
conveyance.

RULES 6(i} AND 7(1) : - Rule 6(1) lays down when Non-Judicial
Stamp papers can be used while Rule 7(1) says how they should be
used.

Rule 6(1) lays down that documents other than pronotes and Bills of
Exchange shall be written on Non Judicial Stamp papers on which the
word ‘Hundi’ was not engraved when they are not stamped with adhesive
labels or special adhesive stamps. According to Rule 7(1) when two or
more sheets are used for a document, a portion of the instrument should
be written on each sheet.

RELEASE AND RATIFICATION : - A Ratification is a supplemental
deed in respect of documents falling under Section 4 chargeable with a
fixed duty of Rs. 5/-. It ratifies a previously execlited document by a
necessary party. It has no separate consideration.But a Release is
an independent instrument falling under Art. 46. The words ‘Release or
relinguish’ convey the same meaning and it can have separate
consideration.

RELEASE AND PARTITION : - Partition is division of joint property
of co-owners or coparceners into severalty. (Sec. 2(15). It is a sort of
mutual release by which each party in lieu of share of property allotted to
him releases his joint right over the shares that are allotted to the other
parties. A partition is binding on all the parties. It falls under Art. 40.

A release (Art. 46) is a one sided document executed by one or more
of the co-owners or coparceners in favour of all the remaining co-owners
or coparceners in consideration of cash or a part of the joint property. If
the consideration is a part of joint family asscts and if all the co-owners
or coparceners execute the document it becomes a partition.

RELEASE AND RECONVEYANCE OF MORTGAGED
PROPERTY : - In a Release, mortgagee under a simple mortgage
relinquishes his mortgage right in the mortgaged property on repayment
of the mortgage money. It does not involve transfer of possession of the
property but only relinquishment of the right. Whereas in the case of
mortgage with possession or English mortgage the mortgagee reconveys
the mortgaged property to the mortgagor on repayment of the debt. It
involves transfer of possession of the property. Release falls under Art.
46 while reconveyance falls under Art. 45. However the IG R & S, in his
progs. No S1/15659/88 dt 11-10-1988 and S3/24952/95 dt 11-10-1995
clarified that release of mortage right be treated on par with reconveyance

of mortgaged property under Art 45. chargeable with a maxmimum duty
of Rs.50/-

RENT AND PREMIUM : - Vide S.51 supra

SECTION 4 AND SECTION 6: - Sec. 4 deals with a single transaction
being completed through several instruments provided the full duty should
have been paid on the principal deed. Each supplemental deed is
chargeable with a fixed duty of Rs. 5/-. This section applies, to sales,
mortgages and settlements deeds only.

Sec. 6 deals with an instrument coming under several descriptions in

Schedules | or 1A. The duty payable is the highest of the duties payable
under each description.
SECTION 5 AND SECTION 6 : - Section 5 relates to a document
which contains several distinct matters capable of being carried out
through different documents. The distinct matters may be of-(a) same
category or of (b) different categories, eg. (a) Sale of different plots of
lands to different purchasers for separate considerations, agreement of
sale cum-GPA, development agreement -cum-GPA and Mortgage by
conditional sale. The duty chargeable is the aggregate of the duties
chargeable on each matter.

Sec. 6 deals with instrument containing a single matter but coming
under several descriptions of the Schedule | or 1A, as the case may be
eg. Sale with indemnity, dissolution of partnership and partition of the
assets between the partners, trust and settlement etc. The duty chargeable
is the highest of the duties chargeable under each description.
SECTION 5 AND SECTION 14 : - Section 5 deals with instrument
relating to several distinct matters and shall be chargeable with the
aggregate of the duties chargeable on such distinct matters contained in
the document.

Section 14 prohibits drawing up another instrument chargeable with
duty on an already executed instrument. According to Sec.14, no second
instrument whether executed or not chargeable with duty shall be written
on stamped paper on which an instrument was already executed.
Endorsment referred to in the proviso under the section are exempted
from this provision namely transfer of the rights created by the instrument
and acknowledgement of the receipt of money or goods, the payment or
delivery of which secured by the instrument.

SECTION 31 AND SECTION 41 : - Application under Sec. 31 is made
to the Collector for the determination of the Stamp duty payable on an
instrument, whether executed or not when the party is in doubt about the
Distinctions between Terms 237

68.

69.

70.

duty payable. It can be made at any time but a certificate under Sec. 32
can be added only if the document is presented within one month from
date of execution if executed in India or within 3 months if executed out
of India from the date of receipt in India. Application under Sec. 41 can
be made to the Collector within one year from the date of execution. The
applicant must satisfy the Collector that the omission to stamp the
document duly, was occasioned by accident, mistake or urgent necessity
and he must voluntarily produce the document with an offer to pay the
proper duty or deficit duty as the case may be.

SECTION 33 AND SECTION 41 : - Sec. 33 relates to deficitly or
insufficiently stamped documents produced before court or a public officer
other than a police official, in evidence or in the discharge of their
respective duties. The court or the officer shall impound such document.

Sec. 41 deals with deficitly or insufficiently stamped documents
voluntarily produced before the Collector along with an application with
an offer to pay the deficit duty. Penalty is also leviable on documents
coming under Sec. 33. but no penalty is leviable on documents dealt with
under Sec. 41 if they are produced within one year from date of execution
and if the Colector is satisfied that the omission to duly stamp the document
was occasioned by accident, mistake or urgent necessity.

Sec. 33 applies to all documents. But Sec. 41 does not apply to
documents chargeable with duty not exceeding 40 paise, or a Bill of
Exchange or a pronote.

SECTION 40 AND SECTION 41 : - Sec. 40 deals with levy of deficit
duty and penalty on documents impounded by Collector under Sec. 33 or
received by him under Sec. 38(2). The Collector levies the deficit duty
and penalty not exceeding ten times the deficit duty subject to a minimum
of Rs.5/-.

Sec. 41 deals with deficitly or insufficiently stamped documents
voluntarily produced by the party to the Collector along with an application
within one year from date of its execution with an offer to pay the deficit
duty. The Collector does not levy any penalty if he is satisfied that the
omission to duly stamp the document was occasioned by accident, mistake
or urgent necessity.

SECTION 70(1) AND 70(2) : - Sec. 70(1) empowers the Collector or
the authorized officer under the section to sanction prosecution for
offences under the Stamp Act while Sec. 70(2) empowers the Collector
or the authorised officer to stay such prosecution or compound such
offences.

SCHEDULE-I AND SCHEDULE I-A : - Schedule-I to the Stamp Act
applies in its entirety to all the centrally administered areas and such
other states who have adopted schedule | without enacting their own
(i.e., Schedule 1A). The rates of duty contained in it in respect of the
following documents apply to entire India except Jammu and Kashmir.
(1) Bill of Exchange, (2) Bill of Lading, (3) Letter of Credit, (4) Debentures,
(5) Pronote, (6) Proxy, (7) Policy of Insurance, (8) Transfer of Shares,
(9) Receipts.(Union List)

Schedule I-A is enacted separately if so required by each state and applies
to the instruments executed in the respective States or received in them
and relating to any property situated in them or to any matter or thing to
be done in them. (Proviso under Sec.3.)

SALE AND EXCHANGE : - Sale is a transfer of property in exchange

. for a price paid or promised (Sec. 54 T.P. Act 1882) while exchange is

the exchange of ownership of one thing for that of another neither thing
nor both things being money only (Sec. 118 T.P. Act 1882). When property
is exchanged for money alone it is sale. When it is exchanged for any
thing other than money alone, it is Exchange, Sale falls under Art. 47-A
and Exchange under Art. 27.

SIMPLE MORTGAGE AND MORTGAGE BY DEPOSIT OF TITLE
DEEDS : - Simple mortgage creates an interest in immovable property
while Mortgage by deposit of title deeds which also is called "equitable
mortgage" creates an interest in the title deeds deposited. The latter applies
only to notified towns (vide Sec. 58(f), T.P. Act 1882.)

Simple mortgage is chargeable under Art. 35 while Mortgage by deposit
of title deeds is chargeable under Art. 7.

SPECIAL POWER OF ATTORNEY AND PROXY : - A Special power
of Attorney as described in Art. 42 of Schedule | A and Sec. 2(21) differs
from a proxy mentioned in Art. 52 of Schedule-I in that the former is a
general provision and the latter is a special provision. Proxy authorises
the agent to vote on behalf of principal in the specified meetings while
the Power of Attorney empowers the Agent to act for and in the name
of the principal in matters other than those falling under the Article
“Proxy”.

SUBLEASE, UNDER LEASE AND USUFRUCTUARY
MORTGAGE : - In both the cases the entire amount is paid in advance.
In usufructuary mortgage, the amount partakes the nature of debt while
in lease it is regarded as advance of rent. In former case there is security
Distinctions between Terms 239

over the property for debt advanced. The former is chargeable under
Article 35(a) and the latter under Article 31 (b).

SURRENDER OF LEASE AND TRANSFER OR ASSIGNMENT OF
LEASE : - Surrender is yielding up of the right to a person, who has the
immediate estate in reversion. Surrender of unexpired portion of the
tenancy right in favour of the lessor is surrender of lease chargeable
under Art. 52 while transfer or assignment of lease is the conveyance of
lessees whole right in the lease to the transferee or assignee, a third
party, chargeable under Art. 54.

TRANSFER OF TRUST PROPERTY FROM TRUSTEE TO
BENEFICIARY AND RELEASE OF BENAMI RIGHT : - Release
of Benami right by the Benamidar in favour of the real purchaser was
previously classified as Release. With the amendment of Art. 46 as
46A, 46B and 46C with effect from 16-8-1986 (Act No.17/1986)
both were ordered to be classified as release of Benami right
under Article 46 (b). Transfer of Trust property from trustee to
beneficiary (Art.53(d)) applies only when the properties were originally
held under trust and transferred by the trustee to the beneficiary.

TRANSFER OF LEASE AND SUBLEASE OR UNDERLEASE : -
An underlease is a grant by a lessee to another called underlessee or
sublessee of a part, or whole of his interest under the original lease,
reserving to himself, a reversion. It falls under Art. 31.

A transfer of lease, on the other hand conveys the lessee’s whole interest
to the transferee including the right to sue or be sued upon the covenants
in the original lease. It falls under Article 54.

TRUST AND SETTLEMENT : - For definition of the term "Trust" —
(See chapter-2 S.No. 107) A deed of trust is chargeable as a settlement
if there was no prior disposition of the property in favour of the beneficiary.
Settlement (Chapter-2 S.No 92) is chargeable under Art. 49 while Trust
deed is chargeable under Article 55A.

USUFRUCTUARY MORTGAGE AND LEASE FOR LUMPSUM
PAID IN ADVANCE :- In both the cases the entire amount is paid in
advance, In usufructuary mortgage, the amount partakes the nature of
debt while in lease it is regarded as advance of rent. In former case
there is security over the property for debt advanced. The former is
chargeable under Article 35(a) and the latter under Article 31 (b).

WILL AND CODICIL : - Will is a legal declaration of the intention of
the testator with respect to his property which he desires to be carried
240 , Distinctions between Terms
into effect after his death. {Sec. 52(b) of Indian Succession Act}. Codicil
is a supplement to the will intended to make modifications to the already
executed will. Both are testamentary documents, exempt from payment
of stamp duty.

82. WILL AND SETTLEMENT :- Will is a testamentary document which
comes into operation only after the death of the testator and the last will
alone prevails. The disposition of property can be in any body’s favour
and for any purpose. It requires no starnp duty.

Settlement is a non-testamentary disposition of property in consideration
of marriage or for distribution of property in favour of relatives or
dependants or for religious or charitable purpose Sec. 2(24). It should be _
stamped under Art. 49, of Sch. I-A.

What are the options by which stamp duty can be paid otherwise
than by stamps?

The party may draft the document on unstamped paper
and take it to the “Proper Officer” before execution to affix requeired
value of special Adhesive labels under Rule 9 by paying cash.

The party may apply to the Collector under Sec.31and pay in cash the
Stamp duty determined by the Collector and get the certificate under
Sec. 32 added on the document unstamped if it is within one month from
the date of execution of the document.

The party may execute the document on unstamped paper and apply
within one year form the date of execution, to the Collector under Sec.
41 with an offer to pay the duty.(vide Note 2 under Sec.10.APSM)

In the case of executed instruments presented within 4 months from the
date of execution or first execution, Sec.10A permits payment of duty in
cash or by way of Bank Demand Draft or by Pay Order.

A document written on both sides of Non-Judicial Stamp paper
was presented for registration .

There is no objection to write on the reverse side of the stamp paper
though it is desirable to write on the face of the Stamp paper alone.
(Note 2 under Sec. 13.APSM)

A person fails to cancel an adhesive Stamp

Any instrument bearing an adhesive Stamp which has not been cancelled
sO as to prevent its use again, shall, sofar as such stamp is concerned, be
deemed to be deficitly stamped. (Section 12(2).)

The Executant of a document noticing deficit duty, attaches a blank
Stamp paper of the value of deficit, signed by him and presents it
for registration before a Sub-Registrar
Procedure

8.

The action of the executant is irregular. The document has to be treated
as deficitly stamped to the extent of the value of the stamp paper attached
and the document is to be impounded, The stamp duty should be paid
before or at the time of execution. So it is irregular to attach the Stamp
paper after execution. (Sec. 17.). Further a substantial part of the
instrument should be written on each Stamp paper used for it. (Vide
Sec. 13 and Rule 7(1.) Hence the procedure adopted by the party is
irregular.(Vide Note 4 under Sec. 13 on P.32 A.P.S.M./ BPRT. 5693,
dated 8.12.1944.)

Sale deed for Rs. 1,000/- executed out of India was brought to
Collector for stamping under Sec. 18 with a request that it might
be stamped with a Stamp of Rs. 5/-

Under Sec. 18, the Collector is bound to affix such Stamps as may be
required by the party and it is not within his province to tender any advice
as to the amount of duty payable on the deed. So the document should
be stamped with Rs. 5/- only as requested by the applicant (Vide Note 1,
under Sec. 18 APSM = P.33)

An instrument executed out of India is brought to the Collector
after expiry of 3 months from the date of its receipt in India

been occasioned by accident, mistake or urgent necessity, proceed under
Secs. 41 & 42 if it is within the period of one year from the date of
execution. (Vide Note 2 under Section (18)APSM. Otherwise it should
be impounded under Sec. 33 and deal with it under Sees. 40 & 42

A party is in doubt about the Stamp duty payable
or

What is the procedure for ascertaining and payment of correct
duty in respect of an executed document.

The party may make an application to the District Collector or any other
officer appointed as Collector under Sec.31 of the Act along with the
document and a copy of it for his authoritative opinion as to the Stamp
Duty payable on the document. The Collector shall coltect adjudication
fee not exceeding Rs. 15/ - and not less than Rs. 5/- and may call for
additional information if any or an affidavit to prove that all the facts and
circumstances affecting the chargeability of the instrument have been
truly and fully setforth in the document. The Collector will then determine
the duty. If the -document is already duly stamped or is not chargeable
with duty, the Collector shall add a certificate to that effect on the
document. If the proper duty determined or deficit portion thereof is paid
he shall (if the document brought to him is writhin one month from the
date of execution) certify that the full duty with which it was chargeable
was paid. If, however, the party does not pay the duty, or if the case falls
under proviso (a)(b) and (c) to Sec. 32, the Collector should not add the
certificate. He shall return the document with his opinion alone. (Vide
Sec, 31 &. 32.)

He cannot impound the document as he becomes functus officio as
soon as he determined the stamp duty (Note 3 under Section 32 APSM)

When an unstamped receipt is detected in audit, the audit officer may
require that it may be substituted by a duly stamped receipt (Vide Sec.
34.). .

21. An unstamped receipt is presented in audit to a public officer in
the discharge of his duties
The procedure is the same as above

22. An unstamped receipt is produced in evidence
An unstamped receipt produced in evidence can be admitted in evidence
on payment of penalty of Rs. 3/- by the person tendering it (Sec.35 (b)).
No duty is leviable in addition to the fine and no endorsement is necessary
CILR 24 ALL 1902, 374 Note 12 under section 35 (page 52 APSM))
All other unstamped receipts produced to a person in charge of a
public office in the discharge of his duties should bé permanently
impounded and sent to the Collector as they cannot be validated (vide
Sec. 40). The Collector will preserve them for 12 years from date of
their execution and then destroy. them (Vide rules 22 and 23 on PP 344
& 345 Of A.P.S.M)

23. An unstamped pronote is produced before a Collector in an
enquiry
Unstamped pronote cannot be validated under Sec. 35 or 40 and 42.
They should be peranently impounded and destroyed after 12 years from
date of its execution. The Collector will preserve them for 12 years from
the date of its execution and then distroy them. (Vide. P 344 & 345 of
APS.M.)

24. Certified copy of a deficitly stamped document is produced before
a Public Officer.
There is no provision to levy deficit duty and penalty on certified copy of
an instrument not duly stamped, which is not actually produced. (Note 4
under Section 35). Deficit duty and penalty cannot be levied on the basis
of the certified copy.

Indicate the procedure under Sec. 41 and 42 when a document
dt. 26.3.2006 styled as.a release for Rs. 1,000/- presented for

attracting Sec. 47-A of the Act.

When a release is treated as conveyance on sale it attracts Sec. 47-A
which says that the duty is payable on consideration or market value of
the property whichever is higher. In this case it is presumed that the
consideration is Rs. 1,000/- and Market Value of the property dealtwith
declared is Rs. 6,000/-. The party may be given an opportunity to get it
validated under Secs. 41 and 42, as the Sub-Registrar is empowered to
act as Collector under Sec. 41 and he may himself Collect the deficit
duty and certify it under Sec. 42. If the party is not willing to apply under
Sec. 41, a report should be sent under Sec. 47-A to the District Registrar
who is appointed as collector under Sec. 47A.

What is the procedure when Stamps are found damaged in Stock?
Stamps found damaged in stock shall be destroyed by or under the orders
of the Collector or by the Inspector General of R & S as the case may be
and their value written off the accounts upto Rs. 300/-. If the value
exceeds Rs, 300/- the sanction of the CCRA shall be obtained.

Comments on Procedure

"Sec. or Section" quoted herein relates to section of the Indian Stamp
Act, 1999

"Rule" quoted herein relates to the Indian Stamp Rules, 1925

" CCRA" denotes Chief Controlling Revenue Authority

" Art. or Article" quoted herein relates to Schedule 1A to the unless
otherwise stated

A Sub-Judge issued a direction to a Sub-Registrar to register a
Security Bond produced before him in evidence in Judicial
Preceeting to collect fees and stamp duty under Art. 48(b)
though it falls under Art. 35(b).

The Sub-Judge has no authority for issue of such direction to the Sub-
Registrar to treat a document as falling under a particular Article. The
High Court has issued instructions to all the subordinate courts not to
issue such directions.

The Sub-Registrar registered a sale deed for Rs.10,000/- on
Judicial Stamps of Rs. 800/- and returned the same to the party .

The document should have been treated as not duly stamped (Sec. 2)(1)
and impounded. If the stamp of Rs. 800/-was sufficient, only the duty
with which the document is chargeable should be collected without penalty
(Sec. 37). The Collector can exercise the powers of remitting further
payment of duty where a document bears a stamp of the proper amount
but of improper description if he is satisfied that the same has been used
solely because of the failure in procuring a stamp of the proper amount
and description.

In a lease deed by Government in favour of a private party
Government agreed to bear the duty and the document was drawn
up on.white paper.

or

Government sold one of its buildings in Hyderabad to a private
party and agreed to bear the Stamp duty payable on the document.
The sale deed was unstamped.

Though the lessee under the lease and the Vendee under the sale have to
pay the stamp duty according to the provisions of Sec-29, there is nothing
illegal in government undertaking to bear the duty and then claiming
exemption under Proviso (1) to Section 3 if Government is a party to the
document and agreed to bear stamp duty (Note 14 under Sec-3).
However Surcharge on Stamp Duty is payable in respect of the
sale deed.

A Sub-Registrar accepts for registration an unstamped receipt
for money, subsequently causes a stamp to be affixed to it and
registers the document.

The action of the Sub Registrar is contrary to Sec. 17. according to
which the stamp duty has to be paid before or at the time of execution of
instrument. He should have permanently impounded it as it cannot be
validated under Sec. 40 & 42.

On being informed that a duly executed document is insufficiently
stamped, the executant purchased stamps of required value,
cancelled them and attached them to the document.

Stamp duty should be paid before or at the time of execution (Vide Sec.
17.) When two or more stamp papers are used to make up an instrument,
a portion of the instrumeiit should be written on each such paper (Rule
7.) The procedure adopted contravenes both the provisions of the Stamp
Act.

6.

A document contains 10 sheets of stamp papers.7 Sheets were
used for writing and 3 remaining sheets were crossed and affixed
with the signatures of the executant. A note on page 7 indicated
that all sheets constitute the document. The Sub-Registrar
registered the document as duly stamped.

In view of the note on the 7th sheet that all the ten sheets form part of
the document, the Allahabad High Court held in a similar case that the
document vs duly stamped. {AIR 1955 ALL 634 (DB).}

A Document requiring a stamp duty of Rs.30/- was drawn on stamp
paper of Rs.25/- and presented to Sub-Register for Registration.
The Sub-Registrar returned the document saying that it required
a duty of Rs.30/-. The parties purchased another stamp worth
Rs.5/- added it to the document, drew a line across it, added
thereon their signatures as well as those of witnesses and the
scribe. The Sub-Registrar then accepted the document and
registered it (vide also S.No14 below).

(i) | Whenadeficitly stamped document is presented to a Sub-Registrar,
he should have impounded it under Sec. 33. His action in returning

it was oong

(ii) Document should be stamped before or at the time of execution.
Vide Sec. 17. Affixing of Stamp after execution was invalid. (Note
4 under Sec. 13).

ii) When/two or more sheets are used for a document a portion of
such document should be written on each sheet. The signature of
parties and attesting witnesses do not form a part of the document.
(Rule 7(1) and Note 2 there under and Sec.13}. Hence the
document is deemed as deficitly stamped even after the insertion
of additional Stamp paper of Rs. 5/-. The Sub-Registrar should

have impounded it.

A Sub-Registrar refused to accept a document for registration as
the matter was written on both sides of the Stamp Papers.

Neither Sec. 13 nor Rule 7 prohibits the writing of the document on both
sides of the Stamp paper (vide Note 2 under Sec. 13 and Note 2 under
Rule 7). Hence the action of the Sub-Registrar was wrong.

11. What are the material alterations in an instrument that render a

new stamp necessary?

Following are the material alternations.

Alterations of (1) time of payment, (2) date of payment, (3) sum payable,
(4) rate of interest, (5) statement of consideration, (6) names of parties,
(7) number of Bank note, (8) Alteration of words “or order”, (9) transfer
of shares, (10) marriage settlement (11) area mentioned and (12) names
of witnesses (See 14 read with Sec. 15)

12. An insufficiently stamped document was presented to Sub-
Registrar for registration. He told the party that it was deficitly
stamped by Rs.5/- The party took back the document, inserted
stamp paper of Rs, 5, scored out two lines in the previous sheet,
added some matter on the sheet inserted, and presented to the
Sub-Registrar. The Sub-Registrar feeling doubtful, sent the
document to the Registrar who treated it as not duly stamped,
levied the entire stamp duty with which it is chargeable and
certified to that effect.

The treatment of the document as not duly stamped and impounding of
the document by the Registrar is correct (Sec. 14) but the Registrar
should have treated the document as deficitly stamped by Rs. 5/- only
and adjudicated the document accordingly.

An instrument executed in India on 10-3-2006 was brought to
the Collector for adjudication on 16.4.2006. He refused to
adjudicate it on the ground that it was brought to him after one
month from date of execution. He impounded it and levied proper
stamp duty and penalty under Sec. 40.

There is no time limit for giving opinion under Sec. 31. The time limit of
one month is only for adding certificate under Sec. 32. Documents filed
for adjudication should not be impounded as the Collector becomes functus
officio after determining the duty. (Note 3 under Sec. 32 P.46 APSM).

A District Registrar adjudicated the document under Sec.31 as
to the levy of stamp duty and ordered for the recovery of the
same under Sec. 48 when he found no scope of realising the same.

As the adjudication was made under Sec. 31, the procedure was incorrect.
The District Registrar becomes functus officio after determination of
the duty (Note 3 under Sec. 32 P.46 APSM)

A Settlement deed relating to property in Guntur District was
executed at Hyderabad and presented before the Collector
Krishna district for adjudication under Sec. 31. The Collector
refused to determine the stamp duty on the ground that he had
no jurisdiction.

There is no objection to the presentation and adjudication of documents
under Sec. 31 ina district different from that in which they were executed
or the property concerned was situated (vide Note 2 under Sec. 31.)
Also any person can apply for adjudication. It is not necessary that the
party to the document alone should apply. But by an Administrative order
the District Registrars have been instructed in I.G.RS proceedings No.
$4/27926/85 dated. 3-1-1986 to entertain applications for adjudication
under sec. 31 in respect of instruments when the property concerned is
situate only in their respective districts.

An insufficiently stamped sale deed was impounded by a Sub-

An insufficiently stamped mortgage deed was presented for
registration by the claimant for compulsory registration. The Sub-
Registrar impounded it. When the claimant failed to pay the deficit
duty and penalty the District Registrar collected them by coercive
process from the Claimant and also sanctioned prosecution of
the claimant on the ground that he abetted the execution of
insufficiently stamped document.

In the case of mortgage deed, the Stamp duty is to be borne by the
Mortgagor (vide Sec. 29). Hence the deficit duty and penalty can be
recovered by coercive process only from the mortgagor but not the
claimant(mortgagee), unless he is bound by an agreement (Vide Note-I
under Sec. 48.). Further, since deficit duty and penalty were paid,
prosecution need not be launched unless it appears to the Collector that
the offence was committed with an intention of evading payment of the
proper duty (vide Proviso to Sec.43 and Note-1 thereunder.(Page 60 of
A.P.S.M.)

For a sale certificate of Rs. 2,000/- the party was directed by the
Court to produce a Stamp of the value of Rs. 50/-. After execution
the court found it insufficiently stamped and impounded it. The
party contested that the levy of penalty was not justifiable as he
produced the stamp as required by the Court. The Collector
accepted the contention and levied only deficit duty.

Even in such cases, the penalty should be levied from the party in the
first instance, but it can be refunded later under Sec. 45(1) — (vide Note
5 under Sec. 40 Page 56 of A.P.S.M.) by making an application in
writing to the CCRA within one year from the date of payment.

Inspection is administrative act. The case.does not fall under Sec. 60 as
it does not attract section. 35. It has to be taken as an administrative
reference as the session court is subordinate to the High Court.

78 ‘A’ purchased certain property for Rs. 10,000/- and settled the

The Registration of the document by the Sub-Registrar is correct. As

80 The District Registrar, Hyderabad compounded an offence of

The compounding fee levied by a Collector is remitted partly by
the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority on appeal.

There is no provision in the Stamp-Law empowering the Chief Controlling
Revenue Authority or any other authority to remit whole or a part of the
compounding fec. Compounding fee is the one levied with the consent of
the party. In such cases the question of appeal does not arise. If the
Collector fixed the compounding fee unilaterally it was irregular.

A Deed of Exchange drawn up in Urdu was presented before the

An exchange deed in Urdu was filed before the District Treasury

if the document is in any oriental language recognised in the Taluk. As
Urdu is one of the languages recognised in Khammam, filing of translation
into English was unnecessary.

A District Registrar complied straight away with request of a Stamp

There is no provision in the Rules for effecting change in place of business

A licensed Stamp Vendor made incorrect endorsement on Stamp

The Stamp Vendors are strictly prohibited from altering endorsemcnts

A document engrossed on stamp paper which did not contain the
Stamp Vendor’s endorsements was impounded by the Sub-
Registrar.

The procedure of the Sub-Registrar was correct (Vide Rule 3(iv)
G.O.Ms.No. 568, Revenue, dated 12.6.1969.

A document was engrosed on three stamps and on one of them
the Stamps Vendor omitted to add his signature. The Sub-
Registrar refused to accept the document for registration.

According to Rule 3(iv) of the Indian Stamps Rules 1925 the stamp paper
must bear the endorsements of Stamp Vendors prescribed under the
rules made under Sec. 74. According to Rule 39(viii) of the rules the
Stamp Vendor should affix his signature on each stamp paper sold by
him as part of the endorsements. Omission to add the signature amounts
to contravention of the said rules rendering the document not duly stamped
(vide Sec. 2(11).

The Sub-Registrar should have impounded the document under Sec. 33.
and reported the lapse of the stamp vendor to the Dist.Registrar who is
the licensing authority.

(i) ADHESIVE LABELS
Mention classes of documents which may be stamped with
adhesive stamps?

The following documents may be stamped with adhesive stamps
(Sec. 11):

(a) Instruments chargeable with duty exceeding? 20 paise except parts
of Bills of exchange payable otherwise than on demand and drawn
in sets.

(b) Bills of exchange and Pronotes drawn or made out of India.
(c) Entry as advocate, vakil or attorney on the roll of High Court
(d) Notarial Acts and

(e) Transfers of shares by endorsement in any incorporated company
or other body corporate and

the following documents also may be stamped with adhesive stamps

(Rule 13).

(f) Bills of Exchange payable otherwise than on demand and drawn in
sets when the amount of duty does not exceed 20 paise for each
part of the set.

(g) Transfer of debentures of public companies and associations.

(h) Copies of maps and plans, printed copies and copies or extract
from registers given on printed forms.

(i) Instruments falling under Arts. 5(a) and (b) and 43 of (Schedule I-
A (Arts. 5(a) and (b) and 38 of Sch.1A)

@) Instruments chargeable under Art. 47 Schedule I.

(k) _ Instrument chargeable under Articles 17 and 32 of Schedule I-A.
(Arts. 5(a) and (b) and 38 of Sch. 1A)
Classified Topics 279

(1) Instruments of transfer of shares of public companies and
associations.

(m) Central excise bonds

If the exact stamp duty cannot be paid for want of Stamps of the required
value in circulation, the amount of deficit can be made up by affixing 10
paise and 5 paise Revenue adhesive Stamps — (Rule 13-A.)
State the manner in which adhesive stamps affixed to instruments
are to be cancelled and the effect of non-cancellation?

The adhesive Stamp affixed to any instrument shall be cancelled in such
a manner that it cannot be used again. The person may cancel it by
writing on or across the Stamp his name or initials or the name (or his
initials) of his firm with dates or in any other effected manner. If the
stamps are not cancelled in the prescribed manner, the instrument shall
be deemed to be unstamped. (Sec. 12.)

Indicate briefly the procedure to be followed to check against
forgery of adhesive stamps?

Rubber Stamp if used should not be used for defacing adhesive stamps
in such a way as to cover the whole or greater part of the Stamp as it
would render detection of forgery difficult or impossible (BSO 86).
There is no objection, however tv the use of a perforating instrumnet. In
case of doubt, a reference should be made to the General Manager,
India Security Press, Nasic Road for opinion who will give it free of
charge in genuine cases if the reference is made by the Departments of
the Government. In the case of parties and civil suits suitable fee will be
charged (BSO 87).

(ii) COLLECTOR UNDER STAMP ACT

Explain the powers of Collector under the Act.
The powers of Collector under Stamp Act are as follows :
Sec.16 : Denoting Duty. 5

Sec.18  : Stamping documents executed out of India and received in
India

Sec.19A : Stamping documents executed in other states of India and
received in Andhra Pradesh.

Sec.26 : Estimating amount of Royalty in respect of Mining Leases granted
by Government.

Sec.31, 32: Adjudication as to Stamp Duty payable on documents.

Sec. 37 read with Rule18 Validating documents bearing stamps of proper
value but of improper description.
Classified Topics

Sec. 39 : Refund of Penalty in respect of documents admitted in evidence
on payment of deficit duty and penalty equal to 10 times deficit duty.
Sec. 40 : Levying deficit duty and penalty on insufficiently stamped
documents.

Sec. 41 : Levying deficit duty on documents voluntarily produced within
one year from date of their execution.

Sec. 42 : Endorsement of payment of deficit duty and penalty levied
under Sec. 40 and 41.

Sec. 45 : Delegated powers to refund duty and penalty levied in excess.
Sec. 48 : Recovery of deficit duty and penalty etc. by coercive process
under Revenue Recovery Act.

S. 49, 51, 52, 54 & 55 : Refund of value of spoiled or misused stamps or
stamps not required for use.

Sec. 61 : Power to move appellate court when the lower court admitted
a document on payment of insufficient duty and penalty.

Sec.43 and 70 : Sanction of prosecution for offences under the Act,
staying such prosecution and compounding the offence.

Sec.73 : Inspection of books, papers, documents etc. in Public Offices to
secure any duty lost to the Government.

ii). DULY STAMPTED

Detail two cases wherein even though the instrument is drawn
upon stamp papers of proper value it is still considered to be not
duly stamped

Documents written in contravention of Secs. 13 and 14 are the two cases
in which, though the amount of duty on proper value has been paid, yet
the documents are held as not duty stamped. (Note under Section 15
APSM)

State whether the following document is duly stamped ?

A sale dated 26.8.2004 relating to property in Mahabvobnagar, a special
grade municipality, executed by ‘A’ in favour of ‘B’ for Rs. 25,000 drawn
up on stamps of — Rs.2200/-. The same property was previously
mortgaged to ‘B’ by ‘A’ for Rs. 15,000/- by a deed of M.W.P., dated
8.10.2000 drawn up on Stamps of Rs.800/-.

The Stamp duty payable on the Mortgage with possession was Rs.750/-
at 5% under Art.35(a). The Stamp duty payable on sale for Rs. 25.000/
- was Rs. 3000/- at 7% under Art.47A(b). The rebate that can be allowed.
under Sec. 24 was Rs.750 only and not Rs.800/-. Hence a duty of Rs.
2250/- should have been paid on the sale deed instead of Rs.2200/-
Classified Topics 281

A transfer of perpetual lease (non-agricultural) by ‘A’ in favour of

‘B’ dated 6.1.2005 for a consideration of Rs, 700 and on condition

that ‘B’ paid to ‘A’ Rs. 60 p.a. during A’s life time drawn on

Stamp papers worth Rs. 75/- bearing superscription “Bombay

Province”. Is the document duly stamped?

The consideration for the transfer worksout to Rs. 700 + 60 x 12 i.e., Rs.

1420/- (total) and chargeable to duty under Art. 54 of Sch. I-A. The

document is therefore sufficiently stamped. It can be deemed as duly

stamped if it was executed in Bombay province. If it was executed
in A.P, the document is considered as not duly stamped.

A special power of attorney authorising the agent to admit

execution of a document before the Registrar of Guntur was

executed at Burma and was received in Guntur on 31-12-2004.

The power was drawn up on stamp paper of Rs. 20/- issued by

courses are open to the party to get it validated and within what

time.

Burma is outside India and therefore the document should have been got

restamped under, Sec.18, within 3 months after its receipt in Guntur on

31-12-2004 i.e., before 31-3-2005 by the Collector or any officer appointed

as Collector under Sec. 18 (vide Sec. 2(9). The power executed at Burma

on stamp papers issued by the Government of Burma is not valid in India

unless restamped under section 18

What are the cases in which instruments bearing Stamp of proper

amount are deemed to be unstamped and what is the procedure

for getting them duly stamped? Discuss?

(i) Every instrument written on impressed stamp shall be written in
such manner that the stamp may appear on the face of the
instrument and cannot be used again (vide Section 13.) No second
instrument chargeable with duty shall be written on stamp paper
upon which an instrument chargeable with duty was already written
(vide Sec.14) Any instrument written in contravention of Secs. 13
and 14 shall be deemed as unstamped(vide Sec.15) They can be
validated under Secs. 40 & 42 without payment of fine. (Vide
Proviso to Sec. 40(1).

(ii) Any instrument bearing an adhesive stamp which has not been
cancelled so that it cannot be used again shall be deemed to be
unstamped. It can be validated under Sections 41 and 42 within
one year from date of execution and if later, under Secs. 40 and 42

(ii) When an instrument bears a stamp of proper amount but of improper

description, it will be deemed unstamped, but the Collector may, on
payment of proper duty, certify it as duly stamped —(Sec. 37, read
with Rule 18.)

(iv) If stamps purchased in other states are used for documents
chargeable with duty in the State of A.P. or if the stamp papers do
not bear stamp Vendor’s endorsements the documents drawn upon
them shall be deemed as unstamped. They can be validated under

The expression ‘duly stamped’ would seem to mean not only

bearing a stamp of proper value but also stamped at the right

time and in proper manner — Discuss?
Proper time of Stamping : Stamp duty should be paid before or at
the time of execution (Sec. 17). The exceptions are :-

(a) . Docts executed out of India may be stamped within 3 months from
date of its receipt in India (Sec. 18).

(b) Bills of Exchange and Promissory notes executed out of India should

- be stamped before they are presented for payment or
acceptance etc. (Sec. 19).

(c) Documents. executed out of the A-P. State in India and received in
A-P. State should be stamped with difference of duty if any, within
3 months from date of its receipt in A.P. State (Sec. 19-A).

(d) Stamp duty can be paid under Secs. 31 and 32 within one month
from date of execution or 3 months from date of receipt in
India from abroad.

(e) Stamp duty can be paid within one year from date of execution
under Sec. 41 and 42.
Proper Manner of Stamping : Vide Para 5 above.

provisions of Secs. 13 and 14.

Vide Items (i) and (ii) and (iv) of para 9 above.
