Through A.P. (Amedment) Act No. 19 of 2005 which has come into
effect from 1-8-2005, the following explanation is added under Article
7(b) of Schedule 1 A,

"Explanation : For the purpose of clause(a) of this article, not
withstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of
any court or order of any authority, any letter, note, memorandum or
writing relating to the deposit of title deeds whether written or made
either before or at the time when or after the deposit of the title deeds is
effected and whether it is in respect of security for the first loan or any
additional loan or loans taken subsequently, such letter, note,
memorandum or writing shall, in the absence of any separate agreement
or memorandum of agreement relating to deposit of such title deeds, be
deemed to be an instrument evidencing an agreement relating to the
deposit of titledeeds."

Agreement relating to deposit of Title deeds

In an agreement relating to deposit of Title deeds a clause that the
borrower undertook not to create any mortgage etc on the property
relating to documents deposited’ and to keep the same free from
encumbrances, amounts to a charge deemed to have been created to secure
the repayment of loan and hence the document has to be classified as
"SIMPLE MORTGAGE" (IG & RS Memo No.G4/6006/81,
Dt.24.4.1982)

Mortgage - Definition of

‘The definition of ‘Mortgage’ deed under Stamp Act is much wider than
the same under Section.58 of the T.P.Act. The Stamp Act is made
applicable to transfer of both movable and immovable properties while
Section 58 of T.P.Act refer to mortgages relating to immovable property
only. In addition a charge is also included in the difination under the
Stamp Act while there is a seperate provision in respect of charge over
immovable property under Section 100 of T-P.Act. Deed of hypothication
is chargeable as a mortgage under Art 35 of Sch [A when a charge is
created on the land, buildings etc mortgaged separately under equitable
mortgage a fact of which is irrelevant (Refered case 112/1979 judgment
of the A.P.High Court dt.23.7.1985 IG's endorsement No.SAc/32267/
87, dt.11.1.1988)

EquitableMortgage (Agreement relating to deposit of Title Deeds)

(i) An instrument " evidencing an agreement to secure the repayment
of a loan upon the deposit of title deeds" was held to be a mortgage
deed as it created a "right over property" viz the right to bring the
specified property to sale for the satisfaction of the claim (AIR
1939 RC 167). The Stamp Act makes no difference between a
legal mortgage and an equitable mortgage. But if a document falls
with in the special class of documents referred to in Art 7 of Sch
1A, then it would be charged as an agreemént relating to the deposit
of title deeds and not as mortgage deed (vide commentary on
Section 2 (17) (Mortgage deed) of the Indian Stamp Act by
K.Krishnamurthy Sth edition - page 87)

(ii) Letters styled as confirmatory letters obtained from the loanees
mentioning deposit of title deeds on a particular date (Form A of
S.B.1) and indicating confirmation of the party of his intention to
create equitable mortgage on subscquent date (Form B) the Bank
is granting Loans after recording the facts in a register. Letter is
not a subscquent or a follow up to any previously executed (duly
stamped) document and hence the letter has to be treated as
“Agreement relating to deposit of title deeds" chargeable under

MORTGAGE WITH POSSESSION
‘A’ executed a Mortgage deed without possession in favour of
‘B’ for Rs.1,000/- Subsequently the mortgagor gives a power
authorising the mortgagee to collect the rents.

The latter document becomes a Mortgage with possession (vide
explanation under Art. 35). Stamp duty already paid on simple Mortgage
can be deducted and the balance only is to be paid.

The Mortgagor has agreed to pay a monthly rent of Rs. 10 for
occupying the house mortgaged and also pay Rs. 10 per month for 5
years to a chit fund company on behalf of the mortgagee towards
discharge of mortgage debt.

Constructive possession is deemed to have been given to the mortgagee.
The duty is to be paid as a mortgage with possession

In a Mortgage without possession for Rs.2000/- the executant
authorises the mortgagee to collect Rs.20/- every month from the
lessee of the mortgagor towards interest.

The transaction becomes a mortgage with possession

‘A’ Mortgaged his properties to ‘B’ for Rs.3,000/- by way of simple
mortgage on 7-3-2005. On 10-3-2005 he executed a power authorising
the mortgagee to manage the secured properties and appropriate
profits in lieu of interest.

The transaction amounts to mortgage with possession for Rs.3000/- dt.7-
3-2005(Vide explanation under Art.35) and a General Power of Attorney
required stamp duty under (Arts. 35(b) and 42(c))

A Further charge with possession for Rs. 520/- ona simple mortgage
dated 20-3-2004 for Rs.700

Duty paid on the simple mortgage dt.20.3.2004 may be adjusted in the
total stamp duty by way of rebate. The document is to be treated as
M.W.P. for Rupees 1,220 and rebate should be given on the stamp duty
paid on the original mortgage in stamp duty payable on Rs.1220/- as
mortgage with possession

Simple mortgage for Rs. 1,000/- executed in favour of general power
of attorney holder in respect of property in Hyderabad.

According to explanation under Art. 35, Sch. I-A the document should
be treated as Mortgage with possession chargeable under Art. 35(a)
plus transfer duty.

POWER OF ATTORNEY
A Power of attorney authorising the agent to execute a sale for
Rs.5,000/- in favour of a specified person of a particular immovable
property and procure registration of the deed.
It is only a special power of attorney. Stamp duty payable is on the M.V.
of the property. (Art 42(b) of Sch.1A).
A Power authorising the agent to receive a certain sum of money
from the R.D.O in a land Acquisition case.
The document is a special power of attorney chargeable with a duty
under Article 42(b), (Note 9, P. 246, A.P.S.M)
A Power authorising the agent to appear in a court to be examined
on behalf of the Principal in connection with a specific suit on the
date of adjournment.
It is a Special power of attorney chargeable to a duty under Art. 42(b).
Sch. I-A
‘A’ authorised ‘B’ to bid at a sale held at abkari rentals and sign
necessary documents on behalf of the principal.
The document is a Special power of attorney chargeable under Art 42(b).
A Power authorising the agent to settle the accounts and sign receipts
relating to the transaction and procure registration of the document
It is a Special power of attorney and requires stamp under Art. 42(b).
Power of Attorney authorising the Agent to sell a house in Pakistan.
The document is chargeable as a special power of Attorney under Article
42(g) on the market value of the house.
A Power of attorney authorising the Agent to vote on behalf of the
principal at a meeting of the Creditors
It is chargeable to duty under Art. 42(b) as a special power
An Instrument whereby X authorises Y to canvas for intending
buyers, enter into agreement of sale if need be, receive sale
consideration, execute the Instrument of Sale, admit execution
thereto, and do all other acts that are incidental to complete the
registration of Sale in respect of a specified immovable property.
The document is a special power of Attorney chargeable to duty on market
value of the property, (Art. 42(g)).
‘A’ executed a document on 5-9-2004 authorising ‘B’ to act in the
matter of the transfer of Patta before the Collector.

The document is chargeable to duty as a Special Power of Attorney
under Article 42(b) (Note 2 on page 244 APSM)

Power of attorney authorising a single agent to take all steps
necessary to complete execution of a decree in a single case.

The document is chargeable as a General Power of Attorney with a duty
under Art. 42(c), (14 on P. 247, A.P.S.M.).)

The executant agreed to pay the claimant Rs. 5,000 for conducting a
litigation and empowers the claimant to conduct a suit in a Civil
Court on his behalf.

If the claimant is authorised to act in the name of the executant as an
agent, the document attracts duty as Power of Attorney under Article
42(c), Schedule I-A. Otherwise it is an agreement not otherwise provided
for, chargeable with a duty under Article 6(c) of Sch. 1A.

A Power authorising the agent for presenting a document for
compulsory registration, to present the same before the Registrar
in Appeal if refused registration and to present the same for
registration if ordered in Appeal.

The document is a General power of attorney chargeable with a duty
under Article 42(c), Sch. I-A as it involves appearance in different offices.
A power authorising the agent to sell a particular immovable

A Power authorising the agent to appear and act on behalf of the

What is the Stamp duty payable on the following document?
Chittemma, while her divorce petition for dissolution of the marriage
between her and her husband was pending in Court, entered into second
marriage illegally with Peddanna. A daughter was also born to them.
The relationship between them later turned sour. Chittemma received
Rs. 10,000/- from Peddanna and executed a deed on 20-6-2006
relingushing her maintenance right over him.

NOTE

A Bench of the Supreme Court, in its judgment dated 13-12-2004 in Civil
appeal Nos. 1774 and 1775 of 2001, held that wife is entitled to
maintenance right even when the marriage was illegal. Therefore it is
construed that Chittemma. though her second marriage was illegal,
possess pre-existing right over the estate of Peddanna. The document is
a Release of maintenance right for Rs. 10,000/- chargeable to duty of
Rs. 100 at 1% on Rs. 10,000/- under Art 46A read with Notification 11
under G.O. M.S. No. 1129 Rev (Regn-1) dept dt. 13-6-2005 given effect
to from 1-7-2005

to Sec.3 read with Sec.29. As regards surcharge, there is no provision in
Municipalities Act for such exemption. Hence a Transfer Duty of Rs.41/
- is payable at 2%.

‘A’ sold to ‘B’ certain agricultural property for a consideration of
Stamp Duties on documents (Illustrations) 405
Rs.15,000/- with a condition to reconvey the property on payment
of consideration within ten years. After some time, within the period
specified, ‘B’ reconveyed the property for the same consideration
relinquishing his right over the property. The market value of the
property at the time of former document was Rs.15000 and the
same at the time of latter document was Rs. 20,000/-

The former document is chargeable as a sale with agreement to resell.
The stamp duty on the sale is payable on the market value of the property
or consideration whichever is higher plus an additional duty as an
agreement to sell under Art. 6A of Sch. I-A read with Sec. 5. The second
document reconveying the property is chargeable as a sale on the market
value of Rs. 20,000/- or consideration whichever is higher. Agreement
to sell agricultural property is chargeable only under Article 6A of
Schedule 1A. (vide APHC judgment dated 7-9-2004 in CRP No.6053 of
2002 (C & IGRS Memo No. S1/16160/04 dt. 2-3-2005). However
Transfer duty is leviable on the re-conveyance deed executed under sale
with agreement resell.

CHAPTER 9
Transfer Duty / Tax

1. (A) _ Transfer duty/Tax as the case may be, is a duty levied in the form
of surcharge on certain classes of instruments in relation to
immovable properties under the Acts governing local authorities
along with the stamp duty on such instruments leviable under the
Indian Stamp Act 1899, as in force fot the time being.

(B) “Local Authority" means the corporation of Hyderabad, the
contonmment of Secunderabad, a Municipal Council, a Zilla
Parished, Panchayat Samithi or a gram panchayat as the case may
be (Rule 2(iii) of the AP Municipalities (duty on transfer of
property) Rules 1965

2. The transfer duty on instruments on which Duty / Tax leviable

under the various Acts are as follows.

(A) The Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act,1955 (section 261)
1. Sales, 2. Exchanges, 3. Gifts, 4. Mortgage with possession of
property

(B) The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 (Section 120)

1. Sales, 2. Exchanges, 3. Gifts, 4. Mortgage wth possession of
property, 5. Lease for a term exceeding one hundred years or in

perpetuity
Transfer duty / Tax 417

3.

4.

(©)

(D)
1.

The Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayat Raj Act, 1994

1. Sales, 2. Exchanges, 3. Gifts, 4. Mortgage wth possession of
property, 5. Lease for a term exceeding one hundred years or in
perpetuity

Secunderabad Contonment :

Sales, 2. Gifts, 3. Mortgage with possession of property

The Transfer duty/ Tax is leviable at a rate as may be fixed by the
Government, not exceeding five percent of the amount on which

The Transfer duty collected on behalf of Gram Panchayat shall be
apportioned and allocated to the concerned Panchayat, Panchayat
Samithi and Zilla Parishad or the concerned local body in the ratio
of 3:1:1 respectively (Vide Rule 9 of Gram Panchayats (Duty on
transfer of property) rules 1965)

In respect of the sale Transactions of AP11C, the transfer duty has
to be adjusted to Gram Panchayat / Municipality at 35%, and to
API11C Industrial area local authority at 65% (Government Memo
No. 30726-A/782/BG/A2/98 Fin/Plg (F.W.B.G.) dept dt. 27-10-
1999)

Transfer duty is not automatically exempt even if stamp duty is
exempted in respect of Gram Panchayat areas. Government is
empowered under the Gram Panchayat Act to grant exemptions
from payment of Transfer duty leviable on any specified document
or class of documents.

But, in respect of the Municipal areas and Corporation areas,
there is no such provision in the Municipalities and other related
Acts enabling the government to grant exemptions from levy of
Transfer duty/Tax in respect of any instrument in such areas.
However, CHENCHU Agricultural labourers belonging to
scheduled tribes under the Scheme of purchase of agricultural land
as part of the economic support programe by all Integrated Tribal
Development Agencies in the state are exempted by Government
from payment of Transfer duty on the value of the land to be
registered in their favour (G.O. M.S. No. 362 P.R. & R.D (PTS II)
dept dt. 11-11-2003 IGRS No.S1/22592/03 dt. 15-12-2003)

thereunder MUTATIS MUTANDIS are applicable to the levy of
Transfer duty in relation to the duty chargeable under the local
Authorities Acts (Rule 3 of the A.P. Municipalities(Duty on
Transfer of property) Rules, 1965 and the A.P. Gram Panchayats
(Duty on transfer of property) Rules, 1965.
In the case of insufficiently stamped instrument liable to payment
of Transfer duty/ Tax, only such portion of duty as is in excess of the
duty payable under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 paid shall be allocated
to the concerned local body under Rule 5(3) of the A.P Gram
Panchayats (Duty on transfer of property) Rules, 1965.

Latest executive instructions with regard to the allocation of
Transfer duty/ Tax to various local bodies.

The following are the latest instructions (as on 1-9-2006).

The Registering officer, simultaneously with the registration of a document
attracting levy of transfer duty shall allocate the Transfer duty to the
concerned local authority. He shall maintain an account of the collection
of transfer duty, by entering the particulars in the book called "Ledger" or
in Account A as the case may be. He shall prepare a consolidated
statement of allocation of Transfer duties collected for various local bodies
for each quarter ending with the 30th June, 30th September, 31st December
and 31st March of every year. The government in their Memo No.
50796/ Regn.1(1)/2000 dt 15-6-2001(Vide Proceedings No. G1/27791/
4/2000 dated 18-8-2001 of the Commisssioner and Inspector General of
Registration and Stamps, Hyderabad)has entrusted the responsibility of
allocating transfer duty collected to the local bodies to the Assistant
District Registrar in the District Registrar's office of the district and the
Deputy Inspector General concerned as supervision authority. The
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, in the
said proceedings has accordingly ordered that the Assitant District
Registrar of the Registrar's Office shall be responsible for the allocation
of Transfer duty on quarterly basis with effect from the quarter ending
with September 2001 and the Deputy Inspector General concerned shall
ensure that the allocation of Transfer duty to the local bodies is done
correctly by the Assistant District Registrar and also obtain a certificate
to that effect form the Assistant District Registrar. The Sub-Registrars
shall prepare a consolidated statement of allocation of Transfer duties
for various local bodies for each quarter and send the same to the Assistant
District Registrar in the District Registrar's Office of the District who,
after due check, shall authorise the concerned Treasury officers for
payment of the Transfer Duty due to the concerned Loal body and also
cause credit of the collection charges of 5% (Annexure - 2) by deduction
from the total transfer duty towards collection charges due to the

REDUCTIONS OF TRANSFER DUTY/TAX
with effect from 1-7-2005

1. Transfer Duty / Tax as the case may be, with effect from 1-7-2005
has been reduced from 5% to 3% on the transfer of immovable
property situated in the limits of all panchayats and Municipalities
(except selection and Special grade Municipalities) in Andhra
Pradesh and similarly from 5% to 2% in respect of property situated
in the limits of all Municipal Corporations, Selection and Special
grade Muncipalities in A.P. (vide notifications relating to reduction
of Transfer Duty/ Tax on transfer of property annexed after
illustrations (transfer duty) No.15 infra

2. Where the Transfer duty is less than fifteen paise, such duty shall
not be collected and where it is more than fifteen paise, fraction of
five paise shall not be collected (para 3(2) of the A.P. Municipalities
(Duty on transfer of property) Rules, 1965 and the A.P. Gram
Panchayats (Duty on Transfer of property) Rules, 1965)

ELUCIDATIONS

1. What is Transfer Duty / Tax?

Transfer Duty/Tax is a duty levied as surchage on tranfer of

IMMOVABLE PROPERTY through instruments of Sale, exchange, Gift,

Mortgage with possession and Lease for a term exceeding one hundred

years or in perpetuity of immovable property in so far as the value

immovable property, on the value of the immovable property is situated
in the area under the jurisdiction of the concerned Local Authority in

Andhra Pradesh

2, What is the maximum rate of Transfer Duty/ Tax leviable
The maximum rate of transfer duty / tax leviable is five percent on the
amount on which stamp duty is levied under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

3. Who is the person liable to pay the Transfer Duty/ Tax?

In the absence of an agreement to the contrary, the transfer duty/tax

shall be paid by the person who is primarily liable for payment of the

Stamp Duty under Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

4. Is the Government empowered to exempt any instrument from
perrent of Transfer Duty/Tax?

i) Section 69(5) of the A.P. Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, empowers the
Government, subject to such conditions and terms as many be, to
exempt any instrument or class of instruments to which the levy
of Transfer duty is applicable -

ii) | But there is no provision in the Municipalities & the Corporations
Transfer duty / Tax 425
Acts to grant exemption from payment of such duty by any authority
in respect of the areas situated in Municipal and Corporation
limits.

5. What is the percentage of Transfer Duty/ Tax leviable under the

various Local Bodies Act with effect from 1-7-2005 ?
The Transfer Duty/ Tax leviable with effect from 1-7-2005 is as under.

Areas in all the panchayats and the Municipalities other than

the areas in selection/ special grade and Municipal Corpora- 3%
tions in Andhra Pradesh

Areas in Selection/Special Grade Municipalities and Munici- } 2%
patcorporations in Andhra Pradesh

6. | What are the executive instructions on allocation and adjustment
of Transfer duty/ Tax?

Vide Para 11 supra under Transfer duty / Tax for the instructions

TRANSFER DUTY (ILLUSTRATIONS)

1. Sale Certificate dated 6-6-2006 issued by the Deputy Registrar
of Co-op. Societies for Rs. 2,000/- subject to the discharge of
mortgage debt of Rs. 4,000/-

Sale Certificates issued by the Co-op. Registrar or the Deputy Registrar
are exempted from levy of Transfer Duty

2. Transfer of Lease with improvements for a consideration of Rs. 3000/

No Transfer duty is leviable on transfer of lease with improvements.
But if building constructed on lease hold lands are sold, the sale deed is
leviable with Transfer Duty (RG. 1973 - P.70)

3. Usufructuary mortgage for Rs. 3000/- dated 4-3-2006. The
mortgaged property is situated in Municipal Corporation area.
Transfer Tax is leviable at the rate applicable to the area where the
mortgaged property is situated, as usufructuary mortgage has to be treated
as Mortgage with possession. The Tax on Transfer of property situated
in Municipal Corporation areas is 2% with effect from 1-7-2005. Tax
leviable is Rs.60/-

4. A Perpetual lease relating to agricultual lands reserving an annual
rentof Rs.100/- with a premium of Rs.2,000/-

In the case of perpetual leases, the transfer duty leviable was at 5% on
the market value of the property or on the value ten times of the average
annual rent reserved whichever is higher. No transfer duty is leviable on
Premium. Now i.e.with effect from 1-7-2005 the transfer duty leviable
is at 3% or 2% as the case may be (vide S.No.5 supra)

Sale for Rs. 5,000/- comprising immovable properties in
Vijayawada corporation area and also in Patna (Bihar State)

The rules regulating the levy of Transfer duty in Bihar State are not
known. The transfer duty is leviable under the local Authorities Act
which apply to the respective State only. No Transfer duty can be levied
on the property in Patna. Transfer Duty in respecct of property in
Vijayawada Corporation area alone is levviable at the rate applicable to
the Municipal Corporation area on the date of the document. The duty
is at 2% from 1-7-2005

Sale of the superstructure of a house.

Sale of superstructure of a house, if it is not intended to be removed as
material under the contract of sale, amounts to sale of immovable property
and attracts levy of Transfer duty at the applicable rate.

Sale deed dated 20-5-2006 by a member of a co-operative society
conveying house in Bapatla Municipality in favour of the Society.
The executant has been a member of the society from 1-7-2000
Transfer duty only should be levied at the rate applicable to Bapatla
Municipality on the date of the Sale deed as the executant is a member
of the society for more than two years.

APPENDIX -3 A
The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities (Duty on transfers of
property) Rules, 1965
[G.o.ms.no.1040, Municipal Administration, Dated 16.8.1965]

In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (a) of sub-section (2) of
Section 326 read with Section 122 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act,
1965 (Andhra Pradesh Act 6 of 1965), the Governor of Andhra Pradesh hereby
makes the following rules for the collection of duty on transfers of property,
the same having been published previously at pages 74-78 of Rules Supplement
to Part Lof the Andhra Pradesh Gazette, dated the 22 April, 1965 as required
by clauses (a) and (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 237 of the said Act.

1. Short title and commencement:- (1) These rules may be called the
Andhra Pradesh Municipalities (Duty on Transfers of Property) Rules,
1965.

(2) These rules shall come into force after expiry of period of one month
from the date of their final publication in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette.

2.  Definitions:- In these rules unless there is anything repugnant in the
subject or context—

(i) ‘Government’ means the State Government;

(ii) ‘Instrument’ means an instrument of sale, exchange, gift, mortgage
with possession or lease in perpetuity of immovable property on
which transfer duty is leviable under Section 120 of the Andhra
Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965;

(iii) ‘Local authority’ means the Corporation of Hyderabad, the
cantonment of Secunderabad, a Municipal Council, a Zilla
Parishad, Panchayat Samithi or a Gram Panchayat, as the case
may be;

(iv) “Stamp Act’ means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as in force in the
State of Andhra Pradesh;

(v) ‘Transfer Duty’ means the duty on transfers of property leviable
under Section 120 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965;
and

(vi) all words and expressions not defined in these rules shall have the
meanings respectively assigned to them by the Stamp Act and the
rules made thereunder.

3. Provisions of the Stamp Act to apply to transfer duty:- (1) All the
provisions of the Stamp Act and the rules made thereunder shall so far
as may be, apply in relation to the transfer duty as they apply in relation
to the duty chargeable under that Act.

GB)

Where the transfer duty is less than fifteen paise, duty shall not be collected
and where the transfer duty is more than fifteen paise, fraction of 5 paise
shall not be collected.
Duties of Registering Officer in regard to the particulars to be
set-forth in instruments:- (1) Whenever any instrument is presented
for registration to any Registering Officer, he shall see whether the
particulars referred to in Section 27 of the Stamp Act are setforth in the
instrument separately as required by the said section read with Section
121 (a) of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 and shall also
ensure that the local authority within whose jurisdiction the property
concerned is situated is setforth clearly in the instrument.
If the said particulars be not so separately set forth in the instrument, the
Registering Officer must impound it and forward it to the Collector calling
his attention to Section 64 of the Stamp Act, read with Section 121 (b) of
the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965.
The duty leviable on an instrument of exchange shall be regulated as
follows : -
(a) _ If the values of th properties exchanged:are unequal the duty shall
“ be leviable on the value of the property of the greater value;

(b) If the values of the properties exchanged are equal, the higher
amount of duty leviable shall be levied; and

(c) The duty levied on an instrument of exchange shall be distributed
among the local authorities concerned in proportion to the
amount of duty levible on the properties in the respective local

areas.
5. Maintenance and consolidation of accounts in respect of trans-
fer duty:-
(1) (a) Every Registering Officer shall maintain an account of the duty

paid in respect of each instrument registered by him showing
separately the duty imposed by Stamp Act and the transfer duty.
He shall also maintain a separate account for each local authority
within whose jurisdiction the property concerned. in situated
ascertaining form the concerned party wherever necessary the
amount-on which the transfer duty is to be levied.

(b) The said account shall be consolidated quarterly for each such
local authority by the District Registrar.

(c) The Inspector General of Registration and Stamps may issue
executive instructions regarding the maintenance of accounts by
Registering Officer in this behalf and the form in which the

Registering Officer owing to the fact that they are not compulsorily
registerable under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, the Collector
before whom any such instrument in produced under Section 31 or 41 of
the Stamp Act, or who impounds any such instrument under Section 33
of the said Act, or receives a certificate of the duty and penalty paid in
respect of any such instrument or the original of any such instrument
under Section 38 of the said Act, shall keep an account of the duty paid
in respect of each instrument showing separately the duty imposed by
the Stamp Act and the transfer duty and forward to the District Registrar
of Assurances concerned within one month after the close of each quarter,
a quarterly consolidated account in the form appended to these rules.
If in any case it is impossible to recover the full duty payable on any
instrument then, only such portion of the duty realised on such instrument
as is in excess of the duty imposed by the Stamp Act shall be treated in
the accounts referred to in this rule as transfer duty. In such case, the
Collector will be the deciding authority regarding the impossibility or
otherwise of the collection of the Stamp duty including surcharge thereon.
Collector to forward to the District Registrar concerned quarterly
Statement of refunds of transfer duty:-Every Collector who sanctions

payable to each Municipality in:every quarter shall be furnished to the
Commissioner of the concerned.Municipality. :

transfer duty paid less a deduction of five percent thereon on account of
the collection of the transfer duty and the amount of refunds referred to
in Rule 6 if any.

In calculating the charges on account of collection of the transfer duty
fractions of ten paise which are five paise or more shall be counted as
ten paise and fractions of less than five paise shall be ignored.

APPENDIX - 5
The Andhra. Pradesh Gram Panchayats
(Duty on Transfer of Property) Rules, 1965
[G.O.MS.No.778, P.R., Dated 5 July, 1965]

In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (3) and (4) of
Section 73 of the Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayats Act, 1964 (Andhra Pradesh
Act 2 of 1964), the Governor of Andhra Pradesh hereby makes the following
tules relating to levy of duty on transfer of property, the same having been
previously published at pages 1-5 of the Rules Supplement to Part VH of Andhra
Pradesh Gazette, dated the 15" Octobe, 1964, as required by subsection (3) of
Section 217 of the said Act.

1, Short title:~

(1) These rules may be called the Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayats
(Duty on Transfer of Property) Rules, 1965.

(2) They shall come into force on and.from 01.09.1965.
2. Definitions:-

In these rules unless the context otherwise requires -
(i) “the Act” means the Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayats Act, 1964;

(ii) “Collector” means District Collector and any officer in charge of
a Revenue division and. includes a Deputy Collector, a Sub-
Collector and Assistant — Collector;

(iii) “Instrument” means an instrument of sale, exchange, gift, mortgage
with possession or lease in perpetuity of immovable property on
which transfer duty is livable under Section 73 of Act;

(iv) “Stamp Act” means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as in force in the
State of Andhra Pradesh;

(v) “transfer duty” means the duty on transfer of property leviable
under Section 73 of the Act;

(vi) all words and expressions not defined in these rules shall have the
meanings respectively assigned to them by the Stamp Act and the
rules there under.

3. Provisions of Stamp Act apply to transfer duty:~

(1) The procedure laid down in the’pravisions of the Indian Stamp
Act, 1899 and the rules thereunder for the collection of stamp
duty chargeable under that Act, shall so far as may be, followed
for the collection of the duty under the Act.

(2) Where the transfer duty is less than fifteen paise, such duty shall
not be collected; where the transfer duty is more than fifteen paise
fractions of five paise shall not be collected.

Co PNAARYN

MARKET VALUE SCHEME
1. A (1) Justification and Introduction

The system was copied from Tamil Nadu with certain modifications. Prior
to the introduction of the scheme in 1971, the Stamp Duty in respect of sale
was payable on the amount of consideration for the sale irrespective of the
value of the property conveyed. Though according to Section 27 of the Indian
Stamp Act, 1899 the parties must state the amount of consideration and all
other facts and circumstances affecting the chargeability of any instrument
with duty or the amount of duty with which it is chargeable have to be fully
and truly setforth in the instrument and failure to do so is punishable under: -
Section 64, there was large scale understatement of consideration for the
following reasons.

Firstly there was no method of ascertaining the real consideration paid
for the sale.

Secondly INTENTION to DEFRAUD GOVERNMENT REVENUE is a necessary
condition to obtain conviction of the offenders under Section 64 but to prove
such intention is very difficult.

Hence the Act was amended by introducing Section 47-A to the Act
(A.P.Act.No.XXII of 1971) effective from 16-8-1975. Prescribing duty payable
under certain Articles of Schedule 1A to the Act-on the basis of market value
of the property affected by the document concemed and in respect of sale
deeds on the sale amount / consideration or on the market value of the property
sold whichever is higher. It is easier to ascertain market value of property than
452 Market Value Scheme

the real sale amount / consideration. This is a necessary measure to plug
leakage of stamp revenue. The Madras High Court upheld the scheme.

A (2) Distinction between Section 27 and Section 47-A

Section 27 says that all facts and circumstances affecting the chargeability
of instruments to duty shall be fully and truly setforth therein. Section 64 lays
down that if any one contravenes the provisions of Section 27 with an intention
to defraud the Government of its revenue, he is punishable with fine upto
Rs.5000/-. As there is no method of ascertaining real sale amount / consideration
in respect of sale deeds, it is difficult to prove in a Court of law, the intention of
the offender to defraud the Government of its revenue.

Under Section 47-A, as amended by Act No.8 of 1998 effective from 23-
4-1998, the duty in respect of conveyance (sale) exchange, gift, partition,
settlement, release, agreement relating to constmtian, development or sale of
any immovable property or Power of Attoreny given for sale or development of
immovable property is made payable on consideration or market value of the
property whichever is higher. In respect of Gift, Exchange, Partition and
Settlement the duty is payable on the market value of the property affected.
Guidelines values were provided to Registering Officers to calculate market
values. If the value declared in the documents is less than such market value
as per the guidelines, the Registering Officer shall keep pending registration
such document presented and refer the case to the District Registrar, who is
appointed as Collector under Section 47A . The Section enables determination
of the correct market value by following the procedure prescribed therefor and
for collection of the difference in duty if any. If the party is aggrieved, provision
is also made for appeal to the Civil Court. This provision of Section 47-A
cannot only plug leakage of stamp revenue and prevent loss to the Government
but also serves as a deterrent.

A (3) Refusal to agree for compounding is ignored and acceptance
of the same is penalised - elucidation

Section 64 provides for punishment for undervaluation of documents or
failure to setforth fully and-truly all facts and circumstances affecting
chargeability of an instrument with an intention to defraud Government of its
revenue with fine upto Rs.5000/-. Section 70 enables compounding of such
offences by the Authorised Officers. The District Registrars, some Sub-
Registrars of Grade I, Joint Sub Registrar I in District Registrars Offices and
some other Officers of the department are empowered to compound such
offences. If an offender to whom a notice is given providing an opportunity to
get the offence compounded out of Court gives consent for such compounding
and payment of agreed compound fee, the offence can be compounded.
Market Value Scheme 453
Otherwise, the offence cannot be compounded in the absence of such consent.

Thus the party who accepts for compounding the offence is penalised under
Section 64,

In some cases, parties are adament and do not agree for compounding.
The only alternative is to sanction their prosecution. But it is difficult to prove
the intention of the party to defraud, which fact is a pre-requisite to sanction
prosecution, with the result that the parties are acquited

It is therefore correct to say that refusal to agree for compounding is
ignored, acceptance of the same is penalised.

A (4) Compounding Fee

There is no provision in the Stamp Law empowering the CCRA to remit
even a part of the compounding fee. Compounding fee is the one levied with
the consent of the party. In such cases, the question of appeal does not arise. If
the Collector fixed the compounding fee unilaterally, it was irregular.

A (5) Executive Instructions

1) _ In the case of documents undervalued and presented to a Sub-
Registar for Registration, the parties have to be advised to get the
document validated under Sections 41 and 42. If they are unwilling,
the document has to be kept pending and reference made to the
Collector under Section 47-A.

2) The composition fee ordered to be levied by officers empowered
to compound offences of undervaluation, if not paid by the party,
can be collected by coercive process under Section 48 (vide Section
70(3).

3) When the party guilty of undervaluation dies, no action need to be
taken against the legal representatives. Action may be taken against
the other persons concerned as "abettors" under Section 64(b) &
(c) provided there is proper evidence.

4) _ Deficitly stamped document produced in undervaluation enquires
should be dealtwith under Section 33 and 40 but not under Section
35.

5) In respect of cases referred to the District Registrar (Collector)
under Section 47-A, the Sub-Registrars have to wait till receipt of
orders of the District Registrar determining the correct market value
of the property before taking any further action on his reference.

A (40) Instruments executed before increase of stamp duty due to
revision of market value of the properties:

 

The stamp duty payable on instruments chargeable under Indian Stamp
Act, 1899 should be determined with reference to the DATE OF EXECUTION of
the instrument as the duty is payable before or at the time of execution of
instruments (Section 17) with exceptions provided under Sections 10A, 31
and 41 of the Act.

" Duly Stamped " means stamped with the value and description of stamps
required by the law in force WHEN THE INSTRUMENT WAS EXECUTED (vide note
under Section 2(ii) on page 7 APSM). The date of execution is criterion far
payment of stamp duty. The relevant factor for collection of stamp duty is
the date of execution of the document [1997 (3) ALD 261 and 2001 (3) ALD
317 (DB)]

Whenever the market value of the properties are revised upwards the
duty on instrument chargeable under Articles of Schedule 1A, having a bearing
Market Value Scheme : 457
on the market value of properties is payable on the basis of the enhanced market
value of the properties or the consideration etc. as the case may be whichever
is higher IN RESPECT OF THE DOCUMENTS EXECUTED ON AND AFTER THE DATE OF
SUCH INCREASE IN MARKET VALUES,

The time for presentation of documents to the registering officers for
registration under the Registration Act, 1908 is Four Montus from the date of
their execution (Section 23 of the Registration Act, 1908) and in continuation,
ANOTHER Four Montus on payment of fine and subject to condonation of delay
(Section 25 of Registration Act, 1908). Therefore the parties will have time
for a total period of 4 + 4 months FROM THE DATE OF EXECUTION of the document
for its presentation for registration as stated above

Hence, when an executed document bears stamp duty required under the
Stamp Law As IN FORCE ON THE DATE OF ITS EXECUTION, such document is DuLy
SrampeD not withstanding enhancement of market value of properties on and
from a subsequent date of its execution and before it is presented for registration.
The question of collection of further duty on the plea of upward revision of
market values taken place after the date of execution of document does not
arise [vide S.Nos.6 & 14 of " Case Law " appended at the end of the " Rules
framed under Section 47-A" = A.P Stamp (POU) Rules 1975 infra]

(i) The Market Value of buildings shall be computed on any one of the
following methods whichever is higher
a) The consideration as setforth in the instrument

b) Market value as declared by the party (as envisaged in Section 27
of the Act, i.e. likely sale value of the property in open market.

c) Value as provided to the Registering Officer on the basis of the
Guideline values and the schedule of the rates of construction.

d) Eighteen times the annual rental value

(ii) Value of buildings on the basis of Annual Rental Value

of the Schedule Property, whichever is higher shall be taken into account

3) The above instructions shall apply to all Municipal Corporations, Special

establishments and Offices.

Market Value Scheme (Undervaluation of Documents) 459

1.

2.(A) UNDERVALUATION OF DOCUMENTS

Enquiry : Undervaluation of deeds with intent to defraud the
Government of its Revenue is an offence under Section.64 of the
Stamp Act. Section 27 lays down that all circumstances affecting the
chargeability of an instrument shall be fully and truly setforth in the deed.
Contravention of the section is punishable with fine which may extend to
Rs. 5,000/- (Section 64) in addition to the amount of loss caused on
account of undervaluation (Section 64-A)

2 (a) When a Sub Registrar is credibly informed that an offence of

undervaluation is committed by a person, he may conduct an enquiry

first instance inform the concerned party that undervaluation is on offence
under the Stamp Act and that if he chooses he may come up for
compounding the offence. Certain Sub- Registrars Grade1 or Joint Sub-
Registrar I in the District Registars Offices and all Assistant District
Registrars and the District Registrars are authorised to compound
offences. If the party does not come forward to get the offence
compounded (vide para 7 below), the Sub-Registrar may seek orders of
the Registrar sanctioning prosecution. If the party comes forward to get
the offence compounded he may be given an opportunity to do so. A
letter of consent has to be obtained from the party. The amount of

3. Although the maximum fine that can be imposed by a court as a
punishment for undervaluation is Rs.5000/-, it does not mean that the
compounding fee cannot be levied in excess of Rs.5000/- . Normally
compounding fee is Computed taking into consideration the amount of
loss incurred by the Government. (Section 64 A of the Stamp Act).

4. If during the course of an enquiry under S.0.482 an insufficiently stamped
document is produced by a party or a witness, the Sub-Registrar cannot
impound it. He can send it to the District Registrar for impounding it as
he deals with undervaluation cases in a Statutory capacity as Collector
under Section 70. After impounding it, the Registrar may proceed under
Section 35 and 38(1) since the document is not admitted in evidence
within the scope of proviso (a) to Sec.35 of Stamp Act. Enquiry under
S.0.482 is only an administrative function and is not a statutory duty.
The person who produced the document has to pay the duty. (Vide Procgs.
No.S2/36395/66), dated 3-3-1967 of I.G.R &S).

2. (B) Rules Under Section 27 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899
[G. O. Ms. No.34,Revenue (Registration I) Department,dt. 8-1-1999]

1. Short Title : - These Rules may be called the "Andhra Pradesh Stamp
(Inspection of Properties) Rules, 1998"

2. Inspection of Property : - The Inspector General of Registration and
Stamps may by order, authorise any officer under his control to conduct
inspection of any property or a class or category of properties registered
under the provisions of the Registration Act, 1908 for the purpose of
ensuring compliance with the provisions of Section 27 of the said Act
and to assess the value of such property.

3. Assessment of Property : - The officer authorised shall complete the
inspections entrusted to him within such period as may be specified and
assess the value of the properties with reference to the market value
prevailing and the construction rates prescribed in accordance with the
Andhra Pradesh Revision of Market Value Guidelines, Rules 1998

4, Action to be taken due to wrong assessment and suppression of facts
:- If the authorised officer detects any deficit duty payable in respect of
any instrument:

a) due to wrong assessment, either the value or the duty payable,
by the Registering Officer, he shall deal with such cases under the
provisions of Section 41-A of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

b) due to suppression of facts affecting the chargeability of the
instrument, the authorised officer shall issue a notice in such form
as may be prescribed to the person concerned within fifteen (15)
days from the date of inspection giving an opportunity to explain
the reasons for the variation

5. Compounding of Offence : -

1) If the person to whom a notice has been issued under rule 4(b),
gives a consent in writing to get the offence compounded, the
authorised officer shall levy and collect compounding fee, which
shall in no case be less than the loss of revenue involved, within
three months from the date of inspection and make necessary
endorsement on the original instrument in such form as may be
prescribed. The authorised officer shall forward a copy: of the
proceeding determining the value of the property and levying
compounding fee for making necessary entries in the relevant
registers and records.

2) Ifthe compounding fee levied under sub rule 5(1) is not paid within
the stipulated period, it shall be recovered under the provisions of
Market Value Scheme 467

section 48 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

3) If the person to whom a notice has been issued under rule 4(b)
does not respond or agree to the assessment of the value and the
deficit amount determined by the authorised officer, the authorised
officer shall launch prosecution against the person under the
provisions of section 64 based on the facts and circumstances as
required under section 27 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899.

6. Inspection of property already inspected by the authorisedofficer

The Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, for sufficient reasons
to be recorded in writing may order for inspection of any property already
inspected by any of the authorised officers and take appropriate action.

The Government have issued rules under Section 27 of Indian Stamp
Act,1899 through the G.O. cited above. In this connection, the following
instructions are issued to all the concerned in supersession of all the erstwhile
instructions issued from time to time from this office in respect of the
spot inspections and super checks : -

1. The Registering Officer (RO) before whom the document is presented
can straight away register the same, if it is otherwise in order, without
conducting spot inspection of the property. However, the R.O. shall
exercise all precautions including the following, in the scrutiny of the
documents to arrest leakage of revenue.

a) Correct classification of document

b) Comparison of the extents of site and built up area mentioned in
the link document and the document under scrutiny.

c) Age of the building as per the link document and the document
under scrutiny.

d) Correctness of the site rates as applicable to residential / commercial
Structures.

e) Comparison of the facts and figures as mentioned in the document
and those figuring in registration check slip.

All urban properties both houses and vacant sites exceeding value of
Rs.5 lakhs in Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad, Rs.3 lakhs in other
Municipal Corporations / Municipalities and Rs.1.5 lakhs in all other
areas are to be spot inspected by the Officers specifically authorised by
C & LG (R&S) after registration of the document to detect suppression
of facts, if any. (Vide para 3 (D) infra enhancing the limits)

i) In exercise of the powers conferred under Rule 2 of A.P.Stamp
(inspection of properties) Rules, 1998, the Inspector General of
Registration and Stamps hereby authorises the Deputy Collectors
(Flying Squad), Vigilance Officers, District Registrars, District
Registrar (Audit) and Assistant to District Registrars to conduct
inspection of properties for the purpose of ensuring compliance
with the provisions of Section 27 of Indian Stamp Act and to assess
the value of such properties.

specific authorisation to the Deputy Collector (Flying Squad) and
Vigilance Officers to conduct Post-facto inspection of properties
effected by documents registered in specified Sub Registry Offices
in each month by 25th of that month. The Deputy Collectors

of properties requiring spot inspection either from the D.I.G or
from the Sub-Registrars concerned.

Registry Offices (other than those allocated to Deputy Collectors
and Vigilance Officers by the Inspector General of Registration
and Stamps) to D.Rs. D.R (Audit) and A.D.Rs. under their
respective jurisdiction.

concerned for allocation of conduction spot inspection to the Authorised

Authorised Officer shall proceed under Section 48 of I.S.Act for recovery

assessment of the value and the deficit amount determined by the
Authorised Officer, he shall launch prosecution against the party under
Section 70(1) of the I.S.Act for suppression of the facts and circumstances
violating provisions under Section 27 of I.S.Act for imposing penalty
under Section 64 of Indian Stamp Act. The prosecution must be launched
not later than 90 days from the day of inspection wherever required.

The attention of the Authorised Officers in the State is invited to the

of the value and the deficit amount determined, the Authorised Officer has to
launch prosecution against the party under Section 70 (1) of the Indian Stamp
Act for the suppression of facts and circumstances violating provisions under
Section 27 of Indian Stamp Act within 90 days from the date of inspection.

Though clear instructions were issued in the matter, certain instances
have been noticed by the Commissioner & I.G., wherein the Authorised Officers
have failed in launching prosecutions against the parties who have not turned
up for the payment of the deficit amount detected. This shows not only the
inaction and negligence of the officers who inspected the properties in the
Post Facto spot inspections but also becoming responsible for failure to collect
the revenues due.

In view of the above position, all the Authorised Officers in the State are
hereby informed that stringent disciplinary action will be initiated against the
officers who are responsible for cases of undervaluations getting time-barred
for launching prosecution due to failure in launching prosecution against the
parties within 90 days from the date of spot inspection.

Sub: Inspection of properties under Section 27 of I.S.Act Rules issued - Post
Facto Inspections - Limits of values of properties enhanced - Instructions
issued- Regarding.

Ref: 1) G.O.Ms. No.34 Rev (Reg-I) Department, dt.8.1.1999

2) This Office Memo No. MV 2/22407/98, Dated 22.1.1999
seloreke

ORDER :

Section 27 of I.S.Act prescribed statutory obligation on the parties to the
document to declare truly and correctly the facts affecting chargeability of the
document with stamp duty. Prior to 1999, the registering officers used to verify
the compliance to the above section after spot inspection of property in the
document before registration.

However, in view of the implementation of CARD project and to adhere
to the time frame of "Registration of document in 1 hour", fixed in the Citizen
Charter, pre-registraion spot inspection of properties were totally dispensed
with and post-facto spot inspections (after registration and return of the
documents) were introduced for the documents with value over and above the
limits fixed as Rs.1.5 lakhs in Panchayats, Rs.3 lakhs in Municipalities and
Rs.5 lakhs in MCH. For the last 5 years the scheme had been implemented
which resulted in quick delivery of documents to the parties and also in some
cases lot of trouble to the authorised officers in locating the properties, in
completing all the inspections of properties above the limit and collecting the
deficit amounts with three times of deficit stamp duty as penalty or launching
prosecution in many cases due to nonpayment of the deficit amounts.

Hence, with a view to streamline the scheme and to use the services of
limited number of authorised officers in a better way to detect cases with respect
Market Value Scheme - Post Facto spot Inspections 481

to High value documents, enchancing the limits of value of properties (fixed in
the year 1999) is considered as inevitable, as the values of the properties also
escalated due to the periodical revision of Guidelines values and structure rates,
during the last fives, Hence, it is felt as a workable arrangement to fix up the
limit of Rs.3 lakhs for Panchayats Rs.5 lakhs for Municipalities Rs.7 lakhs for
Municipal Corporations other than MCH and Rs.10 lakhs for Municipal
Corporation of Hyderabad.

All the authorised officers are hereby directed to inspect all the urban
properties structures & buildings (excluding Apartments) with the value of
Rs.10 lakhs and above in Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad, Rs.7 lakhs and
above in all other Municipal Corporations, Rs.5 lakhs and above in all
Municipalities and Rs.3 lakhs and above in Panchayaths in the Sub-Registrar
Offices allotted to them by the D.LG. concerned.

3 (F) Circular Memo No. MV 1/9758/2005, Dated 29.07.2005 of the
C & IGRS, Hyderbad

Sub: Indian Stamp Act 1899 - Prevention of under valuation - Application of
rider rates - certain instructions - pre-registration spot inspection of
documents valued as per rider rates - Regarding

Ref: 1) C &1G's. Circular Memo No. MV 1/4856/2005, dt.19.03-2005
2) C & L.G's. Circular Orders in Peshi, dt.18.06-2005

sesoiedok:

It is observed that in some registrations involving the application of rider
rates, large scale loss of revenues to the State Exchequer is being reported on
account of the parties misinforming the factors effecting the chargeability to
stamp duty like correct door number, locality, classification (residential /
commercial / or dry / wet), location etc. The Registering Officers are not ina
position to arrest this leakage of revenue due to the fact that there are multiple
rider rates in the same Ward and Block / Village, on account of pre-registration
inspection of properties having despensed with and of mechanical acceptance
of erroneous particulars furnished by the parties in unsuspecting manner by
them, as well.
Market Value Scheme - Post Facto spot Inspections 483

In order to ensure the norm of one property one rate, it is being examined
whether the Market Value Revision Committee may be advised to fix up the
highest rate in Ward - Block / Village as the single rider rate or the programming
under CARD project may be made to take only the highest Ward and Block /
Village as rider rate. Pending a considered decision on the matter it has been
decided to provide for pre-registration spot inspection of properties by the
Registering Officers where recourse to rider rates is made in documents
presented for registration and accordingly the following instructions are issued
to prevent loss of revenue to the State Exchequer by misapplication of rider
rates.

1. All the Registering Officers before whom documents involving
the application of rider rates is made to the properties contained
therein shall keep such documents pending and conduct spot
inspection of such properties within twenty four (24) hours of
presentation of such documents before they are admitted for
registration.

2. The Registering Officers should as far as possible conduct pre-
registration spot inspection in the presence of Executant / Claimant
or their Representatives and a S.A / J.A of that office. The
inspection report should be drawn up with the signature of the
Sub-Registrar and the S.A/J.A and filed document wise in separate
miscellaneous file labelled as "Pre-Registration Spot Inspection
File" duly numbering each page serially upto 500 pages.

3. “Authorised Officers" for post facto spot inspection allotted to a
Registration Office will go through the pre-registration spot
inspection file and proceed to verify properties covered by all
documents registered with values lower than the higher Ward -
Block / Village rate.

4. The Registering Officers will personally be held responsible for
deficits arising due to improper or incorrect application of rider
rates and all such deficits will be included in the N.D.C of the
errant Registering Officer, and come entail disciplinary action under
APCS (CC&A) Rules, 1991.
484 AP Stamp (POU) of instruments Rules 1975

4, RULES FRAMED UNDER THE INDAIN STAMP ACT, 1899
(ANDHRA PRADESH AMENDMENT) Act, XXII of 1971

Rules Under Section 47- A

(G. O. Ms. No. 1031, Revenue (U-2), 315" July 1975.)
(G. O. Ms. No. 997, Revenue (U ), 14" Aug. 1975.)
(G. O. Ms. No. 191, Revenue (U), 11" Feb. 1982.)
(A.P.Gazette R.S to Part ii, 7" Aug. 1975. Page 800)

In exercise of the Powers conferred by Section 47-A and 75 of the
Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Central Act No.2 of 1899) the Governor of Andhra
Pradesh, herebty make the following rules

Rules

1 Short title and commencement —

(1) These rules may be called the Andhra Pradesh Stamp (Prevention
of undervaluation of Instruments) Rules, 1975.

(2) They shall come into force on the 16" August 1975.
2. Definition — In these rules unless the context otherwise requires-
(a) “Act” means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Act No.2 of 1899);

(b) “‘Authorised agent” means a person holding a power of attorney
authorising him to act on behalf of his principal:

(c) “Form” means a form appended to these rules;

(d) “Registering officer means the Registering Officer appointed under
the Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act XVI of 1908);
(e) “Section” means a section of the Act.

3. Furnishing of statement of market value — (1) if an instrument related
to a number of items of property, the market value shall be specified in
respect of each item separately. For this purpose, the party executing
the document shall attach a separate statement to the instrument,
furnishing therein information about the various items of properties
involved and his own assessment of the market value of each of those
items separately.

Explanation 1:-If, an instrument covers lands, comprising several survey
numbers or sub-division numbers, the market value shall be specified in
respect of the land covered by each survey number or sub-division
number, as the case may be separately.

Explanation 2:-(1) If an instrument relates to only one item of property
and that property is a building, or if an instrument related to more than
AP Stamp (POU) of instruments Rules 1975 485
one item of property and one or more such items is or are a building or
buildings , the particulars mentioned in the Annexure to these rules shall
be furnished in respect of the building or each of such buildings as the
case may be.

(2) The registering officer shall, before registering an instrument, satisfy
himself that the party has enclosed to the instrument a statement, giving
the market value in respect of each of the properties separately, as required
by sub-rule (3) and Explanations 1 and 2 above.

(3) The registering officer may., for the purpose of satisfying himself whether
the market value or the consideration has been correctly furnished in
the instrument or not, make such enquiries, as he may deem fit. He may
elicit from the parties concerned any information having a bearing on
the subject and call for and examine any records kept with any Public
Officer or authority.

Note

Section 47-A applies to conveyances, sales, exchanges, gifts, partitions,
settlements, releases, agreement relating to construction, development
or sale of any immovable property or power of attorney given for saleor
development of immovable property (sub-section 1 of Section 47-A with
effect from 23.4.1998 = Act No. 8 of 1998)

Case Law

Determination of market value of property for purpose of registration,
Registering Authority cannot refuse to register a document solely on the basis
that the market value stated in the document is not in accordance with the rate
shown in Basic value guidelines register - Rules in the said register are only a
piece of relevant material which has to be taken into account along with the
other relevant materials

Party agrivated by the action of the Registering Authority in refusing to
register a document on the ground of undervaluation cannot straight away come
to the High Court invoking Writ jurisdiction without exhausting statutory
remedies provided under Section 47A of the Act [APHC Judgment dated 4-6-
2002 - Writ Appeal Nos.458 and 459 of 1990 = 2002 (6) ALT 180 (DB)]

(4) If the Registering Officer is of the opinion that the market value of the
property affected by the instrument is not correctly furnished, he shall
keep the document pending and without delay refer the matter to the
Collector with details of his assessment of the Market Value arrived at
by him in the Form. I. No copy of such document shall be granted
notwithstanding anything contained in any of the provisions of any other
Act or Rules.

Procedure on receipt of a reference under Sub-Section (1) of section

47-A.

On receipt of a reference under Sub-Section (1) of Section 47-A,

accompanied by a statement in Form I from a registering officer the

Collector shall issue a notice in Form II.

(a) Toevery person by whom, and

(b) Toevery person in whose favour the instrument has been executed
informing him of the receipt of the reference and asking him to
submit to him in writing his representation, if any, to show that the
market value of the property or the consideration thereof has been
truly setforth in the instrument, and also to produce all evidence
that he has in support of his representation within twnety one days
from the date of service of the notice.

(c) The Collector shall also maintain office-wise register of references
received from each registering officer in Form V

The Collector may, if he thinks fit, record a statement from the person to

whom a notice under sub-rule (1) has been issued.

The Collector may for the purpose of his enquiry-

(a) Call for any information or record a statement from any Public
officer or an officer or authority under the Government or any
local Authority:

(b) Examine and record statements from any member of the public,
an officer or authority under the Government or the local Authority:
and

(c) Inspect the property after due notice to the parties concerned.

After considering the representations, if any, received from the person

to whom notices,under sub-rule (1) has been issued, and after examining

the records and evidence before him, the Collector shall pass an order in
writing determining the “market value” of the properties or the
consideration and the duty payable. The basis on which the market value
or consideration was determined shall be clearly indicated in the order.

Principles for the determination of the market value or

consideration: The Collector shall, as far as possible, have also regard

to the follawing points in determining the market value or consideration,

Case Law

Rule 5 of A.P.Stamp (prevention of undervaluation of instruments) Rules
1975 provide GUIDE LINES for determination of market value of the
properties. The market value of the property shall have to be determined
based on the likely sale value of the property in the OPEN MARKET
AT THE TIME OF EXECUTION [APHC Judgment dated 2-5-2003 in
W.P. No.5025 of 2003 and Batch = 2003 (4) ALT 735]

The Market Value of the property is what the property would fetch in
open market on the date of execution of the document. [Sub-Regisrar,
Banjarahills, Hyderbad Vs Damodar Reddy 1997 (5) ALT 187 (DB)]
“Omitted”. (G.O.Ms.No.191 Rev (V) dated 11-2-1982)

Final order determining the market value or consideration:-

1) The Collector shall after considering the representation received
in writing and those urged at the time of hearing and after careful
consideration of all the relevant factors and evidence placed before
him, pass an order, determining the market value of the properties
or the consideration thereof and the duty payable on the instrument,
the time within which the deficit amount of stamp duty shall be
paid, communicate the order to the parties and take steps to collect
the deficient amount of stamp duty, if any.

2) The Collector shall, after receipt of the reference under sub-
section(1) of section 47-A, dispose of the case expeditiously.

3) A copy of the order shall be communicated to the registering
officer concerned for his record.

4) If the parties to the document.-fail to prefer an appeal within 2
months under rule 9 from the date of the receipt of Collector’s
orders under rule 7, or fail to pay the deficit stamp duty or such

Appearance through advocate or authorised agent —

In any enquiry under these rules, any party to an instrument may appear

either in person or through an advocate or an authorised agent.

Appeals —

An appeal under Sub-Section (4) of section 47-A of the Act shall be
preferred to the appellate authority within two months from the date of

receipt of the Collector’s order determining the market value or
consideration under rule 7.

The appeal shall contain the following particulars, namely:-

(a) Full name, father’s name or husband’s name, occupation and
address of the applicant.

(b) Full name, father’s name, or husband’s name, occupation and
° address of every person executing the instrument;

(c) Full name, father’s name, or husband’s name, occupation and
address of every person claiming under the instrument;

(d) Date and nature of the instrument;

(e) Registration number, date of registration and name of office where
the instrument was registered;

(f) Name of town or village in which the property is situate together
with the name of the taluk and the registration sub-district.

(g) Number and date of Collector’s order appealed against;

(h) Market value of the property or the consideration as setforth in the
document.

(i) | Market valne of the property or the consideration as determined
by the Collector.

Every appeal shall be accompanied by-

(a) The original or a certified copy of the order appealed against;
(b) The original or a certified copy of the instrument; and

(c) Memo of grounds of appeal.

Every appeal shall be presented in person or by an advocate or an
authorised agent or sent by registered post to the appellate authority
having jurisdiction, which shall endorse the date of receipt.
490 AP Stamp (POU) of instruments Rules 1975

10. Procedure for the disposal of appeals:-
(1) If an appeal is admitted by the appellate authority a date shall be
fixed for hearing the appeal. The appellate authority shall issue a
notice to the appellant informing him of the date on which and the
time and place at which the appeal shall be heard. Such notice
Shall also state that if the appellant does not appear on the day so
fixed or any other day to which the hearing may be adjourned, the .
appeal shall be liable to be dismissed for default or disposed of on
merits ex-party.
(2) The appellate authority shall send a copy of the notice to the
- Collector together with copy of the appeal and obtain the records
of the case form the Collector
11. Hearing of the appeal:-

On the date fixed or on any other date to which the case may be
adjourned, the appellate authority shall hear the appellant and receive
any evidence adduced on his behalf. It shall also hear the person, if any,
appearing on behalf of the Collector and receive the evidence, if any
adduced in support of the Collector’s order.

12. Order in appeal: -

(1) After considering all the evidence adduced and representations
made on behalf of the appellant and the Collector and examining
the records of the case, the appellate authority shall decide whether
or not the market value of the properties or the consideration
thereof, as determined by the Collector under sub-section (2) or
sub-section (3) of section 47-A is correct. In case, the appellate
authority does not accept the valuation of the properties or the
consideration determined by the Collector it shall determine the
correct market value of the properties or the consideration and the
duty payable on the instrument. The appellate authority shall
embody its decision and the reasons thereof in an order and
communicate it to the appellant, the Collector and the registering
officer concerned.

(2) After receipt of the orders issued by the Appellate authority under
Sub-Section (4) of Section 47-A, if the parties fail to pay deficit
stamp duty if any, or if such deficit stamp duty is not recovered by
coercive process under section 48, the Registering Officer shall
destroy the document after 5 years from the date of the orders of
the Collector under Sub-Section (2) of Section 47-A

(3) If any officer by conducting spot inspection or otherwise detects
that a document is under-valued and reports to the Collector with

Return of records to Collector:-

As soon as may be after the order is passed under rule 12, the appellate
authority shall return to the Collector the records obtained from him

A (4) Circular Memo No. MV 1/14112/98, Dated 26.06.2000 of the
C& IGRS, Hyderbad

Sub: M.V.Scheme - Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act - Test check of the
records by Accountant General Audit Party pertaining to cases referred
to Collectors under Section 47-A during 1997-98 - Certain instructions
- Issue of - Regarding.

RR

During August 1977 to May 1998, the Accountant General's Audit Party
had conducted test check of the records relating to M.V. of properties referred
to Collectors under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act, in the office of the
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, Office of
the Deputy Inspector General, Kurnool and 9 District Registrar Offices to assess
the effectiveness of the implementation of the provisions regarding fixation of
Market Values, levy and Collection of proper Stamp Duty payable thereon. In
the said audit, the following defects are noticed in implementing the provisions
of Section 47-A of the said Act.

A. a) Delay in disposal of references by Collectors under Section 47-A.
b) —Non-collection of deficit Stamp duty already determined.

c) — Large variations between the Market Values reported by Registering
Officers and those determined by the Collectors and Nonadherence
to principles laid down for determining the market value.

d) Delay in referring the cases by the Registering Officers to the
Collector

e) Improper maintenance of prescribed Registers and Non-
reconciliation of number of cases referred by the Registering
Officers and received by the Collector

f) Pending cases not yet received by the Collector from Revenue
Authorities.

B. (a) According to Rule 7(2) of A.P.Stamp Rules, 1975, the Collector
under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act shall after receipt of the
references under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act from the
Registering Officers dispose of the cases expeditiously by
determining the values of the properties correctly and stamp duty
payable thereon. But the Accountant General during his test check
of the records found that 161650 cases (both Pre and Post) involving
Rs.4204.16 lakhs are pending for disposal upto March, 1977. As
per the reports submitted by the Collectors, upto March, 1999 only
2024 cases (both Pre and Post) involving an amount of Rs.170.54
502 Market Value Scheme - Section 47A Cases (Instructions)

(b)

Cc)

lakhs have been disposed leaving the balance of 159626 cases (both
Pre and Post) involving Rs.4033.62 lakhs and submit compliance
accordingly every month.
Non-collection of deficit stamp duty in determined cases :
According to Rule 7(1) of A.P.Stamp Rules, 1975,(POURules, 1975 supra)
the Collector shall (i) pass an order determining the M.V. of the instruments
(ii) communicate the orders to the parties and (iii) take steps to collect
the deficit amount of stamp duty if any. If the party fails to pay the
stamp duty as determined by the Collector and not prefering an appeal to
the Appellate Court within 2 months, the next course of action is to proceed
under Section 48 of Indian Stamp Act to recover the deficit amount by
distress and sale of movable property of the person from whom the
amounts are due or by any other process in force for the recovery of the
arrears of land revenue.
Large variations between the Market Values reported by the
Registering Officers and those determined by the Collectors and
non-adherence to principles laid down in determining the Market
Values :

While determining the Market Value of properties or consideration, the
Collector has to follow the principles laid down in Rule 5 of A.P.Stamp
Rules, 1975 (POU Rules) and shall have regard to such points as
classification of land, nearness. to roads, location, developmental
activities, land tax and valuation of sites with reference to taxation records
of local authorities concerned.

Besides the above, in this office Memo No. MV 1/17239/91, dt.29.7.91
certain guidelines have been issued to all the District Registrars acting
as Collectors under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act to follow while
disposing of references by the Collectors. Those instructions were
reiterated in the year 1996 & 1997. Again through I.G's Memo No. MV
1/24202/97, dt.31.10.97, keeping in view the large variations between ~
the Market Values reported by Registering Officers and those determined
by the Collecots, all the Collectors, were directed to discuss invariably
the following points in the orders passed by them as Collectors while
disposing of cases under Section 47-A.

1) Complete schedule of the property effected with consideration.

2) Value as per M.V.Guidelines and the reasons putforth by the S.R.
in Form-I for referring the document under Section 47-A.

3) The points putforth by the party for not paying the stamp duty as
per value calculated by the S.R / Market Value Guidelines Register,
through his representation and evidence produced thereof.
Market Value Scheme - Section 47A Cases (Instructions) 503
4) Inspection of the property by the Collector - Land use, distance
from the main village/ town, local enquiries regarding value.

5) Enquiries with the Revenue Officials including local Revenue
Officials.

6) Whether verified Pattadar Pass Books and connected Revenue
records.

7) _ Particulars of previous transactions in three preceeding consecutive
years of the same property or similar properties situated or adjacent
to or in the vicinity of such property.

8) Examination and consideration of the values of adjacent land or
lands.

9) Prevailing value, and the value it would have secured if placed in
an open auction, may also be furnished, the value considered in
land acquisition cases, if any, may also be taken into account.

D)Delay in referring cases by the Registering Officer to Collectors

As per Rule (4) of A.P.Stamp (Prevention of under valuation of
instruments) Rules, 1975, if the Registering Officer is of the opinion that the
Market Value of the property effected by the instrument is not truly setforth, he
shall keep the document pending and without delay refer the matter to the
Collector for the determination of the Value.

In the Citizen Charter formulated for Registration and Stamps Department,
atime limit of 5 working days is prescribed for making a reference to Collector
under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act. Hence all the District Registrars are
requested to see that cases are referred under Section 47-A within the said
period of 5 working days (both for offices covered by CARD Project and not
covered by CARD Project) from the S.R.Os concerned and dispose of the cases
expeditiously by determining the value of the property and stamp duty payable
thereon. If any delay is noticed in referring the documents, the concerned
registering officer may be awarded exemplary punishment.

E) Improper maintenance of Prescribed Registers And Non Rec-
onciliation of Number of Cases Referred by the Registering Of-
ficer And Received by the Collectors

According to Rule 3(5) and 4(1) of A.P.Stamp (Prevention of under
valuation of instruments) Rules, 1975, every Registering Officer has to niaintain
a register of reference to the Collectors under Section 47-A of I.S.Act in Form-
IV to watch their disposal and the Collector has to maintain office-wise Register
of references received from each SRO in Form-V under his jurisdiction.

In this connection all the District Registrars are requested to follow the
504 Market Value Scheme - Section 47A Cases (Instructions)
instructions, verify the Registers (Form -IV) maintained by the Registering
Officers of his jurisdiction regularly once in a quarter and ensure that they are
maintaining the register promptly and upto date. Similarly they shall maintain
the Register (Form-V) upto date in his office and get reconciled the number of
cases received by him with the cases referred by the Registering Officers of his
district and he is responsible for prompt maintenance of both registers at Sub-
Registrar Offices and his office.

Attention of the District Registrars / Collectors under Section 47-A is
invited to the subject cited. During the course of review of 47-A disposals it is
noticed by the undersigned that many of the D.Rs as 47-A Collectors are not
following the rules prescribed to follow wiuiie disposing the cases. In futherance
to the Prevention of Undervaluation Rules 1975, the following instructions
are issued for strict compliance while disposing the cases and while issuing
the proceedings.

1) DR. should prepare a location sketch clearly indicating the land /
property in question, the existing habitation, land marks in the
vicinity if any and also the road adjacent to the property

2) — Ifroad is mentioned in the location sketch, the width of the road is
also to be clearly stated in the location sketch as well as in the
proceedings.

3) The transactions that took place in the vicinity of land (for which
disposal is being given) have to be mentioned with details.

4) ~The layouts if any, already approved in the vicinity of the iand or
the lands purchased for the purpose of layout have to be
clearly mentioned in the proceedings.

5) If there are any lands / properties that are sold in the vicinity of
land / property in question, the same should also be discussed in
the proceedings.

6) Principles prescribed in Rule 5 for determination of the market
value have to be followed.
