ORDER :

It has come to the notice of Commissioner & Inspector General (R&S)
that several cases are lying pending for determination of Market Value under
Section 47-A, on the plea that there are instructions not to disregard the guideline
values at the time of disposal of cases under Section 47-A referred by the Sub-
Registrars, This inaction on the part of the Authority vested with delegated
powers to determine the Market Value under Section 47-A within the time
limits of (2) months as fixed in the Citizen Charter, which causes lot of public
hardship due to non disposal of pending documents. Some of the District
Registrars have been playing appreciative active role for the disposal of pending
cases after getting the matter finalised by the Anomalies rectification Committee
which is statutorily constituted under the A.P.Market Value Guidelines rules
1998.

After careful examination of the statutory powers under Section 47-A
and revision of M.V.Rules 1998, it is felt desirable to get all pending cases
under Section 47-A, in cases where more than 20% to be disregarded by way
of diference in market value guidelines such cases to be referred to the Anomilies
rectification Committee and dispose off the cases as per the opinion / uecision
of the Anomilies Rectification Committee.

All the District Registrars are instructed to list out such pending cases
(more than 20% M.V.guideline value) Village / Town wise and take steps to
dispose of not less than 50 cases per month and report the progress in disposing
the cases every month.

level without making any kind of reference regarding valuation to the
Commissioner & Inspector General (R&S). The District Registrars should
closely follow the instruction contained in the reference 2nd cited annexed
and pass speaking determination orders in the light of valuation disclosed by
Index-II particulars of subject / adjacent properties. The District Registrars
are free to gather information from any source like Government / Court
auctions, compensation paid in land acquisition cases or seek advice from
Anomalies Rectification Committee, but in no case these values should be
sent to the prior approval of the Commissioner & Inspector General (R&S) as
prejudging of any value by a revision authority is not conducive to principles
of natural justice.

All the Deputy Inspectors General should obtain the determination orders
from the District Registrars working under their control and review them
critically at their level on or before 15th of every succeeding month as per the
procedure prescribed in the reference 2nd cited, The Deputy Inspectors Generai
should send detailed proposals for suo moto revision by the Commissioner &
Inspector General (R&S) of the determined cases where any unjustified
disregard is noticed in the orders of any Collectur (D.R) within two (2) months
from the date of passing of the order by the District Registrars.

The Collectors (D.Rs) are further informed that any loss of revenue arising
in their determination orders will be included in their N.D.C's besides initiating
stringent disciplinary action under APCS (C.C&A) Rules, 91 by even

promptly and become liable for all consequences out of delays in their submission

reasons.

When the Registering Officer takes a decision to make a reference to the
Collector under Section 47-A in respect of a document, in which the value
setforth by the party is found to be less than the Market Value prevailing as per
the Market Value Guidelines, he should identify and select latest registered
transactions with equal or higher rates in the first instance and if they are not
available, he can select the registered transactions at least for past 3 years for
similar properties adjacent to the affected property with full details and furnish
against column 11 of form - I as per Rule 4,

The full details for this purpose : -

(@__ incase of Agricultural land, the particulars of document No. / year
/ date of execution, Survey No. (Wet or Dry), extent, consideration
/ Market Value per acre.

(ID Incase of site involved, the details of Ward No. Name of the locality
/ Street and rate per Sq. Yard.

All these details should be furnished invariably to the Collector under
Section 47-A. While doing so care must be taken to select and furnish only
such latest or past registered transactions which are quite relevant and found to
be in conformity with or higher of the Market Values adopted by the Registering
Officer in the reference. If the time lag or interval period between the past
registered transaction and the present transaction is too long the Registering
Officer have to explain as to how the Market Value has increased during this
intervening period. Such details have to be necessarily indicated in column 11
of Form-I in support of the Market Value of the property worked out and
508 Market Value Scheme - Section 47A Cases (Instructions)

mentioned by him against col.8 of Form-1.

If the Market Value assessed by a Registerin : Officer in respect of a
document is supported by the latest or past registered transactions there will be
either no scope or very less scope to the Collector under Section 47-A for
disregarding the Market Value assessed by the Registering Officer, because
the Collector under Section 47-A is bound to examine and look into the
registered transactions furnished by the Registering Officer in support of his
value of the property before determining the Market Value of the property
under Section 47-A and again the Collector will be constrained to give cogent
reasons for disregarding the Market Value or discarding any of the registered
transactions furnished to him as irrelevant.

Against Col.8 of Form-1 the Registering Officer should not use the words
"Basic Recister VALue" but specifically mention that the value of the property
has been assessed as per the Market Value prevailing in the concerned area.

A certificate is prescribed to be added by the Registering Officer to the
effect that past transactions and other relevant statistical data is furnished to
the Collector under Section 47-A along with the reference under the section.
This fact has to be reported along with Report of Progress of Work as an
enclosure every month to the District Register. The following is the certificate
prescribed.

“Certified that I have personally verified and satisfied myself that the
particulars of past transactions and other necessary information as envisaged
under sub-rule (3) and (4) of Rule-3 of 1975 Rules (POU Rules, 1975 supra)
have been duly furnished to the Collector under Section 47-A of Indian Stamp
Act in respect of all the documents referred to under Section 47-A of Indian
Stamp Act”

This aspect has to be verified by the District Registrars during the annual
inspection by incorporating it as an item in the Inspection Report. Any deviation
to the instruction, when noticed during the inspection of Registrar Office by
the Inspector General, will be viewed seriously.
Market Value Scheme - Case Law under section 47A 509

6.CASE LAW UNDER SECTION 47-A OF INDIAN STAMP ACT,

1,

1899
Sale deed executed by Court

Sale deed was executed through Court in a suit for specific performance
of contract which was decreed. The Registering Officer is required to

. consider the value setforth under the Rules and refer the instrument to

the Collector. (2004(i) ALT 14.3 (DN.OHC]
Stamp duty only on bid amount in Court auction:

When a sale deed in respect of which stamp duty and registration fee are
paid on the bid amount in Court auction the Collector has no power
to enquire under Section 47-A and determine the market value of the
property disclosed in the sale deed (1998 (6) ALT 604).

Section 47-A - Applicability:

Jurisdiction of Registering Officer to refer the matter to Collector for
determination of market value operative only when he has reason to
believe that consideration amount reflected in the instrument is not truly
setforth. Section 47-A is not applicable to a case where sale amount is
genuinely shown in sale deed though it is less than the market value.
Residential plot of land allotted by Housing Board to petitioner, price
fixed at Rs.400/- per sq.yard upheld by the High Court. Same value
reflected in sale deed. No reason to believe that the said value is not true
value. Reference made by Sub-Registrar to Collector is without
jurisdiction. Issuing notice by Collector fixing the value of land at
enhanced price of Rs.1400/- per sq.yard and levying stamp duty thereon.
Not legal and liable to be quashed. Invoking of jurisdiction by Sub-
Registrar under Section 47-A. Erroneous (1991(4) ALT 626; 1998(2)

~ APLJ 101; 1998 ALT (Rey) 691).

Market value of lands adjacent:

Market value fixed by Registering authorities a few months earlier and
the same fixed a few months later based on the Basic Value Register
without any other supporting documentary evidence and disregarding
the valuation fixed a few months earlier and based on local enquiries
from persons who have neither sold nor purchased lands. Constitute
error of law warranting interference exercising power of judicial review
(1997(3) ALT 808).

Guideline value of property:

Guideline values has relevance only in the context of Section 47-A of
the Indian Stamp Act. It is not final but only indicates a ‘primafacie' rate
prevailing in the area of ascertaining correct market value of the property
disclosed in an instrument requiring payment of stamp duty. The
510

Market Value Scheme - Case Law under section 47A

2)

8)

9)

guideline value is a rate fixed by the authorities under the Stamp Act for
purpose of determining the true market value of the property.(2004(2)
SCC 9)

Market value - Determination as on the date of document:

(i) The market values of the property shall have to be determined
based on the likely sale value of the property in the open market at
the time of execution of the instrument (2003(4) ALT 735)

(ii) Sale under Article 47-A. Equating a registered agreement of sale
with sale cannot be done for the purpose of Section 47-A of the
Stamp Act. Market value at the time of execution of sale deed is
to be taken for purpose of duty.(2002(i) An.WR 420 AP).

(iii) Sale deed executed pursuant to decree in a suit for specific
performance of agreement of sale. Stamp duty payable be
calculated on the market value of the property prevailing on the
date of execution of sale deed and not at the rate prevailing at the
time of execution of agreement for sale [2002 (6) ALT 144 (DB)]

(iv) Also vide S.No.14 below

Computation of value of house property on the basis of rental value:

Computation of value of house property for levying stamp duty and
registration charges. Multiple of 18 years of rental value adopted by
Sub-Registrar is quite reasonable. Guideline issued for adopting a
particular multiplier have no statutory force [1993 (1) ALT 582 (DB)]}

Stamp duty where the value mentioned in Court judgements and
decree :

Market value of the subject matter of an instrument undervalued as per
the Registering Authority - Judgment and decree of Civil Court
mentioning market value of property to be taken a correct value and
stamp duty paid thereon. Direction given to Registering Authority to
register the sale deed presented in favour of petitioner taking into account
the consideration mentioned in the judgement and decree of the Civil
Court [Amareswary Venkateswar versus Sub-Registrar Badvel - 1998(3)
An W.R.259; 1989 (3) ALT 677 followed]

Purchase of land in Public Auction :

Purchase of land and building for rupees 5 lakhs along with plant and
machinery for rupees 20 lakhs in a public auction held by APSFC.
Obtaining sale deed only in respect of land and building by paying stamp
duty on the purchase value of Rs 5 Lakhs. Notice issued calling upon for
payment of deficient stamp duty on the difference value of rupees 20
lakhs and proposal to refer the matter to the Collector on refusal to pay.
Market Value Scheme - Case Law under section 47A 511

10)

11)

No undervaluation . Value correctly indicated. Matter cannot be referred
to the Collector. Availability of alternative remedy of challenging the
order of the Collector by way of an appeal before the competent Civil
Court is not lone ground for driving the parties from pillar to post to
satisfy the whims and fancies of the authorities and the authorities cannot
go scot-free with their fanciful actions.[Sri Bharatia Pulvarisers (P) Ltd,
Adilabad Vs Sub-Registrar of Assurances, Asifabad (1997 (6) ALT 801
= 1998 (1) LS 67)]

Agricultural lands - valuation :

Sale deeds - Agricultural lands - Potential value and possibility of land
being used as house sites in future - Not relevant factors. Valuation
made in conformity with valuation of adjacent agricultural lands
represents the market value on that date, Revaluation under Section 47-
A not required. Direction given to accept the said valuation and register
the documents.{Maddula Nagasiromani, Maddula Ramakrishna Rao Vs.
Subordinate Judge, Kovvur (1996 (1) ALT 3350]

Delays in Execution of Sale deeds by Courts :

Delay due to cumbersome legal procedures : Agreement of Sale - Specific
performance- Vendees performed their part of the agreement. Vendor
refused to execute sale deed. Delay occurred in execution of sale deeds
by Court due to cumbersome legal procedures. Vendees not responsible
for delay. Registering Officer cannot insist on vendees to pay stamp
duty on the market value of properties prevailing at the time of execution
of the sale deeds by Court because of such delay. Under Section 47-A
of the Act, Registering authority is empowered to hold an enquiry only
to satisfy himself whether the value of the property was truly shown in
the document or not i.e. whether the consideration paid by vendee to the
vendor is truly mentioned in the document or not or whether the
instrument was undervalued to avoid stamp duty. It is not the concern
of the Registering Authority to see whether market value of property as
given in the instrument is proper or correct. Nothing to show on facts
that the sale consideration shown in sale deeds is not true consideration
passed between the parties. Insistance to pay stamp duty on market
value of property as on the date of execution of sale deeds by Court
without conducting any enquiry as to whether consideration shown in
the instrument is true or not. Not justified. Direction given by the lower
Court to petitioner Sub-Registrar to register the sale deeds for the amount
shown therein. Not illegal (Sub-Registrar, Kodad Town and Mandal,
Nalgonda District Vs. Amaranaini Chitnna Venkata Rao (died) 1998(2)
ALT 457; AIR 1998 AP 252; 1987 (1) APLJ 131; 1989 (1) ALT 546;
1989 (3) ALT 677 and 1997(1) An W R 616 followed)
512

12.

13.

Market Value Scheme - Case Law under section 47A
Collector's orders determining value under Section 47-A -
Reasons to be furnished : Determination of value: Determination of
value of an instrument of conveyance for registration by the Collector on
reference by Registering Authority - No reasons assigned by Collector
in his order. Order is not legal.[B.Subramanyam Vs. RDO (1986 (2)
ALT 99 (NRC)]
Basic Value Register is not the sole basis for determination of
market Value : Market value of property : - Instrument of conveyance
- Market value determination. Value mentioned in the basic value register

* should not be the sole basis. What the property would fetch in the open

14,

15.

market on the date of execution of the instrument is the market
value of the property. [ Sub-Registrar, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad Vs.
Damodar Reddy 1997 (5) ALT 187(D.B)]

Value fixed by Government under Land Ceiling Act :

Condition imposed on the land owner by Government while granting
exemption under Land Ceiling Act not to dispose of excess land to a
named society at a price higher than the one fixed by it. Price so fixed
has nothing to do with the market price on which stamp duty is chargeable
under the Stamp Act. Registering Authorities have a statutory power to
determine the market value of property following the procedure under
Section 47-A of Stamp Act, keeping in view several circumstances
including basic value register. Price so determined will prevail over the
price fixed by the Government in exercise of delegated power under
Land Ceiling Act. Registering Authority is not bound by the value fixed
by parities or Government. Petitioner cannot insist on collection of stamp
duty only on the value fixed by the Government under Land Ceiling
Act. Refusal to register the sale deed unless stamp duty as fixed by the
Registering Authority is paid on the value arrived at by him. Sustainable.
If the party is aggrieved he has got right of appeal under the provisions
of Stamp Act.(Bhagya Lakshmi Co-op. Housing Society Ltd, Hyderabad
Vs. Sub-Registrar Bowenpally, Secunderabad Contonement,
Secunderabad (1998 (5) ALT 225; 1997 (5) ALT 187 (DB) followed)
Reference to the Collector under Section 47-A by keeping document
pending :

Registering officer has power to keep instrument presented for
registration pending and refer the matter to the Collector for determination
of market value if he is of opinion that the market value has not been
truly setforth in the instrument. For the limited purpose of forming such
opinion and taking action under Section 47-A, he can take the rates shown
in basic value register as relevant consideration though market value
Market Value Scheme - Case Law under section 47A 513

cannot be determined solely on the basis of said register. Fixation of
price of land by Government at Rs.35/- per sq.meter for its sale is nota
statutory determination.’ Such determination cannot limit power of
Registering Officer statutorily granted from taking action under Section
47-A of the Act and referring the matter to the Collector for determining
market value. Action of the Sub-Registrar in keeping the sale deed of
the Society pending adjudication by Collector under Section 47-A of
the Act is not illegal.(Vidyanagar Housing Cooperative Society Ltd,
Hyderabad Vs the State of Andhra Pradesh 1195 (1) ALT 620; AIR
1995 AP 223)

Third Party Objections :

Third party cannot question inadequacy of consideration in a sale
transaction on the ground that the sale consideration is not adequate or
that property is undervalued. Sale deed to be stamped as per market
value of property but not as per consideration fixed for sale. [Kavitha
Goud Vs. Nookala Sudarshan Reddy 2004 (5) ALT 293 (DB)]

Guidelines of the Authorities - Validity :

Consideration in an instrument : Section 47-A (i) as amended by
A.P.Amendment Act 17 of 1986 - Consideration in an instrument being
less than the value fixed by the Government in basic value register.
Refusal of Sub-Registrar to register the document on the basis of
instruction issued by Inspector General of Registration and Stamps. Not
legal. No statutory basis provided to basic value register is not enough
to show that the consideration is less than the market value - Case of
undervaluation to be shown [M/s. Sagar Cements Ltd Vs. State of A.P.
(1989(3) ALT 677)]
514 Market Value Scheme - Internal Audit System

7. INTERNAL AUDIT SYSTEM
(A) Procedure

Through Proceedings No.MV 3/5549/90,dt.12.11.1990, the Inspector
General of Registration and Stamps has prescribed the undermentioned
ptocedure to streamline the Internal Audit System in supersession of
the instruction issued earlier

1) Headquarters of the Audit Sub-Registrars shall be the Registrar's office
from where they shall function under the administrative control of the
Registrar concerned and their expenditure shall form part of Registrar's
budget.

2) Their audit programme shall be drawn by the District Registrar in the
last week of the succeeding month and communicated to the Sub-
Registrar (Internal Audit) well in advance, and the Registrar shall ensure
that the Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit) strictly adheres to the programme
so drawn. A copy of the programme shall be submitted to the Inspector
General and Deputy Inspector General concerned promptly without fail.

3) While drawing programme of the Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit), the
Registrars shall ensure that the backlog is covered first continuously
without fail.

4) The Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit) on completion of the audit of an
office shall prepare the audit report within 3 days and submit the same
to the District Registrar in duplicate. The Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit)
shall ensure to obtain the explanation of the Sub-Registrar against each
item remarked in the half-margin as is done by Accountant General's
audit party.

5) The audit must be effective and the remarks must be based on guidelines
issued from time to time from the Inspector General for assessing value
of the property and should not be whimsical and fanciful. It should not
be made based on their personal interpretations.

6) On receipt of the audit report from the Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit),
the District Registrar shall critically review the report within a week
and take prompt follow-up action to recover the loss, if any from the
concerned under Sec.41-A of the Indian Stamp Act. A copy of the
review shall also be sent to the Sub-Registrar concerned along with the
duplicate copy of audit report received from the Sub-Registrar (Internal
Audit)!

72) If the Registrar feels that the loss occurred was due to blatant negligence
of the Registering Officer for which disciplinary action is contemplated,
shall submit a special report against the Sub-Registrar concerned to the
Inspector General to be despatched in the name cover of the Special
Market Value Scheme - Internal Audit System 515

8)

9)

10)

lt)

12)

Officer (Market Value) with a copy to the Deputy Inspector General
concerned. Instructions as to the action to be taken against the Sub-
Registrar concerned shall be awaited from Inspector General.

The audit report shall be submitted by the Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit)
to the Deputy Inspector General in quadruplicate within (3) days after
completion of the audit for review, duly obtaining explanation of the
Sub-Registrar in the half-margin of the report.

The Deputy Inspector General on receipt of the audit report shall review
it critically within a week and communicate a copy ofthe review along
with audit report to the Registrar (Audit) / District Registrar concerned,
and to the Sub-Registrar concerned.

On receipt of review from the Deputy Inspector General the District
Registrar under whose jurisdiction the Sub-Registry office falls, shall
take immediate steps for recovery of deficit amount pointed out in the
review under Section 41-A of the Indian Stamp Act.

In order to review the performance of the Internal Audit Officers (Sub-
Registrar and District Registrar) and to assess the progress made in the
matter of collection of deficit stamp duty and registration fee a monthly
return in the form (vide Annexure-I) shall be submitted to the Inspector
General by the District Registrar, to be despatched in the name cover to
the Special Officer (Market Value) by Sth of succeeding month.

Maintenance of certain. registers to watch the progress in disposal
of audit paras and collection of deficit amount.

Every audit report must be assigned serial number to be terminated by
the end of the calendar year and every item remarked must be termed as
‘ Audit Para (I-A)'. The audit party must clearly write the audit para, on
the lines the Accountant General's audit party write remark showing as
to how the loss was caused which must be supported by the guidelines
issued from time to time by the Inspector General. The name of the
Sub-Registrar and Senior Assistant (Market Value) responsible for the
loss shall be written clearly under the remark.

Every Sub-Registrar (Internal Audit) and Registrar (Audit) shall maintain
a register called " Register of Internal Audit Report " in the proforma
(Annexure-II). Every audit report must be accounted for in this register.
All the previous audit reports should also be assigned serial numbers
and accounted for in this register. In every correspondence the number
of audit report and the number of audit para must be referred to. When
action is finalised against any audit para a suitable entry shall be made
in the audit report against the para and number of the para shall be rounded
off in red ink. When action on all the paras of the audit reports is finalised
516

B. INSTRUCTIONS
(.G's Memo No.MV 3/17548/91, dt.1.8.1991)

Internal Audit should be done as per the programme issued by concerned
District Registrar without any deviation.

A copy of the Tour programme of the Internal Audit staff should be
marked to the Vigilance Officer (R&S) concerned.

Concerned District Registrar / Sub-Registrar (Audit) should visit Sub-
Registry Office along with their staff and do the audit work as per the
programme and under no circumstances they should leave the audit work
to their staff alone.

Concerned Deputy Inspector General / District Registrar / Vigilance
Officer should personally ensure that the District Registrar / Sub-
Registrar (Audit) are present during the audit of Sub-Registrar Offices
as per the programme and make a special report to the Inspector-General
when any of them is found absent during his surprise visit to the Sub-
Registry Office. Officers from Inspector-General's Office will also be
deputed to see whether Internal Audit programme is being implemented
without any deviation.

The District Registrar / Sub-Registrar (Audit) and his staff should verify
50 documents per head per day in urban areas and in other areas the
documents to be verified should be100 per individual per day.

Audit notes should be prepared on the Accountant General Audit lines
with reference to particular Act / Rules and departmental guidelines and
on issue of half margin memos replies should be obtained from the Sub-
Registrar concerned on the same day.

Various registers prescribed in the Inspector General's guidelines should
be opened and maintained at various levels as per instructions.
Review of audit reports by the Deputy Inspector General / District
Registrars should be prompt and there should not be any delay in
communication of reviews to concemed officers.

The Internal Audit relating to the officers where the regular Sub-Registrar
is ripe for transfer or due to retire should be completed at least 3 months
in advance to the probable date of transfer / date of retirement and final
order should be passed on all the items at least 2 months in advance to
the date of relief of the Sub-Registrar.

Old Audit Reports pending with District Registrars and Audit District
Registrar should be given topmost priority. Action should be finalised
by ordering recoveries from the parties or taking action against the
persons responsible for revenue losses.

1.

The responsibility for answering the Internal Audit item, furnishing the
required information, initiating action for collection of the amount,
maintaining watch register of collection of the amount lies with the
regular Sub-Registrar whoever is present in the office. The Internal
Audit remarks relating to previous periods should not be neglected under
any circumstances. Time bound action should be taken on all the current
internal audit paras and recording of the para after taking final action
should be ensured within 3 months from the date of communication of
final orders in the review by the officer concerned. Periodical review
should be made to watch this aspect by all the Supervising Officers
(Assistant District Registrar, District Registrar, Vigilance Officer and

8. MARKET VALUE - REVISON
The A.P Revision of Market Value Guidelines Rules, 1998

[G. O. Ms. No. 301, Revenue (Registration I), dt. 4-5-1998]

In exercise of the powers conferred by section 47-A of the Indian

Stamp Act, 1899 (Central Act II of 1899) and of all other powers hereunto
enabling and in supersession of the Andhra Pradesh Revision of Market Value
Guidelines Rules, 1997 issued in G.O.Ms.No. 530, Revenue (Regn. I)
Department, dated 21* June, 1997, the Government of Andhra Pradesh hereby
makes the following rules:

1

2.

3.

Short title and commencement:— These rules may be called the
Andhra Pradesh Revision of Market Value Guidelines Rules, 1998.
(Published in A.P. Gazette Part - 1 extraordinary dated 4-05-1998)
Commencement :— They shall come into effect from the date of
publication of the rules in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette. (4-5-1998)
Definitions :— In these rules, unless the context otherwise, requires ~
(a) “Act” means the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 ( Act No. 2 of 1899) ;
(b) “Committee” means a committee constituted under these Rules ;
(c) “Format” means formats appended to these Rules ;

(d) “Market Value Guidelines” means the set of values of
immovable properties in different villages, municipalities,
Corporations and other local areas in the state, arrived at by the
respective Committees, from time to time in terms of these Rules
and incorporated in the registers prescribed.

(e) “Registering Officer” means the Registering Officer appointed
under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act XVI of 1908).
Market Value Scheme - Revision of M.V. Guidelines Rules 1998 523

 

4, (1) Central Valuation Advisory Committee :— (i) A Central
Valuation Advisory Committee with the following composition shall be
constituted to evolve general or specific guidelines from time to time for revision
of Market values for the use of the committees constituted under Rule 4 (2) :
Chairman :— Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps.
Members :— (1) Secretary to Commissioner of land Revenue ;

(2) Commissioner and Director of Agriculture ;

(i) Joint Inspector General of Registration and Stamps
o/o The Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps
(ii) The following shall be the terms of reference of the committee:-

(a) to evolve guidelines for the fixation of market values in respect of
different categories of land like agricultural land, urban land, Industrial
Area, Mining, Plantation, Commercial, non-agricultural land etc.

(b)  tocollect information in connection with achieving the above objective

(c) To undertake tours within the state as may be required for evolving the
Guidelines.

(iii) The Central Valuation Advisory Committee shall consult the following
organizations, registered bodies for obtaining their opinion on the growth
rate, market conditions, elasticity of demand and other factors relevant
for evolving general guidelines for the revision :

(1) Builders Forum, Hyderabad (Regd. No. 8628).

6. Procedure to prepare Market Value Guidelines Registers :— While
working out values of land and buidings, the Committee shall take into
account the established principles of valuation mentioned in Rule 5 of
the Andhra Pradesh Stamp (prevention of Undervaluation of Instruments)
Rules, 1975 and any other factors that they may deem necessary like
condition of real estate market, interest rates, and loaning activity of
Housing Finance Institutions/Banks, Inflation rates, price of building
material, Government policies on Town Planning, Building construction,
Urban Development and prices of Agricultural produce.

7. Formats for the Registers :— The formats for the registers of Market
Value Guidelines pertaining to Urban Properties and Agricultural lands
shall be in Form J and Form II, and in Form 1A for the area covered by
Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad.

8. Supply of Market Value Guidelines Registers to various Officers :-
(1) The Market Value Guidelines prepared as per Rules 6 and 7 shall be
made available to each Sub Registrar by the Conveners of the
Committees.

(2) The Sub-Registrar shall cause supply of copy of relevant portion thereof
to the following officers :—

(i) Mandal Revenue Officer ;
(ii) Mandal Development Officer ;
(iii) Gram Panchayat ;
(iv) Municipal Council ;
(3) One copy of the Guidelines shall be exhibited at a conspicuous place in
the office of the Sub Registrar and District Registrar for use of public.
9. Power of Special Revision :—
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in these Rules, the Commissioner
and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps may order for a special
revision of Market Value Guidelines in any specified area under the
following circumstances leading to sudden appreciation of land values,—
(a) Setting up of an Industry or group of industries or Infrastructural
projects.

(b) Development of large scale housing projects.

(c) Development of Ayacut under irrigation projects.

(d) Any other special circumstances having an impact on the values
of immovable property in any specified area.

(2) Incases covered by sub-rule (1) above, the Committees constituted under
Rule 4(2) shall take up the revision of Market Value Guidelines within
time frames stipulated by the Commissioner and Inspector General of
528 Market Value Scheme - Revision of M.V. Guidelines Rules 1998
Registration and Stamps.

(3) Such revised values shall be implemented on a date to be fixed by the
Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps.

10. Furnishing of Extracts of Market Values to Committee in certain
cases :— The Registering Officers shall furnish to the Convener of
Committee mentioned in Rules 4(2) and 13 and extract of the Market
Values in respect of the instruments presented for registration which
consideration or Market Value of the subject property which is more
than that specified in the market Value Guidelines, by the 30" day of the
following months.

11. Land Acquisition Officers to furnish copies of awards to the
committee in certain cases :— All the Land Acquisition Officers
appointed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 shall, whenever the
amount of compensation awarded by them or subsequently enhanced by
the courts, is higher than the Market Value Guidelines, send a copy of
such award or order of the court as the case may be, to the Conveners of
the Committees mentioned in Rules 4 and 13 within thirty days from the
date of payment of compensation.

12. Summons to the public, public officers and recording statements by
the Committees :— The Committee constituted under Rule 4(2) and
13 may, if they think fit to do so :

(a) _ record the statement of the person on whom , the notice has been
served and may for the purpose of inquiry :

(i) call for any information or record from any Public officer or Officer
or Authority under the State Government or any local authority.

(ii) record statement from any member of the public office or Authority
under state Government, or any local authority.

(b) call upon the parties to be present on the date specified in the
notice and on such other day as may be fixed by it.

13. The Authority competent for rectification of Anomalies :—

(1) _ ifany representation is received from parties aggrieved by the rates shown
in the Market Value Guidelines or if any Officer of the Department notices
anomaly, the issue shall be referred to the committee specified in sub-
rule 1(2) and such Committee shall send proposals to the Commissioner
and Inspector General for rectifying the anomaly by upward/downward
revision after duly following the procedure prescribed under the Rule.

(2) The following Committee shall be the authorities competent to rectify
any anomalies arising out of revision of Market Value Guidelines taken
up under these Rules.

market value and send a proposal to the Commissioner and Inspector
General for approval.

14. General Control and Supervision:— It shall be competent-for the
Commissioner and Inspector General to issue such administrative
instructions of general nature as may be required from time to time for
the effective implementation of these Rules.

CHAPTER -11
Stamps Sale Counter of Registration Offices

In this chapter : -

1. B.S.O denotes " Board Standing Orders " (A.P. Stamp Munual, 1978)

2. S.O. denotes " Standing Orders (Registration Manual - Part II)

3. A.P.S.M. denotes " Andhra Pradesh Stamp Manual, 1974 "

4 C & IGRS. denotes " Commissioner and Inspector General of
Registration and Stamps

5. Procgs. denotes " Proceedings "

1. STAMPS SALE COUNTERS OF REGISTRATION OFFICES
Preacuble :Prior to the introduction of the scheme of Sale of stamps through
Sub-Registry Offices, there was scope for the licensed private stamp vendors
to corner the supply and sale of stamps creating artificial scarcity. Instances of
sale of stamps at prices more than their face value by some stamp vendors were
also noticed, creating hardship to the purchasers of stamps. Though stamps
are sold by the Treasuries, it was a cumbersome procedure consuming more
time, causing great inconvenience to the purchasers.

In order to cater to the needs of the public more promptly and save them
from inconvenience and hardship, the system of selling stamps of all categories
- both judicial and Non judicial - across the counter was introduced first in
select Registration Offices and subsequently extended the system to many more
offices throughout the State. The system has been working satisfactorily. The
Chief Controlling Revenue Authority declared all Sub-Registrar Offices in the
State as "SUB DEPOTS" for sale of judicial and nonjudicial stamps.
Consequently "Stamps Sale Counter" has been established in almost all Sub-
Registrars Offices in the State.

A. Stamps Sale Counter

1) All the Sub-Registrars Offices are declared as SUB-DEPOTS for sale
of judical and nonjudical stamps of all descriptions (BSO 65=B)
Note:Sub-Depots-constitution of 178 SROS as Sub-Depots-GO Ms
No581Rev(Regn-1) dt. 7-5-2003 (IG’s no. GS03/15/2005/11.dt 1-2-
2005)

2) The Officer in-charge of the Sub Depot. Viz. Sub-Registrar who are
apppointed under Registration Act, 1908 to sell stamps is called " EX-
OFFICIO STAMP VENDOR " (BSOs 60A & 60B)
Stamps Sale Counter of Registration Offices 545

Officers at the time of inspection of this item in their offices.

20-12-1984. The following are the said instructions:

B. Indents

Indents for supply of stamps from the Treasury/Sub-Treasury should be
checked by the Sub-Registrar (Ex-Officio Stamp Vendor) personally,
keeping in view the needs of the Depot. The indents should be
consecutively numbered for each calendar year. They shall be presented
to the District Treasury Officer / Sub-Treasury Officer in duplicate. The
District Treasury Officer / Sub-Treasury Officer shall return the duplicate
copy to the Sub-Registrar with particulars of the categories,
denominations and value of the stamps supplied under his dated signature.
The Sub-Registrar shall file those copies serially in a file book and
simultaneously copy them in ' Indent Register ' which should be
maintained in the form prescribed in Annexure-I. All corrections in
this Register shall be attested by the Sub-Registrar.

Immediately on receipt of the stock of stamps from the Treasury / Sub-
Treasury and before filing the indent as prescribed above the Sub-
Registrar shall verify it with the entries made in the indent by the District
Treasury Officer / Sub-Treasury Officer and satisfy himself that there is
no discrepancy between the two. Any discrepancy in this respect shall
be brought to the notice of the District Treasury Officer / Sub-Treasury

Officer at once. The shroff or the person obtaining the delivery of the
stock from the Sub-Treasury Office shall be held personally responsible
for any shortage in stock detected by the Sub-Registrar on its receipt
from Sub-Treasury.

All correspondence with the Sub-Treasury Office as regards such
discrepancies and variations shall be preserved in a separate file.

C. Ledgers

Soon after the verification of the stock with the Indents, it shall be entered
in the Ledger in red ink under various categories and denominations and
the balance struck in red ink. The entries and value shall be ckecked and
attested with the dated initials of the Sub-Registrar.

The Ledger shall be maintained in the form prescribed in Annexure IT

D. Sales

At the commencement of each working day, the Sub-Registrar shall
handover to the clerk stamps of different categories and denominations
under proper acknowledgment in a Register called "Stamps Issue
Register". In case of need, stamps may be issued more than once ina
day following the said procedure.

At the close of the day, the balance of stock and the sale proceeds shall
be returned by the clerk to the Sub-Registrar who shall acknowledge
their receipts in the said Register.

The " Stamps issue Register " shall be maintained in the form prescribed
in Annexure III

The name and addition of the purchaser and the name and addition of
the person for whom the stamps are purchased shall invariably be written
on the stamps and in the sales Register. The clerk / shroff shall endorse
the fact of receipt of money on the indent over his signature.

The Sub-Registrar shall verify the indent of the party with endorsements
made on the stamps and satisfy regarding the receipt of the money before
affixing his signature on the stamps. Under no circumstances he shall
sign on blank stamp papers.

Acknowledgement in token of receipt of the stamps by the parties shall
be obtained on the indents.

Indents received from the parties shall be serially numbered for each
day. They shall be tagged separately under each category and shall be
preserved month-wise and the indents relating to each calendar year
shall be bundled up separately.
Stamps Sale Counter of Registration Offices 547

E. Sales Registers

(a) The Sales Registers of different categories shall be closed at the end of
each day, the abstract of various denominations and values of stamps
sold shall be prepared and deductions made in the ledger. The total
number and value of stamps sold as noted in the Sales Register shall be
verified with the grand total for the day noted in the ledger. The Sub-
Registrar shall attest the abstract and the entry in the ledger in token of
such verification every day.

(b) The stamps issued shall be numbered consecutively for each calender
year separately under each category, viz, Judicial and Non-Judicial etc.,

F. Remittances

(a) The sale proceeds of each day shall be remitted on the next working
day.

(b) The Challans shall be numbered consecutively for each calendar
year.

(c) A separate ' Remittance Register ' shall be maintained in which
the sale proceeds under different categories for each day shall be
entered and the total struck. The number and date of the challan
through which the remittance is made shall be noted and
acknowledgement of the person entrusted with the remittance with
amount in words and figures shall be obtained in it. The total shall
tally with the amount noted in the Account under the relevant
column.

(d) The Sub-Registrar shall verify the challan after remittance, affix
his dated initials, and file it.

G. Reports and Returns

(a) The monthly plus and minus statement (i.e opening balance plus
stock received during the month minus sales and the closing
balance) and (2) the statement of balance of stamps under each
category shall be prepared at the end of each account month, only
after physical verification by the Sub-Registrar who shall check
up the total values of balances noted in the two statements with
the concerned ledgers before sending them to the Sub-Treasury
Officer for reconciliation. He shall add a certificate in the ledger
relating to each category in the form prescribed in Annexure IV.
The Sub-Registrar shall obtain the certificate of verification by
the Sub-Treasury Officer on the duplicate copy and submit a copy
thereof along with a copy of the certificate prescribed in Annexure

H. Transfer of Charge

On each occasion of transfer of charge the Relieving Officer shall
verify the entire stock of stamps and both the Relieved and
Relieving Officers shall record the result of such verification on
the Certificate of Transfer of Charge.

The ledgers shall be signed by both the Relieved and Relieving
Officers after striking the balances as on the date of transfer of
charge

I. Inspection and Audit

At the time of Annual Inspection, the District Registrar shall
physically verify the balances and values noted in the ledger with
the actual stock on hand. He shall also check the sales and other
registers to satisfy himself that they are being maintained properly.
He shall sign with date in the ledger in token of verification and
record the fact in the Inspection Report.

They shall conduct detailed audit of all stamps in sub-depots under
their jurisdiction at the time of annual inspection of S.R.Os. They
may also audit the sub-depots as and when feel it necessary to
check irregularities if any.

They shall invariably submit to the Inspector General separate audit
report in the proforma given below within 3 days from the date
of inspection.

They shall obtain the monthly returns promptly from the stamps
sub-depots and scrutinise them minutely every month and take
prompt necessary action at their level if any irregularity is noticed.

S.O 790 (i) The Sub-Registrar shall prepare the indent, obtain the required
stamps and preserve the. stock.

Gi) | He shall place an indent to replenish the stocks whenever necessary.
All denominations of stamps, to cater to the needs of the public shall be
maintained.

ii) He shall maintain

(a) Stock Registers of each category of stamps, i.e Nonjudicial, judicial, Court
fee and copy stamps. As soon as the stock is received it should be
entered in the ledgers in red ink as a receipt and attested by Sub-Registrar
with dated initials.

(b) Separate Sales Registers in the proforma given below should be
maintained for each category of stamps. At the end of each day, the
number and the value of denomination of stamps sold should be accounted
for in the relevant register i.e stock register as "Sales" and the "balance"
should be struck and attested by the Sub-Registrar with dated initials.

(c) Acash book should be maintained in the proforma given hereunder. The
cash book should be signed by the Sub-Registrar with the date at the end
of each day.

(d) _ The Sales to the public should be niade upto 4-00 P.M. normally, though
can be continued when the work is less, with usual lunch break. A
notice may be displayed prominently about the sale of stamps to the
public indicating the timings of sale.

(e) i) The indent form to be obtained from the public is also given in the
Annexure (Form No.4 infra)

ii) The indents for stamps presented with cash should be received from the
public by the Assistant or Shroff. After receipt of indent together with
cash, he should check the accuracy of value of stamps required and
thereafter enter the amount in cash register. The Stamps should then be
taken out and necessary entries made in the Sales Register and on the
stamp papers. Thereafter these stamps so endorsed are to be passed on
to the Sub-Registrar who is an Ex-Officio Stamp Vendor for his
verification and signature on the Stamps. Then the stamp papers should
be delivered to the parties after obtaining acknowledgements on the
indents.

(f) | The sale proceeds of the stamps should be remitted through Shroff on
the next working day. The amount shall be remitted to the heads of
account given in the proforma prescribed for “Cash Register” (Vide

RELEVANT EXTRACT FROM THE RULES for SUPPLY and
DISTRIBUTION of STAMPS & the BOARD STANDING ORDERS
(As Applicable to the State of Andhra Pradesh)

A. RULES FOR THE SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION OF STAMPS

Extent of Application:- These rules apply to all classes of stamps.

Explanations:- For the purposes of these rules —

(1) | The term “Postage stamps” except where expressly otherwise provided
will include “Postal and telegraph stationery”.

(2) The expressions “Stamps” and “non-postal stamps” except where
expressly otherwise indicated will include match excise banderols and
tobacco excise duty labels.

XX XX XX XX XX XX
PART I - DISTRIBUTION, CUSTODY AND SALE
A. Local depots and Branch depots and stocks to be kept.

XX XX XX XX, XX XX.

13. Every treasury including those attached to political and salt agencies
shall be a local depot for the custody and sale of stamps of all descriptions.
The State Government may establish local depots at places where there
is no treasury:
Provided that match excise banderols and tobacco excise duty labels
shall be stocked at the local and branch depots selected by the State
Government for the purpose.
Stamp Vendors Rules 561

14.

15.

16.

Each local depot shall maintain a reserve stock of stamps equal to the
probable consumption of three months in the case of postage stamps
and other stamps which are the property of the Central Government
tobacco excise duty labels and match excise banderols and four months
in the case of non-postal stamps, in addition to the stock required for the
quarterly, four monthly or annual consumption as the case may be. The
State Government may direct that the supply to be maintained either
generally or in respect of any particular kind of stamp or in certain
local depots shall be equal to the probable consumption of such other
period as they deem expedient.

If the supply of stamps in any local depot should run short before the
receipt of the supply from the Central Stamp store the officer in charge
of the local depot should indent for a supply from a neighbouring depot,
sending copy of the indent to the Controller of Stamps, Nasik Road, or
to the Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, A.P. or to the officer
appointed under Rule 13 (ii), the G.S.O. Hyderabad shall be local depot
for the custody and sale of stamps of all descriptions for the cities of
Hyderabad and Secunderabad.

XX XX, XX XX XX XX XX XX,

Urgent indents on neighburing depots as authorized in Rule 15 may
ordinarily be made on a depot in the same State or administration. If the
depot-is in another State or administration the general or special orders
both of the State Government or Local Administration controlling the
supplying depot and of the State Government or Local Administration
controlling the indenting depot will be necessary.

Subject to the proviso to Rule 13 every subordinate treasury shall be a
branch depot for the sale of stamps of all descriptions. But in any case
where the sale of stamps from such a branch depot is insignificant and
equal facilities exist for the supply of stamps from a depot in the same
station as the branch depot, the State Government may direct the closing
of the branch depot; provided that without the previous sanction of the
Union Government, the State Government may not order that the
maintenance of stock of postage or Central excise revenue stamps in a
sub-treasury may be dispensed with even if the post office authorities
do not require it. In their order, Mis.No.1671 Revenue, dated 29" August,
1927, Mis.No.2692, Revenue dated 15" November, 1928 and Mis.No.532
Revenue dated 21" March, 1930 Government have relieved all the sub-
treasuries in the State from the duty of maintaining stocks of postage
stamps.
562

Stamp Vendors Rules

18.

Note

The supply to be kept in a branch depot should be not less than the
probable demand for three months in respect of postage stamps and other
stamps which are the property of the Central Government tobacco excise
duty labels and match excise banderols and four months in respect of
non postal stamps; but the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority
appointed by competent authority for the purposes of the India Stamps
Act, 1899, may direct that the supply shall be equal to the demand of
any other period, instead of three months in respect of postage stamps
and other stamps which are the property of the Central Government
tobacco excise duty labels and match excise banderols and four months
in respect of non-postal stamps which it may consider expedient. The
stock should be kept upto this amount by indenting and obtaining supplies
from the local depot from tiie to time as may be necessary.

:-In A.P. State, it has been prescribed that the supply to be kept in a
branch depot shall be equal to the probable demand for one moth together
with a reserve stock sufficient for a month. At the end of each month,
the officer incharge of a branch depot shall submit an indent for such
number as may be necessary to maintain the supply and reserve stock
specified above. The Board of Revenue may however direct that the
supply to be kept in any branch depot or depots shall be equal to the
probable demand of three months in the case of postage stamps and the
probable demand of three months in the case of postage stamps and the
prpobable demand for four months in the case of non-postal stamps. In
such cases, an equal quantity shall be kept as reserve stock and the officer
in charge of the branch depot shall submit an indent at the end of three
months in respect of postage stamps and at the end of four months in
respect of non-postal stamps for such number as may be necessary to
maintain the prescribed supply and reserve stock.

As soon as the number of stamps in the branch depot not receiving its
supplies direct from the Central Stamp store falls below the number
issued from the depot in the preceding four months, the officer in charge
of the depot shall prepare an indent for a supply equal to the probable
consumption of two months. The indent shall show, in separate columns
for all denominations of stamps, whether a supply is required or not the
balance in the branch depot, the quantity sold in the preceding four months
and the quantity indented for which should be approximately one-half
of the quantity sold in the preceding four months. The periods of “four
months and “Two months” in this rule may be altered by the Chief
Controlling Revenue Authority appointed by competent authority for
the purposes of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 to such other periods as it
may deem expedient. (vide note under Rule 18)

the consumption of three months in the case of postage stamps and other
stamps which are the property of the Central Government tobacco excise
duty labels and match excise banderols and four months in the case of
non-postal stamps in addition to the quarterly or four monthly or annual
demand,

B. Accounts, Returns, Storage etc.

As soon as possible, after the arrival of supply of stamps from the Central
Stamps Store or from another local depot, the Officer incharge of the
depot shall personally examine the outward appearance of the boxes or
pockets and satisfy himself that they bear no marks of tampering. He
shall then have the boxes or pockets opened in his presence and the
contents of each box or pocket counted either by himself or in his presence
immediately on being opened in accordance with Rule 22 (relates to the
functions of the Treasury Officer). Where the treasury is local depot the
boxes or pockets should invariably be placed immediately on arrival in
strong room of the Treasury, then opened one at a time in the presence
of Treasury Officer who must be watching all the time the boxes or
pockets are being opened and their contents examined and counted. In
no case must be a second box or pocket be opened until the contents of
the first have been completely examined and verified and placed in the
proper receptacle as required by Rule 26. The number and value of
stamps received shall be compared by the officer incharge with the invoice
submitted and a receipt shall be sent to the officer who sent the stamps
as soon as may be convenient and in no case later than fifteen days after
the arrival of the stamps.

XX XX XX XX XX XX XX XX.

If any of the stamps received are found unfit for issue due to faulty
manufacture, they should be returned at once to the Controller of Stamps,
Naisk Road. The press will not be liable to replace free of charges
stamps found unfit for issue from cause other than faulty manufacture.
Stamps that are’ through any cause rendered unfit for issue at any time
after receipt shall be disposed of in accordance with Rules 48, 49 and 54
(b) and the rules framed by the State Government under Rule 49.
Immediately after the stamps received have been counted they shall be
placed in proper receptacles in the store under double lock in the presence
of the Officer incharge, arranged in parcels and packets containing known
quantities the amount and value of each denomination being entered at
the same time in a register maintained to show the receipts and issues to
564 Stamp Vendors Rules

and from the store under double lock. These entries shall be checked by
the officer in charge at the time when the stamps are deposited, and the
correctness of the arithmetical calculations of additions to balance, as
well as of the values compared with quantities, shall be verified and
initialed by him at the time. The register shall then be placed with the
stamps in the double lock receptacles shall not be removed therefrom,
nor shall any entries be allowed to be made therein except in the presence.
of the officer in charge.

Note:- In all cases where stamps registers have to be checked, the actual
check of quantities against values is a very important one; the correctness
of the calculations of value must be tested in detail either by actual
multiplication or by use of correctly prepared tables, and this check should
never be omitted. These remarks apply also to such of the following
rules as prescribed a check of this kind. It is not necessary, that the
complete checking should be done by the officer himself. It will be
sufficient if the officer personally checks 10 per cent of the entries in
each class of stamps leaving the remaining entires in each calss to be
checked by a sub-ordinate under his supervision

C. Sales

27. The treasurer or such other officers of Government as the Board of
Revenue or the Government may appoint shall be ex-officio vendors of
all descriptions of stamps in each local depot. Except as provided in
Rule 33, sales to Government departments, the public or to licensed
vendors shall not be made direct from the store under double lock, such
sales being made by the ex-officio vendor from the supply entrusted to
him forthis purpose, to be kept by him under single lock, as prescribed
in the following rules.

28. The stock of stamps to be left with the treasurer to be kept by him under
single lock shall be limited to a week’s supply unless the value of the
stamps, stock notes together with cash left with him is below the security
taken when the value of the stamps in his possession may be increased
by the difference. He will maintain a register (which will be in the English
language) of receipts into and issues from single lock in the same form
as the double lock register, and on a fixed date near the beginning of
each month he will prepare an indent for the quantity required for the
month in a form showing the balance in his hands an average month’s
consumption and the quantity required. When this indent is presented to
the officer in change he will examine the single lock register and check
the correctness of the arithmetical calculations made therein. If he
approves the indent, he shall then give out the quantity required from the
Stamp Vendors Rules 565

30.

store under double lock, check the correctness of the entries made in the
single lock register, initial both registers correspond with those made in
the single lock register, initial both registers and return the double lock
register into the double lock store. The same procedure should ordinarily
be followed when stamps are issued from double lock at any intermediate
date, but when it is necessary to make issues more than once in one day,
the prescribed checks need be applied at each time of issues only to the
particular descriptions of stamps given out from double lock. There shall
be a fortnightly verification of the balance of stamps in the hands of the
ex-officio vendor unless the State Government desires that such
verification should be more frequent, e.g., on every day on which stamps
are issued to the stamp vendor from the double locks.

XX XX XX XX XX XX XX XX

The following rules have been framed by the State Government regarding

sales of stamps by ex-officio vendors.

(1) Ex-officio vendors shall sell only such stamps as they may be
directed to sell by the Board of Revenue or Government.

(2) Every ex-officio vendor selling stamps to any person who is nota
licensed vendor shall write on the face of every stamp paper which
he sells, just below the stamps impression, a serial number as
determined by the orders of the Board of Revenue or Government
the date of sale, the name and residence of purchaser, and if the
stamp is purchased for the use of any person other than the person
who tenders the money for it, the name and residence of such other
person also together with his father’s name (vide G.O.Ms.No.362,
Revenue (U), dated 9.4.1974 A.P. Gazette, dated 23.5.1974) and
value of the stamp in full, in words and his own ordinary signature:
at the same time, he shall make corresponding entries in a register
to be kept by him in such form as the Board of Revenue or
Government may prescribe. Any such vendor who shall knowingly
make a false endorsement on the stamp sold or a false entry in his
register renders himself liable prosecution under the Indian Penal
Code:

Provided that in the case of Copy of stamp papers and Hundies,
the endorsement shall be made on the back.

(3) Every ex-officio vendor shall without delay deliver any stamp
which he has in his possession for sale on demand by any person
tendering the value in any currency which would be accepted on
behalf of the Government by the Collector of the District.
566

Stamp Vendors Rules
(4) No ex-officio vendor shall sell any stamps, the use of which has
been ordered by competent authority to be discontinued.

(5) Every ex-officio vendor shall keep and render such accounts as
may be prescribed by the Board of Revenue or Government and
shall allow the Collector of the District or any officer duly
authorised by such Collector, by the Board of Revenue or by the
Government at any time to inspect such accounts and the register
which he is required to keep under Rule 2 and to examine the
stock of stamps in his possession.

(6) Every ex-officio vendor shall, at any time, on the demand of the
Collector or other officer duly authorised by the Board of Revenue
or Government deliver up all stamps remaining in his possession.

(7) When application for an impressed sheet of a particular value is
made to a Treasury officer, he shall if possible, issue a single sheet
of the particular value. If a single sheet is not available, he shall
issue the fewest possible sheets that will amount to the required
value.

(8) When, however the value of the stamp paper applied for is higher
than the highest value of stamp which the vendor is authorised to
sell, such vendor shall not attempt to supply such stamp by the
sale of number of the stamped sheets he is authorized to sell.

The following rules have been prescribed by the State Government in
consultation with the Auditor-General for the disposal of non-postal
stamps which are property of the State Government and which are

(1) Stamps found unfit for issue whether at the time of their receipt or
subsequently owing to faulty manufacture shall, as soon as their
unfitness is discovered, be sent to the Controller of Stamps, Nasik
Road, for replacement free of cost.

(2) All stamps found unfit for issue at the time of their receipt owing
to causes other than faulty manufacture, such as stamps sticking
together or becoming damaged in transit or found damaged in stock
at any time after receipt or accidentally damaged or spoilt while in
the custody of postal officials shall be destroyed by or under the
orders of the Collector as provided in Rule (5) or by the Inspector
General of Stamps and their value written off the accounts up to
the value of Rs.300. The Inspector General of Stamps may
authorise the Assistant Inspector General of Stamps to destroy the
stamps in his office. If the value of stamps to be destroyed exceeds
Rs.300 the sanction of Board shall be obtained for their destruction
and for the write-off of their value, Collectors of districts are
Stamp Vendors Rules 571

autorised to sanction the exchange of fresh adhesive revenue
stamps of the same value for these accidentally damaged or spoilt
while in the custody of postal officials.

Losses of Stamps During Transit or from stocks in the Central Stamps

The terms of supply form the Central Stamps store are f.o.r. Nasik Road
and once the stamps are dispatched from the store they become the
property of the department or Government which would be entitled for
their proceeds on sale. When shortages occur in the consignments of
stamps dispatched from the Central Stamps Store, whether occasioned
by theft, accident or other causes, the resultant loss represented by the
manufacturing value of the missing stamps etc., as well as the potential
loss shall fall on the department or government owining the stamps unless
serious negligence is established against the dispatching or receiving
agency.

C. Relevant Extract of Standing Orders from Registration Manual -
Part II

Sale of Stamps
General

S.0.780. Instrument covered by the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, unless
otherwise exempted, are to be executed on stamp papers which are Non-Judicial
and suits and cases filed in Courts require to be levied with judicial stamps.
Both judicial and non-judicial (Non-Postal Stamps) of different categories and
denominations are sold through two agencies (1) Official and (2) Private. All
varieties of Stamps irrespective of value and denomination are sold officially
through District Treasuries and certain Sub-Registry Offices, which are declared
as Local Depots and Sub-Depots. In so far as Hyderabad City is concerned,
the General Stamp Office of the Inspector General of Registration and Stamps,
shall also be a Local Depot. Since stamps are required by the registering and
litigant public and commercial concerns at different places, both Urban and
Rural, some private individuals are also licenced to vend these stamps on
commission. Their appointment is governed by the conditions laid down in
their licences. The District Registrars are the appointing authorities for private
stamps vendors in their jurisdiction. The sale of stamps through official and
private media is regulated by the Board Standing Orders printed in the Andhra
Pradesh Stamp Manual. The public should not be allowed-to suffer for want
of Stamps of any kind and denomination. As scarcity of stamps may result in
undesirable repercussions, all the local and Sub-depots and private stamps
vendors shall preserve adequate stocks keeping in view the public demand.
The Sub-Registrars and District Registrars may apprise the Sub-Treasuries
and District Treasuries in case they are aware of shortage of stamps

c) While granting licences, the Licensing Authority can specify any
special conditions warranted such as sale of only judicial stamps,
sale of particular denominations etc.

d) — Itis not mandatory to issue a Licence to old and lapsed Licensees.
The applications from them can be treated as fresh and can be
disposed of along with other applications for the same area.

e) The posts of Stamp Vendors located within 3 kilo meters of a Stamp
Counter (Sub Depot) may not be filled if a vacancy arises on
account of resignation or demise etc.

Note: Private Stamp Vendors should not use office premises

f) _ Itis desirable to discourage the monopoly of sale of Stamps in the
same family. Renewal in respect of Stamp Vendor who is a relative
of a Document Writer should not be considered. The word

"Family" should be used in a wider sense and not in a Jegal sense,
Registration Rule 201 (hh) of Rules relating to Document Writers
may be followed in this context.

The Registrar shall ensure that Stamp Vendors are evenly
distributed in the district and also in the towns and that there is no
concentration of Stamp Vendors in a particular place leading to
unhealthy competition in some places and dearth of stamps in other
places.

The Registrar shall critically review the work of Stamp Vendors
with reference to indents made, when he visits Sub-Registrar
Offices for annual inspection or otherwise. He may avail the
opportunity to contact the Sub-Treasury Officer to find out whether
all the Stamp Vendors are evincing interest in making the stamps
readily to the public by indenting stamps promptly and preserving
the adequate stocks. He may also write to the Sub-Treasury Officers
to satisfy whether the stamp vendors are earnest in their business
by indenting regularly for the stamps of all denominations which °
are normally required by the public. If the stamp vendors are
inactive and fail to maintain the required stocks of different
categories of stamps for which they are licenced, their holding
licences does not serve any public good. By issuing suitable
notices, the Registrar may take steps to substitute them.

If the Stamp Vendors proceed on long leave it is evident that they
are not evincing keen interest in their profession. If the absence of
a Stamp Vendor is more than 6 months, the Registrar amy appoint
anew Stamp Vendor in his place instead of nominee of the Stamp
Vendor.

The Registrar shall maintain Registers for issue, renewal of
Licences and for punishments awarded to Stamp Vendors

If the Registrar is satisfied as to the reasons explained by an
applicant, a duplicate licence can be granted without any fees.

D. Action Against Stamp Vendors

S.0.785: (i). The private Stamp Vendors shall strictly adhrere to the
stipulations of Licences and the Standing Orders governing their appointment
and Sale of Stamps. They shall not resort to sale by antedate, alteration in
endorsements, sale at higher rate than face value etc., which may be reviewed
by appointing authorities as serious violations requiring exemplary
punishment. The Registrar shall take appropriate, including criminal, action
against the sale by unauthorised persons and touts. Care shall also be taken
against sale by one Licenced Vendor for another.

(ii) | Greater check shall be exercised against the practice of family members
of Stamp Vendor making Stamp endorsements in his absence or family
members selling stamps over which the stamp vendor has already made
endorsements.

(iii) The action taken by the District Registrars against Stamp Vendors for
grave violations should be commensurate with gravity. The action
contemplated should have statuary effect on the erring Vendors. The
appointing authority should realise that soft pedaling and pusillaneous
attitude towards the guilty will not produce the desired results of ensuring
discipline among the Stamp Vendors and act as deterrant against other
Stamp Vendors who are prone to such _ tendencies.

(iv) Whenever a prima facie contravention of any Rule or order or conditions
of licence by any Stamp Vendor is noticed, the Registrar has to give an
opportunity to the concerned to explain for the irregularities. Principles
of natural justice will have to be observed and a show-cause notice has
to be issued specifying the allegation in detail before action is taken.
The particular Rule for the distribution and supply of stamps of the Board
Standing Order which he contravened should be quoted. The allegation
is to be supported by the recorded evidence and it must also be mentioned.
In the case of oral evidence the name of witnesses under each item of
allegation shall be noted. Final orders may be passed after receipt of
explanation from the Stamp Vendor fully discussing the evidence adduced
and explanation offered in respect of each and every allegation holding
or otherwise the charge as proved. The punishment imposed shall be
specified in the order.

(v) Cancellation / suspension of Licence can be ordered for any breach of
Rules. Standing Orders including violation of stipulations contained in
the Engagement Bond based on the gravity of offence. Forfeiture of the
whole or part of the security mentioned in the engagement Bond by the
Licencing Authority can be imposed for less grave violations.
592 Stamp Vendors -Standing Orders of R&S Department

 

E. Miscellaneous

S.0.786. The Stamp Vendor should not prepare Annexure 1-A under
Section 47-A of Indian Stamp Act, 1899, 37-G of Income Tax Act, Patta
Transfer Application, 'M' Notices, Plans etc., accompanying a document.

§.0.787.. Though Board Standing Orders of Andhra Pradesh Stamp
Manual contemplate sanction of temporary licence regarding the disposal of
stock of a stamp vendor whose licence lapséd or who died leaving stock or
otherwise, yet it should be discouraged. The Stamp Vendor or representative
of the deceased Stamp Vendor may be advised to apply for refund of excess
stock.

S.0.788. (i) The Sub-Registrar shall append a certificate regarding the
number of pages in the Sales and Stock Register of the Stamp Vendors in their
respective jurisdictions.

(ii) They shall collect records of the Stamp Vendors at the end of each
calendar year and scrutinise them. Any grave irregularities noticed by
them shall be submitted to District Registrar concerned for initiating
suitable action.

(iii) The Sub-Registrar may sanction leave for one month and below to the
Stamp Vendors. Leave for more.than a month should be sanctioned by
the District Registrars (Appointing Authorities)

(iv) There is no objection to grant a certified copy of Stamp Vendor Licence
(which is public document) to a third party who produces a Court's
Certificate to the effect that a copy of it is required to be produced in a
Court or file some other documentary evidence to show to the satisfaction
of the authority empowered to grant such copy that he requires a copy
bonafide for his own use (Board's Spl. 03/3461/75, dated 28.8.1975)

F, Records - Preservation

Preservation period of Stamp Vendors records is as under
(G.O.Ms.No.1440 Rev (U) dept. dated 29.8.1978 = Disposal of S.Vs.
Record Rule, 1977)

Stamp Vendors Indent Register 13 years
Stock Register of Stamps 13 years
Daily Sales Register 12 years

Prior Approval of the Licensing Authority for destruction shall be
obtained.
Mode of destruction shall be as follows
S.V. Indent Register By tearing into pieces
Stock Registers of stamps By tearing into pieces
Daily Sales Register of Stamps By burning
Note of destruction of records shall be made in Red ink in the Register
of Records against the entries of the records destroyed. The note shall
refer to the file number and the date of sanction order of the Licensing
Authority together with mode and the actual date of destruction of the
records (A.P.Gazette Part I Page 420,dt. 28.9.1978 = I.G's endt.No.R.C1/
28640/70, dated 19.12.1979)

H. Engagement Bond by Stamp Vendors

The engagement Bonds for Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousands only)
required to be furnished by Stamp Vendors before sanction of licence shall be
in the proforma prescribed in B.S.O 77(2)(1) of the Stamp Manual 1974. Supra
such Bonds should be signed by two witnesses. It is to be charged with a
stamp duty of Rs.300/-at 3% on the value of Rs.10,000/- under Article 13 of
Schedule 1A.

Note : An ‘undertaking’ (agreement) on N.J. Stamps of Rs.10/- has also
to be obtained before grant of Licence to stamp Venders BSO 77 (2) Supra)

I. Court Fees - A.P.Advocates Welfare Fund Stamps

1) The Ex-Officio Stamp Vendors (Sub-Registrars) should affix the date
and their signature on the Court fees A.P. Advocates Welfare Fund Stamps
sole by them. (BSO 77(2) = IG RS Memo No. GS 02/25014/93-1, dated
30.8.1993.

2) Restriction on sale of number of sheets of N.J.Stamps :
All the Stamp Vendors are instructed not to issue more than 10 (ten) sheets
of Non-Judicial Stamps either to any individual or to an institution in a day to

avoid scarcity of Stamps (C & IGRS Momo No.G S03/19039/2004, dated
5.102005)
